The specification assumes both configurations are solvable, assumes TLC is running in single-worker BFS mode so counterexamples are shortest, and uses the final interleaved specification to obtain shortest step counts s1 and s2 for the two independent instances.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of solving the classical water‑jug (Die Hard) puzzle for two different physical configurations of jugs running concurrently, and a means to compare how many primitive steps each configuration needs to reach a specified target volume. The model should treat each configuration as an independent instance of the same jug system (same allowed primitive actions: fill a jug, empty a jug, pour until source empty or destination full), with its own fixed set of jug capacities and its own current contents. The system must be able to run both instances together and produce executions in which instances advance independently so that the number of action steps performed by each instance can be counted.

The specification must guarantee:
- Only behaviors corresponding to legal jug actions for each configuration are allowed.
- Both configurations start empty and, when a configuration reaches the target volume in one of its jugs, that fact can be detected and recorded.
- The exploration semantics must permit interleavings of actions from the two configurations so that each configuration’s step count reflects only its own actions.
- The model must enable checking that both configurations can solve the target (i.e., there exist finite sequences of legal actions reaching the target) and produce a shortest-counterexample behavior in which both have reached the target, thereby exposing the minimal number of steps taken by each configuration.
- Preserve independence: the two instances share no mutable state except for bookkeeping counters used only to measure steps.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a thin Apalache-oriented wrapper around a separate helper module named RingBuffer. It introduces typed constants and a single variable ringbuffer, then instantiates RingBuffer so that the helper module can be typechecked in isolation. The comments explain that the underlying helper module defines Init and parameterized actions such as Write, EndWrite, BeginRead, and EndRead, but this wrapper itself does not define Next, temporal behavior, or fault handling, and leaves preservation of NoDataRaces to concrete protocol modules such as Disruptor_SPMC.
desc_intent:
Model a bounded ring buffer data structure accessed concurrently by multiple readers and multiple writers. The buffer has a fixed capacity of slots, each holding either a value or a distinguished NULL. Writers may reserve a slot, publish a value into a reserved slot to make it visible, and complete their write; readers may claim a slot that contains a value, consume that value, and complete their read. The model must support multiple writers and multiple readers operating concurrently on different slots, but must prevent data races on the same slot: at most one writer may be writing a given slot at a time, and a slot being written must not be read until the write is published. Likewise, a slot being read should not be concurrently reclaimed for writing until the read completes.

Specify the buffer’s externally visible API: initialization, an operation for a writer to begin and end a write to a specific slot, and an operation for a reader to begin and end a read from a specific slot. Capture state that records which slots hold which values and which threads currently hold read or write claims on each slot.

State the correctness properties the model must guarantee:
- Safety: no two writers may concurrently claim the same slot; no writer and reader may concurrently hold conflicting claims on the same slot that would allow a reader to observe a partially written value.
- Atomic visibility: once a writer has completed publishing a value, any subsequent reader that claims that slot must observe that full value (not NULL or a prior value).
- Liveness assumptions as appropriate: progress of readers/writers when slots are available (or state clearly which progress guarantees are required versus only safety).

Do not prescribe scheduling or low-level implementation details; leave scheduling nondeterministic so the model can be used to check that any interleaving of allowed operations preserves the properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a ring buffer abstraction with a fixed number of slots indexed modulo the buffer size. Each slot stores either a value from Values or the distinguished NULL value, and the module additionally tracks the sets of readers and writers currently accessing each slot in order to model multi-step reads and writes. The specification provides initialization, index computation, begin/end read and write actions, and invariants such as type correctness and absence of data races; comments explicitly state that client specifications using this module should include NoDataRaces as an invariant.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a fixed-size circular buffer (ring buffer) accessed concurrently by multiple producer and consumer threads. The model should describe the buffer as a bounded array of slots holding either a value or a special empty marker, and expose operations for producers to write a value into a slot and for consumers to read a value from a slot. It must account for the buffer index wrap-around semantics: sequence numbers map to slot indices modulo the buffer size.

Model the concurrency of multiple producers and multiple consumers so that each logical read or write access may be implemented as a sequence of substeps (e.g., begin, perform, end) and so the model can track which threads currently hold read or write access to each slot. The system must forbid data races: at most one writer may be active on a given slot at a time, and no slot may have active readers and active writers simultaneously. The model should include type and bounds constraints (buffer size positive, sets of readers/writers nonempty, values distinct from the empty marker).

State the correctness requirements as invariants: safety properties ensuring absence of data races and preservation of slot contents except when a valid write occurs; and basic type safety for buffer structure. Also specify an initial state where all slots are empty and no threads hold access.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides Apalache-specific type annotations and concrete helper values for a distributed replicated log specification. It models a system with a set of servers, a set of values, an integer lag constant, and a single state variable cLogs mapping each server to a sequence of values representing its current log. The module also instantiates another module named DistributedReplicatedLog, but this file itself only defines the typed variable tuple vars and two concrete set-valued helper operators for servers and values; it contains no actions, temporal specification, fairness, or proof content.
desc_intent: Specify a replicated log service running on a fixed set of servers that supports concurrent client appends and asynchronous, unreliable communication. The model should describe how each server maintains a locally ordered sequence of proposed values and how append operations and log propagation interact under eventual-delivery semantics with possible message loss, reordering, and network delays bounded by a parameter. The system must allow clients to append values to any server; appends are locally accepted and assigned an order at that server immediately. Servers periodically exchange their logs (or log segments) to propagate entries to others. The model should permit divergent local orders temporarily (availability under partitions) but must guarantee eventual convergence: if no new appends occur and the network becomes reliable, all non-faulty servers eventually have the same prefix of entries up to the last delivered append operations. Specify invariants ensuring that servers never lose locally accepted entries, that entries once appended persist at their origin, and that propagation only adds entries (no reordering or mutation of an existing entry). Express safety conditions disallowing contradictory values at the same logical position once that position is globally stabilized; express liveness conditions that under eventual synchrony and no new appends all servers converge to include every value that was appended to any non-faulty server. Include a tunable lag/delay parameter and model crash-stop failures of servers (they stop sending/receiving but keep their local logs).

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a state-based CRDT counter replicated across a finite set of nodes. Each node stores a vector-like map of counts for every node, local increments update only the originating node's own component, and gossip merges copy pointwise maxima from one node's view into another node's view. The spec assumes Node is finite, defines safety and monotonicity properties over the replicated counter state, and introduces a fairness/liveness package asserting weak fairness for gossip and that eventually only gossip steps occur; it also states a convergence property that all node views are repeatedly eventually equal.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a distributed, eventually-consistent grow-only counter replicated across a finite set of nodes. The system maintains at each node a local vector of nonnegative integers, one entry per node, that records how many increments that node has observed or performed. The model should capture two kinds of atomic events: a local increment at a node that increases that node’s own counter entry, and pairwise gossip between nodes where the receiving node merges the sender’s vector by taking the elementwise maximum. The model must enforce that all vectors are always maps from nodes to vectors of natural numbers and that local counters never decrease (monotonicity). 

Specify safety properties: no node’s recorded count for some origin can ever be less than that origin’s self-count at any node (local view respects origin’s self increments). Specify liveness and convergence properties: given fairness assumptions that gossip interactions occur sufficiently often (e.g., every gossip action is weakly fair and eventually only gossip actions occur while increments happen only finitely often), the system must converge: eventually all nodes’ vectors become equal (state convergence) and the common vector reflects the total number of increments performed by each node. Also require that increments are asynchronous and may interleave arbitrarily with gossip before the fairness period. The specification should leave the set of nodes parameterized and finite.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies an abstract distributed replicated log system in which each server maintains a local committed log and can either copy entries from a longer log or extend its own log. The model assumes a strong shared-state style fault-free view in which a server can directly inspect the logs of all other servers, rather than communicating through messages; comments note that this is unrealistic for real distributed systems and contrast it with protocols such as Raft. The specification enforces a machine-closed fairness condition requiring weak fairness for both copying and extending at every server, proves an invariant bounding the lag between server logs, proves that every server keeps extending forever, and also defines a stronger synchronization property that is intentionally not guaranteed.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a replicated append-only log service running on a finite set of servers. The system must allow each server to grow its local log by appending sequences of values and to copy progress from other servers so that logs converge within a bounded lag. Model time as an interleaving of atomic steps where any server may either append new entries to its own log subject to a bound that depends on current relative lengths, or copy some suffix (possibly partial) of another server’s log to advance itself. Do not assume synchronous message delivery; instead express only the abstract effect of a copy operation that reads another server’s current log state and appends a contiguous segment of missing entries. The model should enforce that every server’s log is a finite sequence of values, and that at all times the difference in lengths between any two logs is bounded by a fixed non‑negative integer parameter (the lag bound).

Specify safety properties: (1) each server’s log is always a finite sequence of values; (2) the absolute length difference between any pair of logs never exceeds the lag bound; and (3) copying only extends a log by appending entries already present on the source (no reordering or insertion in the middle). Specify liveness properties: (a) every server is eventually able to make progress and append strictly more entries infinitely often (subject to the lag bound), and (b) eventual pairwise convergence is permitted but not required — the model should allow but not mandate full equality of logs. Parameterize the model by the set of servers, the value domain, and the lag bound.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a generic operator MapThenFoldSet that, given a binary operator 'op', a base value, a mapping function 'f', a choice function 'choose', and a set S, applies 'f' to each element of S and then folds the results using 'op', starting from 'base'. The folding order is determined by the 'choose' function, which selects an element from a set; if 'choose' is not deterministic, the result may depend on the order unless 'op' is associative and commutative. The module comments explain the intended use and provide an example, and reference simpler versions of fold for sets, functions, and sequences in other modules. No temporal properties or state variables are present; this is a pure functional operator definition.
desc_intent: Model a deterministic fold-with-mapping computation over a finite set: given a finite input set, a pure mapping function applied to each element, a binary combining operator, and a specified identity/base element, the system should compute the result of combining the mapped values of all elements. The model should allow nondeterministic choices of the next element to process (to reflect arbitrary scheduling or order of traversal) and must ensure the final result does not depend on the order of processing whenever the combining operator is associative and commutative. The specification must capture termination (the fold completes after a finite number of steps when every input element has been processed) and preservation of the multiset of mapped values (each element is mapped exactly once). It should express correctness properties: (1) when the operator is associative and commutative, all possible execution orders produce the same final result; (2) when the operator is not associative or commutative, the model can exhibit order-dependent results; (3) idempotent or identity laws hold when appropriate (e.g., combining with the base yields the mapped value); and (4) the fold is total on finite input sets and produces the expected result for singleton and empty sets. Do not prescribe a specific traversal algorithm or scheduling policy — allow arbitrary choices and verify the required invariants and final-state equivalence properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a collection of operators for reasoning about functions in TLA+, including restriction, range, pointwise operations, inverses, and properties such as injectivity, surjectivity, and bijectivity. It provides operators to restrict a function to a subset of its domain or to values satisfying a predicate, to check if one function is a restriction of another, and to compute the range of a function. The module also defines operators for constructing sets of injections, surjections, and bijections between sets, and for checking their existence. Additionally, it includes fold operations over functions, leveraging a local instance of the Folds module. The specification is utility-focused and does not model a distributed algorithm or system, nor does it specify temporal properties or fault models.
desc_intent:
Model a library of pure mathematical functions and their relations that operates on total finite mappings between sets. The specification must describe abstract operators for: restricting a mapping to a subset of its domain or to domain elements or range values that satisfy a predicate; computing the image (range) of a mapping; testing whether one mapping is a restriction (submapping) of another; forming the pointwise combination of two mappings by a binary operator; constructing an inverse relation from values back to domain elements (including a partial inverse restricted to a target set); and computing the inverse of a bijection. Also specify predicates that characterize injective, surjective, and bijective mappings between two given sets, and define the sets of all injections, surjections, and bijections. Include existence tests that check whether at least one injection, surjection, or bijection exists between two sets.

Additionally, specify a fold operation that aggregates the values of a mapping by an associative, commutative binary operator (optionally restricted to a provided subset of indices), with an explicitly given base value and a deterministic result independent of iteration order.

State the domain and type constraints (finite domains, total functions from one set to another) and the required correctness properties: restriction operators preserve mapping values on kept domain elements; IsRestriction correctly characterizes submapping relation; Range yields exactly the set of images; pointwise combination is defined only when one domain is contained in the other and agrees elementwise; inverse maps each value to some original preimage when such exists; injectivity, surjectivity, bijectivity satisfy usual logical equivalences; the fold result is invariant under any permutation of indices (given operator properties).

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a replicated log in which nodes append transactions to a shared log and track, per node, how many log entries have been executed. The state consists of the sequence-valued log and a function executed mapping each node to a natural number, with actions for writing a new transaction and for executing pending transactions. The spec states type correctness and safety, and studies convergence under different fairness assumptions, including sufficient fairness conditions that imply all nodes eventually catch up to the log length and several fairness variants that are identified as insufficient or effectively false.
desc_intent:
Specify a replicated append-only log service for a fixed set of nodes and a fixed set of transaction identifiers. The system should allow any node to propose (append) a new transaction to the global log and should allow every node to execute transactions in log order. The model must ensure the log is a sequence of transactions that only grows by appending, and that each node maintains a local progress counter measuring how many prefix entries it has executed. Propose actions that append a transaction (allowed only when the proposer’s progress counter equals the current log length) and that allow a node to execute the next pending transaction (allowed only when its progress counter is less than the log length). The specification must state that the initial log is empty and every node’s progress counter starts at zero.

Require the following correctness properties: (1) Safety: no node may execute beyond the current log length (local progress never exceeds the log length); (2) Type invariants: the log is always a finite sequence of transactions and every progress counter is a natural number; and (3) Convergence (liveness): under appropriate fairness assumptions, every node’s progress counter eventually equals the log length (all nodes eventually catch up to all appended transactions). Describe what fairness assumptions are sufficient to guarantee convergence (for example, fairness for executing actions or for write actions, or both) and note which weak fairness assumptions are insufficient. Do not prescribe an implementation strategy beyond these behavioral requirements.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides Apalache-specific type annotations for a key-value store specification by declaring typed constants and variables and then instantiating the underlying KeyValueStore module. It does not define the algorithm itself in this file; instead, it supplies concrete constant sets and state variable declarations intended to match the imported specification's expected interface. The file contains no actions, temporal specification, fairness, assumptions, or proof content.
desc_intent:
Model a transactional in-memory key-value store that supports optimistic concurrency via per-transaction snapshots and deferred writes. The system must allow clients to begin transactions, read keys, write keys, and commit or abort transactions. Each transaction operates on a snapshot of the global store taken at transaction start; reads inside a transaction return the snapshot value for keys not yet written by that transaction, and its own written values for keys it has updated. Writes performed by a transaction are buffered locally until commit. A commit must succeed only if no write–write conflict exists with other committed transactions: that is, for every key a committing transaction has written, the current global value must still equal the value in that transaction’s snapshot for that key; otherwise the commit must fail and the transaction should abort. On successful commit, all buffered writes atomically update the global store. Aborts discard a transaction’s buffered writes and leave the global store unchanged.

Specify safety properties: snapshot consistency (a transaction never observes a value that contradicts its start snapshot except its own writes), atomicity of commit (either none or all of a transaction’s writes become visible), and serializability with respect to committed transactions (committed results are equivalent to some serial ordering of successful commits). Specify liveness assumptions optionally: progress for a transaction that encounters no conflicting concurrent commit should eventually be able to commit. Allow arbitrary finite sets of keys, values, and transaction identifiers.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies client-centric isolation levels for transactional databases, following definitions from Crooks et al. It models database states as total functions from keys to values, operations as read/write records, transactions as sequences of operations, and executions as sequences pairing each transaction with its parent state. The spec defines helper predicates for read states, completeness, write sets, conflicts, transaction effects, and all possible executions, and then formalizes commit tests for Serializability, Snapshot Isolation, Strict Serializability, Read Committed, and Read Uncommitted, along with simple type predicates and a debug helper.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a transactional storage system that defines executions of transactions over a key-value state and formalizes client-centric isolation levels. The model should treat a transaction as a sequence of read and write operations over keys, and an execution as a total order in which transactions are applied to produce a sequence of states starting from an initial state. The system should allow non-deterministic interleaving of transactions by considering all permutations of a given set of transactions and the resulting parent states for each transaction.

Require the model to define, for each operation, the set of possible states from which that operation may read (including writes performed earlier in the same transaction). Using that notion, specify for a given execution when each transaction has valid read states for all its operations, and when a single state is “complete” for a transaction (i.e., every operation of the transaction can read from that state). Also define a transaction’s write set and a notion of write-conflict between a transaction and a candidate read state.

Formulate commit tests that characterize standard isolation levels: Serializability, Snapshot Isolation, Strict Serializability (with an external timestamp order), Read Committed, and Read Uncommitted. For each level, require the existence of an execution (a permutation of the transactions from the given initial state) such that every transaction satisfies that level’s commit test. State these correctness properties as existential or universal requirements on executions, without prescribing how the system schedules or implements transactions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a simple key-value store that supports transactions with snapshot isolation. Each transaction takes a snapshot of the store, chooses nonempty read and write key sets, reads from its snapshot, applies its writes locally, and then commits only if its write set does not conflict with keys missed due to concurrent committed transactions. The specification includes a PlusCal algorithm translated to TLA+, a temporal specification with weak fairness for each transaction process, a termination property, type correctness conditions, and client-centric isolation checks for snapshot isolation and serializability through an instantiated module.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a concurrent key‑value database that supports client transactions using snapshot isolation. The model should describe transactions that (1) begin by taking an instantaneous read snapshot of the shared key‑value store, (2) perform a sequence of reads from that snapshot and local writes that update only the transaction’s local snapshot, and (3) attempt an atomic commit that applies the transaction’s writes to the global store only if doing so does not conflict with intervening writes that the transaction missed. The system must allow multiple transactions to be active concurrently, track which keys each active transaction has not observed (i.e., writes that became visible after its snapshot), and ensure that commits propagate written keys to other currently active transactions’ “missed” sets so those transactions can detect write–write and certain write–read conflicts.

Model the concurrency of transactions, nondeterministic choices of read‑sets and write‑sets, and the possibility that a transaction aborts (or fails to apply) if conflicts are detected on commit. Specify liveness so every transaction can progress through start, read, update, and commit steps and eventual termination (assuming no permanent conflict). State types and initial conditions: a global store initialized to a sentinel value for all keys, a finite set of transaction identifiers, and per-transaction local state for snapshot, read/write sets, and an operation log for verification.

Require these correctness properties:
- Snapshot Isolation: every transaction reads a consistent snapshot taken at its start; committed writes become visible atomically; no transaction sees partial effects of other transactions.
- No lost updates for non‑conflicting transactions: if two transactions write disjoint key sets, both commits may succeed and their effects are preserved.
- Safety of conflict detection: a commit that would overwrite keys missed by the transaction must be prevented from committing.
- Type invariants: store, transaction‑set, and per‑transaction structures conform to their declared domains.

Also provide an abstract operation log of reads and writes sufficient to assert higher‑level client‑centric properties such as serializability checks (expected to fail under write‑skew) and to validate snapshot isolation.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the temporal property Spec => [](TypeInvariant /\ TxLifecycle) of a key-value store system, as specified in KeyValueStore.tla. The proof demonstrates that the system maintains both type invariants and correct transaction lifecycles throughout its execution. The proof is structured hierarchically, showing that the invariants hold initially and are preserved by all possible transitions, including transaction operations and stuttering steps. The design leverages previously defined operators and actions from the KeyValueStore module, and uses TLAPS proof commands and structure to establish the result.
desc_intent: Specify a transactional key-value store that supports concurrent transactions, multi-key reads and writes, and atomic commit or rollback. The model should treat keys and values as abstract finite types and represent transactions as distinct identifiers. The system must allow opening a new transaction, performing adds, updates, and removes of keys within a transaction, and then either closing (committing) the transaction or rolling it back. Committing a closed transaction must make its written changes visible in the global store atomically; rolling back must discard all its tentative changes. Reads within a transaction must see that transaction’s own writes and either a consistent snapshot of the global store taken when the transaction opened or a well-defined isolation view; non-transactional reads must see the committed global state. The model must allow transactions to overlap in time and must ensure that one transaction’s tentative writes are not visible to other transactions until commit. Specify invariants expressing type correctness, that transactions maintain lifecycle constraints (opened → operations → closed/rolled back → no further ops), and that commits preserve atomicity (no interleaving partial commits) and durability of committed updates in the global store. State safety properties: absence of lost updates, no writes by closed/rolled-back transactions, and preservation of key domain. Also require a temporal property that the invariants hold invariantly (always).

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple key-value store with snapshot-isolated transactions. Each open transaction has its own snapshot of the store, a set of keys it has written, and a set of writes it has missed from other transactions; commits succeed only when there is no write-write conflict between the transaction's written keys and its missed keys. The spec defines transaction opening, add, update, remove, rollback, and close/commit steps, and proves that under the behavior specification the type invariant and transaction lifecycle cleanup properties always hold.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a key-value database that supports multi-operation transactions with snapshot isolation semantics. The model should describe clients opening transactions, reading and modifying a private snapshot, aborting, and committing. A transaction’s reads and writes operate on a snapshot taken when it begins; writes produced by a transaction are not visible to other transactions until the transaction successfully commits. Commits must be serialized by checking for write-write conflicts: a transaction may commit only if none of the keys it wrote were concurrently written (and committed) by another transaction in the interval between its snapshot and its commit. If two concurrent transactions write the same key, at most one may succeed; the other must be prevented from committing and may either abort or be retried. Transactions that write to disjoint key sets should be able to commit concurrently without interfering with one another.

Model the lifecycle of transactions (open, perform reads and writes on snapshot, commit, abort), the store state, per-transaction snapshots and per-transaction write-sets. Provide invariants ensuring type-correctness of state components and that closed/aborted transactions leave no leftover per-transaction state. Specify safety properties: snapshot isolation (reads see the snapshot taken at open), no lost updates for non-conflicting transactions, and write-conflict detection forbidding both concurrent writers of the same key to commit. Also state liveness goals informally: progress for non-conflicting transactions (they can commit) and the ability to abort or retry conflicting transactions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a minimal wrapper around external modules. It extends KeyValueStore and TLC, and defines one top-level operator, TxIdSymmetric, as Permutations(TxId). The module itself contains no variables, actions, temporal formulas, assumptions, proofs, or PlusCal constructs.
desc_intent: Model a replicated multi-version key-value store with transactions and a deterministic client-visible serialization that preserves causal and atomic write behavior. The system manages a set of keys, multiple versions per key, and a dynamic set of transactions that can read and write multiple keys. Transactions execute in three conceptual phases: acquire a snapshot, perform reads and writes against that snapshot, and commit their writes atomically. Replication presents versions to readers in a consistent manner: each read sees a version that respects real-time and causality (no read observes a write that causally depends on a commit not yet visible), and committed writes become visible together at a single logical commit point. The model must allow concurrent, possibly conflicting transactions and provide a mechanism for ordering or resolving conflicts so that the observed behavior is equivalent to some serial execution that respects each transaction’s snapshot and program order. Specify safety properties: atomicity of commits (all-or-nothing visibility), snapshot isolation (read operations return values from a single, consistent snapshot), and serializability or linearizability with respect to transaction commits. Also specify liveness assumptions minimal enough to avoid trivial deadlock: nonfaulty clients eventually make progress when not contending indefinitely. Include invariants capturing version monotonicity and uniqueness of commit identifiers.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines general-purpose utility operators for TLA+ specifications rather than a complete transition-system model with variables and a behavioral Spec. It provides helpers for set intersection testing, maximum and minimum selection from a set, reduction over sets and sequences, sequence indexing and manipulation, conversion from sequences to sets, an intersection operator over a set of sets, permutation generation for finite sets, and a small testing helper that prints a diagnostic when two values differ. The module has no state variables, no actions, and no temporal correctness properties; it is purely a library of state-level and mathematical operators built using sets, sequences, choice, recursion through finite-domain function definitions, and TLC's Print operator.
desc_intent:
Specify a library of small, purely functional collection utilities to be used by larger specifications. The model must include operations over finite sets, finite sequences, and sets of sets, and must treat these collections as immutable values. Required operations:

- A test whether two sets intersect (nonempty intersection).
- Total functions that compute the maximum and minimum elements of a nonempty finite set of comparable natural values, returning a well-defined element.
- A generic fold/reduction over finite sets and over finite sequences that applies a binary operator and a base value to produce a single result; the set reduction must be order-independent and well-defined for any finite set.
- Conversion between a finite sequence and the corresponding set of its elements, and a way to test whether a sequence is empty.
- A function returning the last element of a nonempty sequence, and a function that removes all occurrences of a given element from a sequence, producing a sequence.
- An operation that computes the intersection of a set of sets (dual to union), defined for a finite collection of sets.
- A construction that enumerates all permutations of a finite set, represented as finite sequences containing each element exactly once.
- A deterministic index operation that returns some valid index of a given element in a sequence containing that element.

For each operation, state preconditions (e.g., nonemptiness), the expected result type, and key correctness properties: soundness (result satisfies the intended meaning), completeness (all valid outcomes are possible for nondeterministic choices), and termination on finite inputs. Ensure the set reduction is invariant under input element order and the sequence reduction follows sequence order. Include unit-test style assertions that fail visibly when an operation produces an incorrect result.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a Knuth-Yao style stochastic state machine for generating one of the outcomes 1 through 6 by repeatedly tossing a fair coin and following a transition graph. The variables track the current dyadic probability mass p associated with the current node, the current control state, and the most recent coin flip. The specification initializes at state "s0" with probability One, evolves by halving p on each step and updating state through the Transition table, and asserts a standard temporal behavior consisting of initialization, next-state steps, and weak fairness of Next.
desc_intent:
Specify a randomized algorithm that generates an outcome from a fixed discrete distribution on six labeled outcomes {1,2,3,4,5,6} by repeatedly tossing unbiased coins and following a finite-state decision process. The model should represent an initial "undecided" state and a finite directed transition graph whose edges are labeled by coin results; some nodes are terminal and correspond to one of the six outcomes. The process repeatedly samples a fair coin and moves along the edge determined by the toss until a terminal node is reached. At each coin toss the remaining probability mass assigned to the current undecided branch is halved. 

The specification must require termination with probability 1: eventually a terminal outcome is selected. It must also require correctness of output probabilities: the probability of terminating at each outcome equals the intended target distribution (given as rational dyadic numbers summing to 1). Probability reasoning should be explicit: track the residual probability mass carried by the current undecided path and show that when a terminal node is reached the accumulated mass yields the correct output probability. In addition, require a quantitative convergence property: for any positive epsilon, with probability 1 the algorithm reaches a terminal node before the residual mass falls below epsilon (equivalently, the residual mass converges to 0 only along nonterminating traces, which have probability 0). Do not prescribe a particular encoding of states or coin flips; focus on the behavior, termination, and distributional correctness properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a simple Markov-style probabilistic transition system encoded in TLA+ using rational weights represented as numerator-denominator tuples. The state starts at an initial node and evolves according to a transition function, while the variable p accumulates path probability mass by multiplying the current probability tuple by the chosen transition weight. The specification defines initialization, a next-state relation with weak fairness, and proves that every behavior satisfying Spec eventually reaches an accepting state or a zero-normalized probability.
desc_intent:
Model a finite-state discrete-time probabilistic process that starts in a single designated initial state and moves along transitions that carry rational probabilities. The system should record (1) the current control state and (2) the cumulative probability mass remaining for the single execution branch being tracked. Each step selects one outgoing destination from the current state according to that state's transition distribution and multiplies the tracked probability mass by the probability of the chosen transition. The model should stop exploring transitions out of a state once the state is in a specified set of absorbing or "accepting" states. The transition graph may contain cycles and branching, and transition probabilities from each state form a proper probability distribution (sum to 1). 

Specify correctness properties ensuring:
- The process begins in the initial state with full unit probability mass.
- At each non-accepting state with nonzero remaining mass, exactly one outgoing transition is taken and the mass is updated by multiplication with the transition probability.
- If the remaining mass becomes zero the process may continue but no further probability is transferred.
- Liveness: from the initial configuration, eventually either an accepting state is reached or the tracked probability mass becomes zero.
- Safety: probability mass never becomes negative and is always representable as a rational number derived by multiplying transition probabilities.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a very simple system in which a single variable x starts at 0 and is repeatedly incremented by 2 forever. The file includes a PlusCal algorithm and its generated TLA+ translation, with the temporal specification given by Init /\ [][Next]_vars. It proves a type invariant that x always remains a natural number and also proves that x is always even, using TLAPS proof steps and the auxiliary divisibility operator a|b.
desc_intent:
Specify a simple infinite-state sequential system that models a single numeric counter repeatedly incremented by two. The model should treat the counter as a natural number initialized to zero and allow an unbounded, nonterminating sequence of steps each of which increases the counter value by exactly 2.

The specification must state the legal initial states and step relation without prescribing an implementation technique. It must permit only those transitions that add two to the current value; no other transitions (including stuttering or arbitrary jumps) are allowed except as required to express temporal properties.

Require and verify these correctness properties:

- Type safety: the counter value remains a natural number in every reachable state.
- Evenness invariant: the counter value is always an even integer (divisible by two) in every reachable state.
- Liveness: the system must always be able to perform another increment (i.e., there are infinitely many steps — no deadlock).

Express the specification using temporal logic so that invariants are provable as safety properties (always holds) and the liveness requirement is stated as a fairness or progress obligation ensuring the repeated increment action can always occur. Avoid encoding internal implementation details; describe only states, transitions, and the properties to be ensured.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies and proves correctness of a very simple algorithm for finding the largest value in a sequence of natural numbers. The algorithm iterates through a sequence variable f, maintains a current highest value h, and advances an index i until termination, after which h is shown to be greater than or equal to every element of the sequence. The specification includes the PlusCal algorithm and its TLA+ translation, defines type and inductive invariants, proves a helper property about the final index value, and then proves overall correctness with TLAPS proof steps. The design explicitly allows infinite stuttering after termination to avoid deadlock.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of an algorithm that scans a finite, nonempty sequence of natural numbers and computes the maximum value in that sequence. The model should describe a procedure that reads the sequence elements one by one in a single pass, maintains a variable representing the current candidate for the maximum, and advances an index until every element has been inspected. The procedure must allow an initially empty-looking candidate (a sentinel) and update it whenever a larger element is observed. The model must terminate when the index has passed the last element and then expose the computed maximum.

Require the following correctness properties to be proved as invariants or theorems of the specification:
- Type/Domain invariants: the input is always a finite sequence of natural numbers, the index always ranges from 1 to length+1 during execution, and the candidate maximum is always either a natural number or the sentinel.
- Inductive invariant: after inspecting k elements, the candidate is at least as large as every element among the first k inspected elements.
- Termination property: the scan finishes (index reaches length+1) eventually.
- Postcondition (functional correctness): upon termination, the candidate is greater than or equal to every element of the input sequence (i.e., it is a valid maximum). Also state any necessary lemmas that relate the index at termination to having examined all elements.

Do not commit to a particular programming-language encoding; describe only states, the allowed single-step transitions that advance the index and possibly update the candidate, and the invariants and liveness properties to be established.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies and model checks an implementation of Booth's algorithm for finding the lexicographically least circular substring, i.e. the least rotation of a sequence. The file contains a PlusCal algorithm and its generated TLA+ translation, with state variables tracking the input sequence, its length, the failure-function array, loop indices, and the program counter. It verifies a type invariant over the translated state and states a partial-correctness property asserting that when the program counter reaches "Done", the computed shift k yields a lexicographically minimal rotation, with ties broken by the smallest shift.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of an algorithm that, given a fixed finite circular string (a sequence of characters drawn from a known finite character set), computes the starting index of the lexicographically least rotation of that string. The model should treat the input string as immutable and represent rotations as cyclic shifts of the string; equal rotations are ordered by their numeric starting index to break ties (i.e., prefer the smallest index among equal rotations). The algorithm must examine characters (and possibly maintain auxiliary indices and a small auxiliary array) but the specification must not commit to a particular implementation technique—only the abstract behavior and required invariants.

Require the following correctness properties:
- Safety: At termination, the reported index denotes a rotation that is lexicographically less-than-or-equal-to every other rotation of the input string; if a rotation equals it, its starting index is not smaller.
- Type and domain invariants: all data structures and indices always remain within their declared finite domains (array indices inside bounds, indicator values drawn from specified sentinel values when used).
- Termination: the procedure terminates after a finite number of steps for any finite input string.

Also specify useful auxiliary definitions: what a rotation is, lexicographic ordering of sequences, and the set of all rotations. Express the main correctness property in terms of these definitions and ensure the model allows checking those invariants and termination for arbitrary finite inputs.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a small model-checking wrapper around a least-circular-substring specification. It introduces two constants, one bounding the character set size and one bounding the maximum string length, and then defines finite ranges derived from those constants for use as model domains. The file does not define any state variables, actions, temporal specification, or correctness properties; it only provides simple value-level definitions intended to constrain or instantiate the imported algorithm.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a function that computes the lexicographically least rotation (circular substring) of a finite string over a fixed finite alphabet. The system should accept as inputs a string length bound and an alphabet size, and operate on any concrete string whose length does not exceed the bound and whose symbols range over the alphabet. The model must express the notion of circular rotation and define the order used for comparing rotations (standard lexicographic order over the alphabet symbols).

The model must capture a deterministic algorithm that, given an input string, produces a rotation index specifying which rotation is least and the resulting rotated string. It should ensure the output rotation is valid (an index within the string length) and that the rotated string is equal to the original string rotated by that index. For empty strings or length-one strings the model should behave correctly (identity rotation).

Key correctness properties to guarantee:
- Minimality: the chosen rotation yields a string that is lexicographically no greater than any other rotation of the same input.
- Uniqueness or canonicality: if multiple rotations are lexicographically equal, the model should deterministically choose one canonical index (for example, the smallest index).
- Stability under equal-symbol alphabets and varying lengths up to the bound.
- Safety: the algorithm never produces out-of-range indices or symbols outside the alphabet.

Include invariants that relate the input, chosen index, and output, and specify termination (the algorithm always produces a result).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines utility operators for finite zero-indexed sequences represented as functions with domain 0..(n-1). It provides constructors and conversions between ordinary one-indexed TLA+ sequences and this zero-indexed representation, along with derived operators for length, valid indices, rotations, and a lexicographic order. The module is a pure mathematical helper library with no state variables, no transition system, no fault model, and no temporal verification properties; its notable design choice is to represent zero-indexed sequences explicitly as functions rather than using the built-in Sequences indexing convention.

This module specifies the level-checking for the TLA+ language. It defines semantic-node structures, level metadata, and recursive correctness conditions used to determine when expressions are level-correct.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of TLA+ level checking for expressions and operator definitions. The model should represent modules, operator definitions, declarations (constant and variable), operator parameters (including higher-order/operator parameters), let-in expressions, instances (with substitutions), and expression forms whose semantics impose level restrictions (constants, state expressions, actions, temporal formulas). It must capture how the syntactic constructs of a module constrain the allowed “level” of subexpressions and operator arguments without committing to a particular implementation method for checking.

Requirements:
- Define the notion of expression level (four levels: constant, state, action, temporal) and how compound constructs determine the required maximum level of their operands (for example, priming, ENABLED, action contexts, temporal operators, and constructs that require non-temporal arguments).
- Represent level constraints on formal parameters and operator parameters, including constraints that an operator parameter must accept arguments of certain minimal levels for each of its positions.
- Capture how the level of an operator application depends on the operator’s declared/derived level and weights, and how operator definitions impose constraints on their parameters (including conservative approximations required for second-order parameters).
- Model how instance substitution and parameter instantiation propagate and combine constraints across module boundaries, and how to detect violations: an instantiation or expression is illegal if constraints require a parameter to be instantiated by an expression whose level exceeds allowed limits.
- Specify key correctness properties: soundness (if the model accepts an expression as level-correct then every expansion that replaces defined operators by their bodies produces an expression that meets the informal level rules), conservative safety for higher-order parameters (disallowing instantiations that could produce illegal levels), and termination/decidability of the checking algorithm on finite module forests.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a binary search algorithm over a sorted sequence `seq` of integer values from a constant set `Values`, searching for a target value `val`. The translated algorithm maintains variables `low`, `high`, and `result`, repeatedly checking the middle element and narrowing the search range until either a matching index is found or the search terminates with `result = 0`. The specification includes a temporal behavior `Spec` with weak fairness on `Next`, a termination property stating that eventually `pc = "Done"`, and a TLAPS proof that the safety property `resultCorrect` is invariant under the behavior.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a deterministic search procedure that, given a sorted finite sequence of comparable integer values and a target integer, repeatedly narrows an index range to determine whether the target appears in the sequence. The model should accept any sorted sequence and any target from a given domain. It must maintain a current inclusive lower and upper index bound that always lie within or immediately adjacent to the valid index range, and a result indicator that is either zero (meaning “not yet found” or “not present”) or an index pointing to a found element.

The model must capture the search loop that chooses a middle index of the current bound and examines the element at that index; if the element equals the target it must set the result to that index and terminate, otherwise it must shrink the bound to the appropriate half that could still contain the target. The model should allow termination when the bounds cross, indicating no element equals the target.

Specify the following correctness properties to be proved as invariants or temporal properties:
- Safety (partial correctness): if the procedure terminates with a nonzero result, the sequence element at that index equals the target; if it terminates with result zero, the target does not occur anywhere in the sequence.
- Invariant bounds and typing: indices and result stay within valid integer ranges throughout execution; bounds always define a contiguous integer interval or adjacent indices when empty.
- Progress/termination: from any initial state the procedure eventually reaches a terminal state (either found or proven absent) under fair scheduling.
- Preservation of sortedness and that narrowing always preserves the existence (or nonexistence) of any target element within the current bounds (i.e., if the target exists in the whole sequence, it is always contained within the current bound until found).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a lightweight wrapper around another specification, Majority, and provides Apalache-oriented type annotations plus a concrete value definition for use with configuration. It declares the constants and variables expected by the imported Majority instance and defines a concrete set of values.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of an algorithm that, given a finite sequence of values drawn from a fixed finite domain, selects a candidate for a majority value and computes its count. The system must accept any input sequence of values and produce two outputs: a single candidate value from the domain and an integer count equal to the number of occurrences of that candidate in the input sequence.

The model should capture the progression of a sequential procedure that inspects elements of the sequence in order, maintains a current candidate and an integer counter, and updates them based only on the current element and the current candidate and count. The model must allow the algorithm to terminate after exactly one pass over the sequence and yield the final candidate and count.

Specify invariants and correctness properties that must hold for every execution:
- The candidate at all times is a value from the given finite domain; the count is a non‑negative integer.
- After termination, the reported count equals the actual number of occurrences of the reported candidate in the original sequence.
- If some value appears strictly more than half of the sequence positions, then after termination the reported candidate must be that majority value.
- The model should rule out illegal states such as reading beyond the bounds of the sequence or using counts that exceed the sequence length.

Do not constrain the algorithm to a specific implementation; allow any stepwise, deterministic or nondeterministic, sequential update strategy that performs a single linear scan and satisfies the properties above.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies Boyer and Moore's majority vote algorithm over an input sequence of values. The algorithm scans the sequence in one pass, maintaining an index i, a current candidate cand, and a counter cnt, and it guarantees that when the scan is complete, any value with an absolute majority must equal cand. The specification includes a temporal behavior Spec with initialization, a next-state action, and weak fairness for Next, and it also defines correctness and an inductive invariant used for reasoning about the algorithm.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of the Boyer–Moore majority vote problem: given a finite sequence of values drawn from a fixed nonempty domain, produce an element after a single left-to-right pass that is guaranteed to be the only possible majority element of the whole sequence. The model should describe a single-pass streaming procedure that maintains only constant additional state (independent of sequence length) and may inspect each input element once in order. It must accept any fixed input sequence of arbitrary but finite length and nonempty value domain.

The specification must state the expected observable output at termination and the correctness requirements: if any value occurs strictly more than half of the positions in the input, then the reported element must equal that majority value; conversely, if no value has such a strict majority, no particular output is required (the procedure may return an arbitrary candidate). The model should record and reason about counts needed to support proofs but should not assume extra storage proportional to sequence length.

Include invariants that make it possible to prove the main safety property (uniqueness of a possible majority equal to the final candidate when one exists) and state liveness so that the procedure completes after processing all input elements. Ensure the model supports checking the safety property for all sequences up to a bounded length.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a thin wrapper around another specification, Reachable, used to attach Apalache type annotations while keeping the original module free of tool-specific annotations. It declares constants for a graph-like structure consisting of a set of nodes, a successor function from nodes to sets of nodes, and a distinguished root node, and it declares variables marked, vroot, and pc with annotated types. The module does not define its own transition system, temporal specification, or correctness properties; instead, it instantiates Reachable with direct substitutions for the three constants and additionally defines concrete constant values NodesVal, SuccVal, and RootVal for use by configuration.
desc_intent: Model a graph reachability procedure that explores nodes starting from a designated root and marks all nodes reachable via directed successor edges. The model should represent a finite set of nodes, a successor relation that assigns to each node a set of outgoing neighbors, and a distinguished root node. The specification must describe nondeterministic exploration steps that can choose an unmarked node reachable from the root via a sequence of successor edges (possibly discovered incrementally) and then mark it. The system must ensure progress: if there exists an unmarked node reachable from the root, the procedure may eventually mark some such node until no reachable unmarked nodes remain. The model should permit arbitrary exploration orders (not require breadth-first or depth-first), but must prevent marking nodes that are not reachable from the root. Safety properties to guarantee: (1) only nodes in the finite node set may ever be marked; (2) once a node is marked it remains marked (marks are monotonic); and (3) a node is marked only if there exists a path from the root to that node following the successor relation. Liveness properties to guarantee: every node that is reachable from the root is eventually marked (fairness assumptions may be stated explicitly). Include an invariant characterizing the set of marked nodes relative to reachability and assert termination when no further reachable unmarked nodes exist.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module contains TLAPS proofs for the safety properties of the parallel reachability algorithm specified in the imported module ParReach. It proves that the invariant Inv is preserved by Spec and also proves a refinement-style safety result showing that the concrete specification implies the initialization and step relation of an instantiated module R under the refinement mapping already defined in ParReach. The file is proof-oriented rather than algorithm-defining: it introduces no new state variables or transition operators of its own, and focuses on invariant preservation, stuttering-step reasoning, and refinement of safety behavior.
desc_intent:
Model a parallel reachability-checking algorithm for a fixed finite set of processes that cooperatively explore a directed graph of states. The system should capture processes that repeatedly attempt to discover and mark a designated root set, propagate reachability information, and eventually terminate while preserving safety. Specify the initial conditions (no marks, all processes in starting control locations) and the allowed atomic steps for each process: steps that inspect or update shared reachability information, steps that mark a node as reached and possibly change a local program counter, and steps that complete and stop participating. The model must allow nonblocking interleaving of process steps and asynchronous choices of which process executes next.

Require these correctness properties:
- A global safety invariant: every update to the shared reachability data must maintain a representation invariant (e.g., consistency between per-process view and the global marked set), and no process may introduce an inconsistent marking.
- Termination safety: once all processes have reached their terminating control location, the shared reachability data is stable (unchanged thereafter).
- Refinement correctness: the parallel algorithm must implement an abstract sequential safety specification under a refinement mapping that relates concrete process-local and shared variables to abstract state; formally, every behavior of the parallel system maps to a behavior satisfying the abstract Init and Next.
- Type invariants: variables always remain within their declared finite domains (process set, node set, control labels).

Do not prescribe a particular implementation structure; instead, define states, allowed atomic transitions, and the invariants and refinement relation the model must guarantee.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a parallel multiprocess version of Misra's reachability algorithm. It models a set of processes that cooperatively explore nodes reachable from a distinguished root, maintaining a shared set `marked` and work set `vroot`, with per-process local variables `u` and `toVroot`; the algorithm terminates iff the reachable set from `Root` is finite, and on termination `marked` equals that reachable set. The specification includes the PlusCal translation, a fairness-based temporal specification for all processes, an inductive invariant used for refinement, and theorems asserting that the parallel algorithm refines the imported reachability specification and satisfies both its safety and fairness parts.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent graph reachability algorithm executed by a fixed finite set of worker processes that collectively determine the set of nodes reachable from a designated root in a finite directed graph. The specification should describe the abstract system, not an implementation: workers repeatedly pick unexplored nodes from a shared work pool, mark a picked node as visited, and add its successors to the shared pool (possibly one successor at a time). The system must satisfy:

- Safety: At all times, every node recorded as visited must indeed be a node of the graph; every node added to the shared pool must be a graph node; and the union of visited nodes and nodes in the pool must always be a subset of nodes reachable from the root.
- Partial correctness: If the algorithm terminates with no workers able to proceed, then the set of visited nodes equals exactly the set of nodes reachable from the root.
- Termination/Progress: The system should terminate (all workers become quiescent) if and only if the reachable set is finite; if the reachable set is finite, then under weak fairness of worker actions the algorithm must eventually reach a quiescent state.
- Refinement relation (informal): The concurrent behavior should be allowed to take extra internal steps (e.g., adding successors one at a time) but must implement an abstract sequential reachability algorithm that adds a node and all its successors atomically.

Also require simple typing/invariant properties for worker-local state to enable proofs of the safety and refinement claims.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies reachability in a directed graph represented by a set of nodes and a successor function Succ mapping each node to the set of its outgoing neighbors. It defines what it means for a sequence to be a path from one node to another, uses existential quantification over sequences of nodes to define when a path exists, and then defines the set of nodes reachable from a given set S. The module includes a typing assumption that Succ is a function from Nodes to subsets of Nodes, and it contains no state variables, actions, temporal behavior, fairness conditions, or proofs beyond the commented note about TLAPS modules.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of reachability in a finite directed graph. The model should describe what a directed graph is, what it means for a path to exist between two nodes, and what nodes are reachable from a given set of start nodes. The model must allow arbitrary finite sets of nodes and arbitrary adjacency information (successor relation) but must not commit to any particular internal representation. It must define a path as a nonempty finite sequence of nodes in which each consecutive pair is connected by a directed edge in the graph, and it must define the existence of a path from one node to another exactly when such a sequence exists. It must define the reachable-from operator that maps any set of start nodes to the set of all nodes reachable from some start node (including the start nodes themselves). Key correctness properties to guarantee: (1) Reflexivity: every start node is reachable from itself. (2) Transitive closure: if a node y is reachable from x and z is reachable from y, then z is reachable from x. (3) Soundness with respect to edges: if there is a direct edge from x to y, then y is reachable from x. (4) Finiteness: for finite graphs, reachable sets are finite. Additionally require invariance under equivalent representations of adjacency (e.g., edge-set vs. successor-function): the reachable-set must be representation-independent.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies Jayadev Misra's algorithm for computing the set of graph nodes reachable from a distinguished node Root in a directed graph. The graph structure itself is taken from the imported Reachability module via the constants Nodes and Succ, and the algorithm maintains two sets, marked and vroot, plus a control variable pc generated by the PlusCal translation. The specification defines the translated PlusCal algorithm, its temporal specification with weak fairness of Next, several state invariants used for partial correctness, a theorem asserting that termination implies the computed set equals the mathematical reachable set, and a liveness theorem asserting eventual termination when the reachable set is finite.
desc_intent:
Specify a system that computes the set of nodes reachable from a designated root in a directed graph. Model an algorithm that progressively discovers reachable nodes using two collections: one representing nodes already acknowledged as discovered and one representing pending nodes to process. The system must begin with the discovered set empty and the pending set containing only the root. Repeatedly, while the pending set is nonempty, choose a node from the pending set and either (a) if that node has not yet been acknowledged, acknowledge it and add all of its immediate successors to the pending set, or (b) if it is already acknowledged, remove it from the pending set. Termination should occur when the pending set is empty.

Require the model to guarantee the following correctness properties:
- Safety (partial correctness): if the algorithm terminates, the acknowledged set equals exactly the set of nodes reachable from the root.
- Invariants: the discovered and pending sets are always subsets of the graph's node set; every successor of an acknowledged node is either acknowledged or pending; and the union of acknowledged nodes with the set of nodes reachable from the pending set always equals the set reachable from the union of acknowledged and pending nodes. These invariants should imply the partial correctness claim.
- Liveness (termination): if the set of nodes reachable from the root is finite, the algorithm eventually terminates (under weak fairness of the processing step).

Also require type constraints on state components and that termination is represented explicitly so model checking and reasoning about invariants and liveness can be carried out.

desc_declarative_gpt: This TLA+ specification provides a TLAPS proof for the Missionaries and Cannibals problem, focusing on type correctness. The proof shows that the system, as defined by the Init and Next operators (from the MissionariesAndCannibals module), maintains the TypeOK invariant throughout all behaviors. The property Spec => []TypeOK is proven, where Spec is defined as Init /\ [][Next]_vars. The proof is structured hierarchically and demonstrates that all reachable states satisfy the type invariant, though the comments note that this is not a real safety property but rather a proof skeleton for illustration.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of the classic Missionaries and Cannibals river‑crossing problem. The system should represent two river banks and a boat that can shuttle between them, carrying at most two people. There are two kinds of agents: missionaries and cannibals. Initially all agents are on one bank. A move is an atomic boat crossing that transfers one or two agents from the bank where the boat is located to the other bank, and then the boat ends up on the opposite bank. Model only legal moves that respect the boat capacity and only allow people who are present on the departure bank to board.

Require safety: at all times on each bank the number of missionaries present must be greater than or equal to the number of cannibals, unless there are zero missionaries on that bank (i.e., cannibals must never strictly outnumber missionaries on a bank where missionaries are present). Require progress/termination: there exists a sequence of legal moves that transfers all agents to the opposite bank (goal state). The model should permit nondeterministic choices of which legal crossing to take. Include explicit state invariants for valid bank and boat configuration types and for the safety property above. Do not commit to a particular search/control strategy; specify the transition relation and the invariants to be checked.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models the classic moving-cat puzzle with a line of numbered boxes. A cat occupies one box and must move every step to an adjacent box without wrap-around, while the observer checks boxes according to a back-and-forth search pattern over boxes 2 through N - 1, reversing direction at the ends. The spec defines an initial state, a cat movement action, an observation action, a combined next-state relation, a temporal specification with weak fairness for the cat's movement, and an eventual victory property stating that the observed box will eventually coincide with the cat's box.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a search game played on a line of N ≥ 2 discrete locations (boxes) where an adversary (the cat) occupies one location and must move each time step to an adjacent location (no staying still, no wrap-around). Each time step the searcher may inspect exactly one location to see whether the adversary is there. The model should allow the adversary to choose either adjacent move nondeterministically, and the searcher to choose which single box to inspect each step according to a deterministic strategy. Do not assume any simultaneous teleportation or skipping of boxes.

Require a search strategy that is generated from a simple repeated sweep pattern which only inspects interior boxes (i.e., excludes the two endpoints) and alternates direction at the interior endpoints, producing a periodic back-and-forth inspection sequence. The specification must state the allowed state space, the transition relation for the adversary moves, and the transition relation for the searcher’s inspection choice (including reversal at sweep endpoints). Impose fairness that the adversary always moves each step.

The key correctness property to guarantee is eventual discovery: starting from any initial positions and any phase of the sweep, the searcher’s strategy must ensure that eventually a time step occurs where the inspected location equals the adversary’s location. Also require invariants preserving bounds (positions remain within 1..N and inspection indices remain within the interior range) and state that the property holds for both even and odd N ≥ 2.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module contains TLAPS-checked proofs for the multi-car elevator specification, focusing on safety properties. It proves that the system maintains type correctness and safety invariants, as specified in the main Elevator module, by strengthening the state invariant and deriving the required invariants as corollaries. The liveness (temporal) properties are not addressed here. The proofs handle the limitations of TLAPS regarding multi-argument function application by explicitly stating unfolding lemmas, and they make explicit the disjointness between Elevator and Floor, which is implicit in TLC models. The proof strategy involves mutual induction over several auxiliary invariants, with detailed case analysis for each action, but the full inductive step for the strengthened safety invariant is omitted as it is complex and left for future work.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a multi-elevator building control system with the following components and requirements.

Model a fixed set of floors and a fixed set of elevator cars that move between floors, open and close doors, and carry persons. Model persons with a current location (either a floor or an elevator), a destination floor, and a waiting flag. Model elevator state including current floor, motion direction (Up, Down, or Stationary), door state (open/closed), and the set of floor buttons pressed inside each car. Model external elevator calls as a pair (floor, direction). The system must support user actions: a person selecting a new destination, calling an elevator from a floor, entering and exiting a car, the elevator opening and closing doors, moving, stopping, and a dispatcher assigning a car to an active call.

Require the following correctness properties to be guaranteed by the model:
- Type safety: all state variables always respect their declared domains (e.g., people locations are either floors or elevators, button sets are subsets of floors).
- Safety invariants:
  - No waiting person is located in the elevator at the same time as their destination (waiting implies location ≠ destination).
  - If an elevator’s doors are open, its current floor is not listed among that car’s pressed buttons and the car is not Stationary (doors open implies a motion direction and the floor not in pressed-buttons).
  - When doors are open and the car has a direction, the corresponding call (floor,direction) is not simultaneously active.
  - A car in Stationary state contains no persons.
  - If a person is located in a car, then either their destination is among that car’s pressed buttons or the car’s doors are open at their destination floor.
- Initial conditions: define an initial state with no active calls, all doors closed, cars Stationary, buttons empty, and all persons located on floors and not waiting.
- Progress assumptions may be left unspecified, but the model should state the safety invariants are preserved under all allowed actions.

Do not prescribe an implementation; instead describe the abstract state, the allowed atomic transitions (preconditions and state effects), and the invariants to be proved inductive for all actions including stuttering.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple multi-car elevator system with a set of people, a set of elevators, and a bounded set of floors. It defines how people choose destinations, call elevators, enter and exit cars, how elevators open and close doors, move, stop, and are dispatched to calls using a simple nearest-eligible-elevator policy rather than a globally optimized scheduling algorithm. The specification includes type and safety invariants, temporal liveness expectations that calls are eventually serviced and waiting people eventually reach their destinations, and fairness assumptions over the main actions; it culminates in a theorem asserting that under Spec, the type, safety, and temporal invariants always hold.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a multi-elevator building control system that coordinates several cars and multiple people requesting service across a fixed set of floors. The model should describe how people decide destinations, make elevator calls, board and exit cars, and how cars move, open and close doors, and accept button presses. It must capture asynchronous interleaving of actions and allow nondeterministic choices for scheduling, subject to fairness assumptions that ensure progress of enabled actions.

Require the model to guarantee the following correctness properties:
