- Type safety: all state components always conform to their intended domains (people locations are either floors or a car, destinations are valid floors, elevator attributes like floor, direction, door state and pressed buttons are well formed, and the set of active calls is a subset of valid call descriptors).
- Safety invariants: no elevator reports a button for a floor unless some passenger inside wants that floor; people inside a car are only carried in a direction consistent with their destination; active elevator calls correspond to actual waiting people (no ghost calls).
- Liveness guarantees: every active call is eventually serviced by some car reaching that floor and opening doors; any person who has pressed a call and is waiting eventually reaches their destination.
- No deadlock: cars that can move, open doors, or respond to calls may eventually do so under reasonable fairness assumptions.

Do not prescribe a particular dispatching or optimization algorithm, but allow expressing a dispatch policy that chooses a car to serve a call (for example, preferring closest stationary or already-approaching cars). The model should separate environment actions (people creating calls and choosing destinations) from elevator actions and include fairness constraints so temporal properties about eventual service can be checked.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models MultiPaxos in the style of state machine replication (SMR) for a single key, supporting both write and read commands. The network is modeled as a monotonic set of sent messages, capturing asynchronous, non-Byzantine behavior: messages may be delayed, duplicated, or lost (with the assumption that lost messages are retried until received). The spec checks linearizability from the client's perspective by observing the sequence of request and acknowledgement events, and verifies liveness by ensuring no deadlocks occur until all requests are observed. The design is modular, with clear separation of client events, server states, and message types, and is implemented in PlusCal with a translation to TLA+ for model checking. Notable design decisions include the use of unique ballots for leader election, explicit modeling of majority quorums, and a focus on practical system behaviors such as idempotency and efficient state space reduction.
desc_intent:
Model a replicated state-machine system that implements Multi-Paxos-style consensus for a single logical key, supporting two classes of client operations: writes (which install a new value) and reads (which observe the current value). The model should describe a set of server replicas that communicate by asynchronous, unreliable point-to-point broadcasts: messages may be arbitrarily delayed, duplicated, or lost, but non-Byzantine behavior is assumed (nodes follow the protocol). Clients submit a finite, pre-determined set of requests; the system should process them until all requests have been acknowledged.

The specification must capture these requirements and correctness properties (without prescribing an implementation):

- Safety (consensus/consistency): committed commands for each log position must be the same on a majority quorum and never diverge; once a command is committed at a position, no different command can later be committed at that position. Reads must observe values consistent with the serialized sequence of committed writes.

- Linearizability from the client viewpoint: the sequence of client-visible request/acknowledgement events must correspond to some sequential execution of the submitted commands that respects real-time order of observed events (each acknowledged operation appears to take effect at some point between its request and acknowledgement).

- Progress/Liveness under non-failure assumptions: if a majority of replicas remain non-faulty and messages between them can eventually be delivered, then every client request is eventually acknowledged (no permanent deadlock before all requests are processed).

- Leader election and preemption semantics: the model must permit leaders to be chosen using ballot numbers, allow leaders to recover prior votes during preparation, and allow higher ballots to preempt lower ones while preserving safety.

Capture replica local state for rounds/ballots, per-slot proposals and votes, commit visibility and apply semantics, and network message sets needed to express Prepare/PrepareReply, Accept/AcceptReply, and Commit notifications. Specify invariants asserting quorum intersection and the preservation of previously accepted votes when forming new proposals so safety holds.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the N-queens problem and an iterative algorithm that computes all valid queen placements on an N x N chessboard. A placement is represented as a sequence or function from rows to columns, and the specification defines when two queens attack each other, what it means for a partial or full placement to be a solution, and the full set of solutions. The file contains a PlusCal algorithm and its TLA+ translation, with variables tracking partial solutions still to explore and full solutions already found, and it verifies safety properties such as type correctness and solution inclusion as well as temporal properties including termination and weak fairness-based progress.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of an algorithm that finds all placements of N queens on an N×N chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no two in the same row, column, or diagonal). The model should treat a full placement as an ordered list of N column positions, one per row, and allow partial placements of length ≤ N representing queens placed in the first k rows. The system should explore the space of partial solutions by repeatedly selecting some partial placement, computing every nonattacking way to place a queen in the next row, and replacing the selected partial placement with those extensions (or recording extensions as complete solutions when they reach length N). The model must permit nondeterministic choice of which pending partial placement to expand next and of which legal column positions to extend with, so the search order is unspecified.

The specification must guarantee:
- Safety: every recorded full placement is a valid nonattacking solution, and every pending partial placement contains no pair of attacking queens.
- Progress: when pending partial placements remain, the algorithm can make progress (i.e., it can always perform an expansion step); termination is reached precisely when no pending partial placements remain and all solutions have been discovered.
- Completeness: once the search finishes, the set of recorded full placements equals the set of all valid N-queen solutions.
- Type invariants: pending and solution collections only contain sequences of appropriate lengths and values in 1..N.

Also state liveness properties ensuring the search does not starve expansions (e.g., a weak/strong fairness requirement on the expansion action). Do not prescribe a particular internal representation or operational scheduling beyond the nondeterministic selection of a pending partial placement and its legal extensions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the N-queens problem and an iterative algorithm for computing all solutions. A queen placement is represented as a function from rows to columns, concretely as a sequence, and partial placements are represented as shorter sequences. The algorithm maintains a set of partial solutions in todo and a set of complete solutions in sols, repeatedly extending one partial solution by placing the next queen in every non-attacking column. The specification includes an initial condition, a next-state action with weak fairness, a type invariant, a correctness invariant relating sols and the mathematical set of all solutions, and a termination property asserting that eventually todo becomes empty.
desc_intent:
Model the N-queens solver that incrementally constructs all valid placements of N queens on an N×N chessboard so that no two queens share a row, column, or diagonal. The model should represent partial placements that place exactly one queen in each of the first k rows for some k ≤ N and full placements when k = N. The system repeatedly chooses a partial placement, computes all column positions in the next row that do not conflict with already placed queens, and replaces the chosen partial placement by all resulting one-row-extended partial placements; if the extension reaches N rows it is recorded as a full solution instead of being requeued. Specify the initial condition, the progress steps that add and remove partial placements and accumulate full solutions, and fairness so that the iterative extension step cannot be permanently disabled.

Require the following correctness properties:
- Safety: every recorded full placement is a valid N-queens solution (no two queens attack each other).
- Sound coverage: when no partial placements remain, the set of recorded full placements equals the complete set of all N-queens solutions.
- Type invariants: partial placements have length < N, full placements have length = N, and placements use only column indices in 1..N.
- Termination liveness: eventually there are no remaining partial placements (the algorithm completes).
Also request that the specification be abstract (describe states as sets of partial and full placements) and avoid committing to a particular exploration order.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module adapts an underlying Nano specification to make it amenable to TLC model checking. It introduces a model-level hash function state and a helper implementation of hash calculation so that hash assignment can be represented with finite state, and it adds a stuttering action to stop progress gracefully once available hashes are exhausted. The specification verifies safety-related properties by asserting that the overall behavior satisfies both a type invariant and the underlying Nano safety invariant, while using a view that ignores hashFunction and lastHash when hashing states for model checking.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a simple permissioned blockchain system that captures how nodes create, sign, and append blocks to a replicated ledger using a finite pool of precomputed hash values. The model should include the following elements and guarantees, stated as requirements rather than an implementation.

- Actors and keys: a finite set of nodes, each associated with a private/public key pair. Some mapping assigns every private key to at least one node and every public key to at least one private key (keys need not be one-to-one).

- Blocks and ledger: blocks carry a creator identity, a pointer to a previous block (by hash), and a set of state changes (e.g., transfers). Each node maintains a local copy of the distributed ledger (a chain of blocks). The system starts from a genesis ledger with an initial balance state.

- Hash resource pool: model a finite set of hash tokens. Each hash token can be assigned to at most one concrete block value. Once a token is consumed to represent a block, it becomes bound to that block forever. If all tokens are consumed, no further block creation should be possible.

- Block creation and assignment: a node may propose a new block extending any existing block it knows that is valid with respect to the state, sign it with its private key, and consume an unused hash token to become that block’s identifier. Block creation must preserve ledger validity (e.g., balances nonnegative, signatures verifying against public keys).

- Dissemination and acceptance: nodes can receive blocks from others and adopt them into their local ledger if they are valid and extend their current view (allow forks). Nodes may accept blocks in any order but cannot invent or reuse hash tokens.

- Safety and invariants to verify:
  - Type and domain invariants: hashes map either to “no block” or to a concrete block; ledgers and messages are well-typed.
  - Integrity of hash pool: no two different blocks share the same hash token; once a token maps to a block it never reverts to “no block.”
  - Signature correctness: every block’s claimed creator must have a corresponding signature verifiable by the public key associated with that creator.
  - Balance safety: applying any block’s state changes to a ledger must not create negative balances and must preserve total funds except for well-defined permissioned minting in genesis.
  - Progress restriction: when hash tokens are exhausted, the system must stutter (no further changes to ledgers or hashes).
  - Liveness goal (optional to model-check): if unused hashes remain and nodes repeatedly attempt valid proposals and reliable delivery holds, then eventually some new block is appended to some node’s ledger.

Model the system abstractly so that correctness properties focus on safety (no invalid blocks accepted, no double assignment of hash tokens, no negative balances) and the resource-limited nature of block identifiers, without prescribing a particular consensus algorithm or message scheduling.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module models an early, now-outdated version of the Nano blockchain protocol. It represents signed blocks, account chains, balances, and per-node ledgers, along with actions for creating and processing genesis, open, send, receive, and change-representative blocks. The specification assumes abstract cryptographic primitives for hashing and signatures, models a distributed setting where each node maintains its own ledger and a set of received-but-unprocessed blocks, and verifies a safety theorem showing that the temporal specification implies the type invariant and a cryptographic safety invariant.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a distributed account-based ledger that uses account-specific chain structures (one chain per account) and cryptographic signatures to authorize state changes. The model should represent nodes that can create and propagate signed blocks of several kinds: an initial genesis allocation, account-opening blocks that claim prior send blocks, send blocks that decrease an account balance and mark funds as transferable to a destination account, receive blocks that claim a prior send and credit the recipient account, and change-representative blocks that update an account’s representative. The system must model a network in which nodes maintain local ledgers, exchange proposed signed blocks, validate signatures and block references, and append validated blocks to their local account chains. Hashing must be modeled abstractly so block identities (hashes) can be calculated and used as immutable references.

Require the model to enforce safety properties: signatures must validate against the public key controlling an account, an account may only be opened once, a receive may only consume a send that has not already been received, send amounts must not exceed the sender’s current balance, and the sum of all account balances never exceeds the initial genesis total. Also require type invariants for well-formed state. Do not prescribe specific implementation details for message delivery or hash/signature encodings beyond abstract operations and their intended semantics.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is an Apalache-oriented wrapper around another TLA+ specification named Prisoner, providing type annotations and a concrete constant value definition used by configuration. It models the constants and variables relevant to a prisoner problem, including a prisoner set, a light state, a count, an announced flag, a per-prisoner signalling function, and a set of prisoners who have visited. The module itself does not define the system dynamics, actions, or temporal properties; instead, it instantiates the Prisoner module and adds a concrete set of prisoner string values for use by APPrisoner.cfg.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of the classic "prisoners and a light" coordination problem. Model N prisoners who are in isolated cells and occasionally, one at a time, are brought into a shared interrogation room that contains a single light switch (or bulb) whose state may be initially unknown. The system runs indefinitely until some prisoner correctly announces that every prisoner has visited the room at least once. The model must allow arbitrary nondeterministic scheduling of which prisoner visits next, subject only to eventual fairness (each prisoner may visit infinitely often). Each visit gives the visiting prisoner the ability to observe and modify only the shared light state and to update their private memory; no other communication channel exists. The goal is to capture a protocol that, when followed by the prisoners, guarantees that eventually some prisoner will make a correct global announcement (i.e., the announcement is made only after all prisoners have visited at least once), and that incorrect announcements never occur.

Specify the state space (shared room state and per-prisoner private state), the allowed transitions for a visit, and an initial condition that leaves the light possibly unknown. Formalize the safety property: any announcement implies every prisoner has visited. Formalize the liveness property: under the fairness assumption of visits, an announcement will eventually occur. Include the ability to model standard leader-based or counter-based protocols and state invariants that ensure no announcement is made prematurely and that the counter logic cannot be tricked by repeated visits.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a fair solution to the classic readers-writers problem using a waiting queue of pending access requests. Processes can request either read or write access, queued requests are served from the head of the queue, readers may coexist, and writers require exclusive access with no current readers. The spec defines initialization, state transitions, weak fairness conditions for all request and service actions, safety invariants about mutual exclusion and writer cardinality, and liveness properties asserting that every actor eventually repeatedly reads, writes, and also eventually leaves those states.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of a fair readers–writers access-control system for a single shared resource. The model should describe an unbounded execution in which a fixed finite set of actors may request either read or write access, may be granted access, and may later release it. Requests must be queued so that all requests are served in a fair, FIFO manner: arrivals are enqueued and the front of the queue is considered for service. Multiple readers may hold the resource concurrently, but writers must have exclusive access. A writer may be granted the resource only when no readers are active. When the queue front is a read request, the system may grant it and may also grant subsequent queued read requests at the front(s) so long as no writer is started; when the queue front is a write request, only that writer may be started. Actors that already have a pending request must not enqueue duplicate identical requests. The model should include liveness constraints ensuring that every actor that repeatedly requests access will eventually be granted and will also eventually release the resource, and that the system does not starve any actor: every request eventually reaches the front and is served. Specify safety properties: readers and writers never hold the resource simultaneously, and at most one writer holds it at a time. Also specify type and queue-wellformedness invariants. Do not prescribe a particular implementation; leave queue and scheduling behavior abstract but constrained to satisfy the fairness and FIFO-serving requirements.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models an improved Software Defined Perimeter (SDP) architecture with a legitimate client, an SDP controller, a firewall, a target server, and an attacker operating under a Dolev-Yao-style attacker model for message interception, replay, spoofing, and probing. The design ties SPA authentication sessions to concrete data-plane TCP connection attempts using encrypted client/server tuple information, and the firewall is configured with exact 4-tuple ACL rules after successful authentication. The spec verifies both safety and liveness-style temporal properties about SPA authentication, anti-replay and anti-spoof behavior, legitimate user access availability, server hiddenness against attackers, firewall rule consistency, and firewall correctness under retransmission scenarios.
desc_intent:
Model a Software-Defined Perimeter (SDP) access-control system that mediates client access to a protected server using single-packet authorization (SPA) on a control plane and dynamic ACL configuration on a data plane. The model should include clients that request access, an SDP controller that authenticates SPA messages and programs the network firewall, a firewall that enforces ACLs on TCP connection attempts, an attacker that can sniff and replay or spoof SPA messages and can initiate TCP probes, and the protected server that accepts TCP connections only when permitted by the firewall.

Specify the allowed behaviors and interactions without prescribing implementation details: SPA messages must carry authenticated, integrity-protected, replay-resistant bindings between a particular client’s access intent and the TCP 4‑tuple for the target service; the controller must validate SPA messages, detect and log replay/spoof attempts, and install ephemeral ACL rules to allow the corresponding TCP handshake when authorization succeeds; the firewall must only forward TCP packets that match installed ACL rules otherwise drop and log them. The attacker may observe SPA and/or TCP traffic, craft forged SPA messages, or reuse captured data to attempt unauthorized access. Requirements and correctness properties: legitimate clients who send fresh, valid SPA messages and then complete the TCP handshake are eventually able to establish connections; no attacker without possession of the client key may cause the firewall to accept a TCP connection to the protected server (safety); replayed or out‑of‑sync SPA messages must not enable unauthorized data access; if the controller installs an ACL for a given SPA, it must be tied to the authenticated 4‑tuple and be short‑lived (no permanent exposure). Also state liveness goals: the controller and firewall together must permit a legitimate handshake within bounded steps after a valid SPA is received.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a Software Defined Perimeter (SDP) architecture with a legitimate client, an SDP controller, a firewall, a target server, and an attacker. The client performs Single Packet Authorization (SPA), the controller authenticates SPA messages and installs firewall ACL rules, the firewall mediates data-plane TCP traffic, and the attacker can sniff, replay, spoof, and probe based on captured information under a Dolev-Yao style threat model that does not break the underlying crypto abstractions. The spec verifies both safety and liveness-style properties, including that attacker SPA attempts are detected, legitimate SPA sessions lead to corresponding ACL rules, legitimate user access can eventually succeed, firewall behavior is consistent, and the attacker should not successfully establish protected service access.
desc_intent:
Model a Software-Defined Perimeter (SDP) access-control system that separates a control plane (authentication) from a data plane (connection admission) and is resilient to common network attacks. The model should include clients (legitimate users), an SDP controller that verifies single-packet-authentication (SPA) messages, a firewall that enforces short-lived access rules on the data plane, a target service that accepts TCP connections, and an attacker capable of sniffing, replaying, spoofing SPA messages, and probing the service. Specify the expected interactions at a high level: clients perform SPA to request access to a hidden service; the controller validates SPA messages (checking freshness, client credentials, integrity) and, on success, instructs the firewall to open a narrow, time- and 5-tuple-scoped data-plane admission rule that permits the client’s subsequent TCP handshake; the firewall enforces rules and logs dropped packets; the attacker can observe messages on network interfaces and may inject forged SPA or TCP packets and attempt to reuse or spoof captured credentials.

Formalize correctness properties including:
- Authorization soundness: only clients with a valid, non-replayed SPA should be able to complete a TCP handshake to the target service.
- Replay/spoof detection: the controller must detect and reject SPA messages that replay a prior Tstamp or that fail integrity/credential checks, and such incidents must be logged.
- Minimal exposure: firewall rules created by the controller must admit only the specific flow (addresses/ports) authorized by the SPA and must prevent unrelated attacker-initiated flows from being accepted.
- Non-bypassability: an attacker who only observes traffic (and cannot break cryptography) must not be able to gain data-plane access unless a valid SPA corresponding to that data flow was accepted by the controller or the attacker can legitimately impersonate credentials.
- Auditability: all authentication decisions, detected attacks, and created/expired firewall rules are recorded for inspection.

Allow modeling of NAT/shared-IP scenarios, per-session freshness counters, symmetric cryptographic primitives abstractly (with perfect secrecy except for modeled reuse), and nondeterministic network delivery (capture/sniff/inject) so attacks can be explored.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides Apalache-specific type annotations and concrete constant-value helper definitions for an underlying single-lane bridge specification. It declares the constant sets for cars approaching from the right and left, the bridge positions, and the overall positions domain, and it declares state variables for car locations and the queue of cars waiting before the bridge. The module instances the separate SingleLaneBridge specification module, but this file itself only contains the declarations, the instance statement, and concrete value definitions; it does not define the transition relation, temporal specification, or fault model directly.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a single-lane bridge crossing problem with multiple cars approaching from two opposite directions. The model should represent an environment in which cars arrive, wait, enter, traverse, and leave a constrained bridge that can accommodate traffic in only one direction at a time and has limited discrete positions. The system must allow cars to queue before the bridge, to occupy bridge positions while crossing, and to rejoin the road on the far side when finished.

Require safety properties:
- Mutual exclusion on the bridge: at any time, all cars that occupy bridge positions must be traveling in the same direction; no two cars from opposite directions may be on the bridge simultaneously.
- Exclusive occupancy: each bridge position may be occupied by at most one car.
- Position consistency: cars progress along adjacent bridge positions without teleportation; a car may only move to the next physical position if that position is free.

Require liveness properties:
- No deadlock: if cars are waiting on one or both sides and the bridge is free or will become free, some waiting car will eventually enter and cross.
- Fairness between directions: the model should avoid permanent starvation of one direction when there is continuous arrival from the other; provide a mechanism or fairness condition that guarantees eventual crossing for all waiting cars.

Also require invariants describing conservation of cars (cars are never lost or duplicated) and that each car’s state is always one of: waiting before bridge, occupying a specific bridge position, or having left the bridge.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models traffic over a single-lane bridge where cars may travel in two opposite directions, represented by the disjoint sets CarsRight and CarsLeft. The bridge admits concurrent movement only for cars traveling in the same direction, and the specification enforces safety conditions preventing cars going in opposite directions from occupying the bridge simultaneously or colliding within bridge positions. The model defines movement, waiting behavior before entering the bridge, weak fairness assumptions for movement and entry actions, and verifies safety invariants, typing constraints, and liveness properties stating that cars eventually enter and eventually exit the bridge.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a single-lane bridge crossing system with cars approaching from two opposite directions. The bridge is narrow so vehicles can travel on it only in one direction at a time, and cars can occupy discrete positions (approach lanes, bridge positions, and exits). The model should support multiple cars on the approach and on the bridge, with a queue for cars waiting to enter. It must permit cars to move forward along their path, enter the bridge when allowed, and leave the bridge to the far side.

Requirements:
- Safety: Never allow two cars that travel in opposite directions to be on the bridge simultaneously. Never allow two cars to occupy the same bridge position at the same time. The number of cars on the bridge must never exceed its capacity.
- Liveness: Every car that reaches the bridge approaches should eventually be able to enter the bridge and eventually exit the bridge (no permanent starvation).
- Fairness: Progress of cars must not be indefinitely blocked by unfair scheduling; specify fairness constraints so that each enabled move of a car cannot be deferred forever.
- External behavior: Cars follow deterministic step-forward movement rules along positions; when a car would step onto the bridge while another car(s) are already on it, entry must be blocked unless they all move in the same direction.
- Environment assumptions: Cars are partitioned into two direction groups (left-bound and right-bound), approach and bridge have ordered position sets, and there is at least one car and at least one bridge position.

State what constitutes a legal initial state (cars start off the bridge at ends) and state invariants and temporal properties to check (safety invariants and eventual entry/exit liveness).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the Slush protocol, a simple consensus algorithm from the Avalanche family, using a PlusCal algorithm translated into TLA+. The model captures nodes that hold colors, loop processes that repeatedly query sampled peers, query processes that answer with their current color, and a client process that initially assigns colors to uncolored nodes. The comments explicitly note that the protocol is probabilistic in intent, but the TLA+ model is not probabilistic and is therefore mainly useful as executable pseudocode plus basic temporal checking. The specification defines an initial state, a next-state relation over the translated PlusCal control flow, a type invariant, and a temporal termination property asserting eventual completion of all processes. It also includes an explicit terminating stuttering action to avoid deadlock once all processes reach the Done control state.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of the Slush consensus primitive (the simplest Avalanche-family protocol) as a distributed, asynchronous message-passing system of N hosts. The model should describe how hosts initially uncolored acquire an initial color from clients, repeatedly sample a fixed-size set of other hosts, query them for their current preferred color, and update their own preference based on a threshold of matching responses. The model must support concurrent execution of querying (querying processes) and answering (query processes) with messages in flight and without relying on probabilistic choice in the specification (sampling and message delivery may be modeled nondeterministically). Sampling must be from the set of other hosts and exclude self. Hosts must run a bounded number of consensus rounds; after completing their rounds they broadcast termination so that responders stop answering. The specification should capture: initialization of node colors (uncolored or one of two colors), query and reply message structure, the selection of a sample set of fixed cardinality, the per-round tally and threshold rule to adopt a color, and message removal after processing.

State the correctness properties to be verified:
- Safety: once all non-terminated hosts have the same preferred color, no subsequent actions can cause any host to adopt the opposite color (consensus is absorbing).
- Agreement (eventual strong agreement for deterministic traces): if all hosts terminate, they agree on a single color.
- Termination liveness: every host that begins with a color completes the prescribed number of rounds and eventually enters termination.
- No message corruption: replies correspond to queries sent earlier (no spurious messages).
Also specify invariants to check: color domain preservation, message typing, sample-set size constraint, and that queries are always directed to distinct other hosts.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a spanning-tree construction algorithm over an arbitrary graph whose node set is fixed by the constant Nodes and whose edge set is chosen nondeterministically as an initial value of the variable Edges. Each node maintains a parent pointer mom and an estimated distance dist from the distinguished root Root; nodes repeatedly update their parent and distance when they discover a neighbor with a shorter path, choosing any improved distance strictly between the neighbor's distance plus one and the node's current distance minus one. The spec checks type correctness, defines a temporal specification with weak fairness on Next, and states safety and liveness properties including a postcondition characterizing rooted, unreachable, and reachable nodes as well as an additional property AllDistancesOne.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a distributed breadth-first spanning-tree construction algorithm that runs on an undirected graph whose nodes are fixed and whose set of edges is initially unknown and may be any subset of possible links between nodes. The model should represent asynchronous local actions in which a node may adopt a neighbor as its parent and update its distance-to-root estimate based only on neighbors’ current distance values. The root node must advertise distance 0 and never change parent; unreachable nodes must remain with a special “infinite” distance and consider themselves as having no parent. The system must permit arbitrary initial undirected topologies and must allow nondeterministic asynchronous choices of which node acts next.

State the correctness requirements to prove:
- Safety: at all times when no further actions are enabled, every node either is the root, or is unreachable (distance infinite and no neighbor with finite distance), or has a parent that is one of its graph neighbors and whose distance equals the node’s distance minus one; in particular parents must lie on a shortest-path tree rooted at the root.
- Liveness: eventually the system reaches a stable configuration satisfying the postcondition above (every reachable node has a parent and correct distance), assuming fair scheduling of enabled actions.

Also require type and structural invariants (distances are natural numbers with a designated “infinite” value large enough, parents are nodes, and edges are undirected pairs of distinct nodes).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof that the SpanTree specification guarantees the type invariant TypeOK is always maintained. The proof shows that if the initial state satisfies TypeOK and every step of the Next action preserves TypeOK, then the temporal property []TypeOK holds under the given specification Spec. The proof assumes certain properties about the constants, such as Root being a node, every edge being a subset of Nodes of cardinality 2, and MaxCardinality being a natural number at least as large as the number of nodes. The proof is structured hierarchically and uses standard TLAPS proof commands.
desc_intent:
Specify a distributed algorithm that constructs and maintains a spanning tree rooted at a designated node in an undirected connected network. The model should represent a fixed set of nodes and undirected edges; each node knows its neighbors and can read and update only its own local state. The algorithm must establish, for every node, a parent pointer that points to a neighbor on a shortest (or strictly decreasing-distance) path toward the root and a nonnegative integer distance estimate from the root. Initially, the root must have distance zero and point to itself; other nodes may start with arbitrary nonnegative distances and parent pointers. The algorithm must permit local updates in which a node, after observing a neighbor with strictly smaller distance, atomically updates its parent to that neighbor and sets its distance to a value between the neighbor’s distance plus one and its previous distance minus one, ensuring progress toward the root without increasing any node’s distance.

Require formal properties to verify: safety — every parent pointer must always reference a valid node, every distance must always be a natural number, and every parent pointer must be a neighbor; invariants should ensure distances are consistent with parent links (parent distance < child distance); and liveness — eventually every node’s distance becomes finite and strictly decreases until it reflects its distance to the root, producing a stable spanning tree rooted at the designated root. Also require that the model forbids creation of cycles that contradict parent-to-root progress.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a small library of TLA+ operators for representing BNF-style grammars as languages over sequences of strings. It includes constructors for singleton-sequence languages, concatenation, union, one-or-more repetition, zero-or-more repetition, a grammar type as a function from strings to sets of string sequences, and a least-grammar operator defined with CHOOSE. The module has no constants, variables, actions, temporal formulas, assumptions, or PlusCal code.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of context-free grammars (BNF-style) that treats grammars as mappings from nonterminal names to sets of finite terminal/nonterminal symbol sequences, and specify operations and properties needed to reason about language generation and minimal grammars satisfying constraints.

The model should represent:
- A grammar as a finite map from nonterminal symbols to sets of right‑hand side sequences (each sequence is a finite list of symbols drawn from an alphabet that can include terminals and nonterminals).
- Concatenation, union, Kleene star, and one-or choices of languages built from sets of sequences, and an explicit empty sequence entity.

The specification must allow:
- Expressing the language generated by a nonterminal as the least set of terminal sequences closed under grammar derivations.
- Defining when a grammar satisfies a predicate (for example, generates or includes certain strings, excludes others, or conforms to syntactic restrictions).

Key correctness properties:
- The language operations (concatenation, union, Kleene star) must have the usual algebraic laws (associativity, distributivity where appropriate, identity elements).
- The generated language for a nonterminal must be the smallest set of terminal-only sequences that contains the direct productions and is closed under one-step derivation and finite composition.
- A minimality property: if a grammar meets a given predicate, there must exist a grammar that satisfies the predicate and is pointwise minimal (for each nonterminal its generated set is included in every other grammar satisfying the predicate).
- Definitions must be unambiguous about empty string inclusion and finiteness of right‑hand sides.

Include invariants and proof obligations to check closure properties and minimality, enabling formal verification that candidate grammars meet the stated requirements.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a formalization of differential equations and their solutions in TLA+. It defines what it means for a function to be a first derivative (IsFirstDeriv) and recursively defines higher-order derivatives (IsDeriv). The Integrate operator expresses the existence and construction of a solution to an n-th order ordinary differential equation with given initial values, using a choice function to select a suitable solution. The module uses real numbers and sequences, and encodes open intervals and neighborhoods for analysis, but does not specify a particular algorithm or system beyond these mathematical definitions.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of solving an ordinary differential equation (ODE) initial-value problem for a system of n first‑order equations derived from a higher‑order ODE. The model should describe a domain of real-valued, sufficiently smooth functions on an open interval around a closed time interval [a,b], with derivatives defined up to order n. It must capture the notion of an n‑th order ODE expressed as an equation D(t, y0, y1, …, yn) = 0 that holds pointwise for all times in an open neighborhood of [a,b], where y0 is the function value and yi is its i‑th derivative. The specification should require initial values for y0, y1, …, y(n−1) at time a and state the existence and uniqueness guarantee for a solution y0 (and its derivatives) on [a,b] that satisfies both the ODE and the initial conditions. Additionally, provide an operator that, given D, a, b and the initial values, returns the vector of values y0(b), y1(b), …, y(n−1)(b) at the endpoint b. Key correctness properties to assert: existence of a solution on an open neighborhood of [a,b]; compatibility of the solution with the initial values; the ODE is satisfied pointwise; the returned endpoint values equal the solution’s values at b; and derivatives up to order n exist and are consistent with the ODE.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines basic graph-theoretic structures and properties in TLA+. It models both directed and undirected graphs as records with node and edge fields, and provides predicates for checking if a structure is a directed or undirected graph. The module also defines subgraph constructions, paths, connectivity, and rooted trees, using set and sequence operations. No temporal properties or fault models are present; the focus is on static graph properties and relationships.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of finite graphs and common graph-theoretic constructs that can be used to verify algorithms that operate on graphs. The model should allow representing directed and undirected graphs as collections of nodes and edges (edges are ordered pairs of nodes), and should support formation of subgraphs (both directed and undirected). It must provide a notion of simple paths (finite, nonempty sequences of nodes where each consecutive pair is an edge) and predicates for reachability between two nodes via such a path.

Require definitions and properties for:
- Directed graphs and undirected graphs (undirected graphs must have symmetric edges).
- Directed and undirected subgraphs constrained to use only nodes and edges from a parent graph.
- Simple paths through a graph and a reachability predicate that holds iff there exists a path from one node to another.
- Strong connectivity: every node can reach every other node.
- Rooted trees (directed trees with a designated root) characterized by: the root has no incoming edge, each non-root node has exactly one incoming edge (uniqueness of parent), all nodes are reachable from the root, and there are no extra structural elements (i.e., edges only between nodes of the tree).

State key invariants and correctness properties to be checked:
- Subgraph containment preserves edge symmetry for undirected subgraphs.
- Path concatenation and reversal properties where applicable (reversing a path in an undirected graph yields a path).
- For a directed rooted tree, uniqueness of paths from any node to the root and absence of directed cycles.
- Strong connectivity implies existence of paths in both directions for any node pair.

The model should be parameterized by an explicit finite set of nodes and support automated checking of these properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models an inner sequential memory/request handling component with per-process register files, a per-process queue of issued operations, and a memory array. Processes can issue requests into free registers, receive responses for reads and writes, and internally remove completed operations from the head of their queue, updating memory for writes and checking consistency for reads. The spec asserts a data invariant over the register file, operation queues, and memory structure, and defines a temporal specification with weak fairness for response actions and queue removal so that enabled operations are not postponed forever.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent request-processing service with a finite set of clients (processes), a finite set of registers that each client can use to submit operations, and a shared memory that maps addresses to values. The service must accept client requests to read or write memory through per-client, per-register submission: a client can place at most one outstanding request per register, and new requests may be issued only into registers that are currently free. Each submitted request records the operation (read or write), the target address, and for writes the value to be stored.

Model the life cycle of a request: it is enqueued on a per-client FIFO queue when issued, then eventually processed by the service, which for reads must produce the value returned and mark the register free, and for writes must update memory and mark the register free. When a request completes, its queue entry is marked done and later removed from the head of the queue; removing a completed write must update shared memory to the write’s value, while removing a completed read must not change memory. The model should allow internal, asynchronous processing and eventual queue-head removal, and must ensure fairness so every issued request is eventually processed and removed.

Key correctness properties to prove:
- Type and structural invariants: per-client queues contain only valid request records and done markers; memory and request counts have the correct types.
- At-most-one-outstanding-per-register: a client-register pair never has more than one outstanding request.
- Read consistency: the value returned for a read corresponds to the memory value at the read’s address at the moment the read is responded to (or otherwise a clear consistency condition relating response to memory).
- Memory update atomicity: writes become visible exactly when the corresponding queue entry is removed from the head.
- Liveness: each issued request is eventually responded to and removed from the queue under the fairness assumptions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models an inner serial memory/register interface that tracks per-process sequences of issued operations, their responses, and a partial order over operation identifiers. It distinguishes read and write requests, records the source write that supplies a read value, and constrains the evolving order relation so that the completed history is serializable by extension to some total order consistent with program order and read-from constraints. The spec initializes empty operation queues, allows issuing requests, responding to reads and writes, and internal steps that only extend the order relation, and it verifies the system with a temporal specification using weak fairness for response actions and for internal ordering steps that eventually compare distinct operations.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent register service that accepts read and write requests from multiple clients, queues each client’s outstanding request in a per-client FIFO, and ensures that every completed operation observes a global serial ordering consistent with real-time and program order. The model should treat requests as operations that may be issued, completed, or remain pending in a client queue. Reads must return the value produced by some write to the same address (or an initial value), and writes must eventually become visible as the value read by later reads according to the serialization.

Requirements:
- Represent an unbounded set of clients and a finite set of registers addressed by some domain; each client may have at most one outstanding slot per register in its queue.
- Allow a client to issue a read or write to a register only when the corresponding per-client slot is free; issuing enqueues the request.
- Allow a write to complete (respond) and mark its queue entry done, freeing the client slot; allow a read to complete by selecting as its return source either an initial write or some previously issued write to the same address, record that source, deliver the corresponding value, and mark the read done.
- Maintain a partial order of operations that can be extended to a total order (serial order) satisfying: (1) the recorded partial order is a subset of the total order; (2) each client’s operations appear in the total order in program order; (3) each read’s chosen source precedes the read in the total order; if the read’s source is not the special initial source, then the source write must be ordered consistently with other writes to the same address (no cycles or contradictions).

Correctness properties to guarantee:
- Safety: every completed read returns a value from either the initial memory or some write to the same address, and this choice is consistent with a global sequential ordering that respects program order and the maintained partial order.
- Progress/Liveness: issued operations that are enabled for completion (reads or writes at the head of a client slot) must eventually be able to respond (weak fairness for completion actions).
- Invariant: per-client queue structure, register slot occupancy, and the relation between recorded request metadata and register state remain consistent throughout execution.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines the interface-level data types and type invariant for a register file. It models read requests, write requests, and free register values as record-shaped values over the constant sets Adr, Val, Proc, and Reg, and then combines them into larger sets used to constrain the state variable regFile. The specification does not define an initial condition, transition relation, or temporal behavior; instead, it provides structural type definitions and a state invariant asserting that regFile maps each process to a mapping from registers to register-interface values.
desc_intent:
Model a shared register file abstraction accessed by multiple concurrent clients. The system exposes a fixed set of named registers indexed by logical register identifiers and a fixed set of client processes. Each client may issue read or write requests targeted at a specific register and carrying a value. The register file must also allow registers to be marked as free/unused. Specify the types and allowed request forms, and require that the register file always maps each process to a full mapping from register identifiers to one of: a read request, a write request, or a free marker for that register.

Specify the allowed behaviors for operations that update the register file in response to client actions: issuing a read request, issuing a write request, and clearing or marking a register free. Ensure that clients can only produce well-formed requests and cannot create values or addresses outside the declared domains. Require that any update preserves the structural invariant that every process has an entry for every register and the entry is always one of the allowed request forms.

State safety properties: the register file must never contain malformed entries, and every transition must maintain the type invariant. State liveness goals: every valid client request should eventually be reflected in the register file (no permanent loss), and free markers can be re-used after a bounded time.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a serial memory specification by existentially quantifying over an initial memory state and two auxiliary values, then delegating the actual behavior to the `Spec` operator of an instantiated `InnerSerial` module. The initial memory is constrained to be a function from addresses to values, while `opQ` and `opOrder` are existentially chosen. The module is a thin wrapper around another module instance and does not itself define actions, fairness, assumptions, or proofs.
desc_intent: Model a single-writer, single-reader linearizable shared-memory register that serves read and write operations submitted by concurrent threads. The model should treat the memory as a mapping from addresses to values and must allow an initial memory state to be chosen arbitrarily. The system must accept a sequence (possibly unbounded) of operation invocations, each being either a write(address, value) or a read(address). Each operation has an invocation and a completion (return) event; operations may overlap in time. The model should nondeterministically schedule invocation and completion events but must record a total ordering of completed operations that respects real-time precedence (if an operation completes before another is invoked, it must appear earlier in the order). Reads must return the value of the most recent write to the same address according to that total order, or the initial value if no preceding write exists. Writes must update the logical memory for subsequent ordered operations. The specification should assert safety (linearizability/atomicity of operations with respect to the total order) and liveness assumptions only as needed for fairness of scheduling (do not require progress of specific threads unless explicitly assumed). Allow the possibility of concurrent overlapping operations but require that every completed operation’s observed result is consistent with some total sequential execution that respects real-time order and the initial memory.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of the main theorem from AsynchInterface.tla, which asserts that the specification Spec implies that the type invariant TypeInvariant is always maintained. The proof is structured hierarchically and uses TLAPS proof commands and references to definitions from the AsynchInterface module. The proof demonstrates type correctness for the asynchronous interface protocol, focusing on the preservation of the type invariant across the system's transitions. The module does not introduce new operators or variables, but rather proves properties about those defined in the extended module.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of an asynchronous single-message handshake interface between a sender and a receiver that communicate via a single shared data channel and explicit ready/acknowledge signals. The system should capture the asynchronous exchange of a value where the sender may present a value and raise a ready signal, the receiver may sample the value when ready and raise an acknowledge signal, and both sides may reset their signals to allow subsequent transfers. The model must allow the sender and receiver to act independently (i.e., not atomically synchronized) and to progress in any interleaving subject to the handshake protocol.

Require that the model enforce the protocol invariants: values transmitted are drawn from the declared value domain; ready and acknowledge signals are booleans; when the receiver accepts a value it reads the value currently presented by the sender only when the ready signal is set; the acknowledge is raised only in response to a valid ready and clears in a way that allows another transfer; the sender does not overwrite the presented value while an outstanding ready/acknowledge exchange is in progress except according to protocol rules. Specify liveness properties ensuring eventual completion of a handshake under fair scheduling assumptions: if the sender repeatedly offers a value, the receiver eventually accepts it, and vice versa under similar fairness. State a safety property that the type and handshake invariants hold in every reachable state. Do not constrain implementation details such as using specific variables or atomic steps.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of the main theorem from Channel.tla, which asserts that the specification Spec implies that the type invariant TypeInvariant is always maintained. The proof is structured hierarchically and uses TLAPS proof commands and backend solvers. The module does not define any new operators or variables, but instead proves a property about the system specified in the Channel module.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a simple asynchronous one-way communication channel between a single sender and a single receiver. The model must capture that the sender can place messages into the channel and the receiver can extract messages, with the channel buffering at most one message at a time (it is either empty or contains exactly one message). The system should allow the sender to attempt to send only when the channel is empty, and the receiver to attempt to receive only when the channel is nonempty. Message values come from a fixed finite set.

State the safety properties that must be guaranteed: the channel's content is always either empty or a valid message from the message set, and no action can create an invalid channel value. Also require type safety for any auxiliary state used to track send/receive steps. Specify liveness requirements optionally: if the sender repeatedly tries to send a particular message when the channel is empty, then eventually the receiver will receive it (or at least the channel will transition accordingly), and if the receiver repeatedly tries to receive while the channel contains a message, then it will eventually succeed. Require that the specification be amenable to mechanical proof: include an invariant that proves the channel's type correctness and is preserved by all actions. The model should not commit to any particular implementation technique beyond these semantics.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the InternalMemory specification, specifically proving that the type invariant (TypeInvariant) is preserved by the system. The proof addresses the fact that TypeInvariant alone is not inductive due to the next-state expression in Do(p) accessing fields of buf[p] that are only valid when buf[p] is in MReq. To resolve this, the invariant is strengthened with BufConsistent, which ensures that buf[p] has the correct type depending on the value of ctl[p]. The main theorem proved is that ISpec implies the temporal property []TypeInvariant, with the proof structured hierarchically and using TLAPS proof commands.
desc_intent: Model a shared-memory request/response service that mediates read and write requests from a fixed set of clients to a simple memory array. The model must include a finite set of client processes, a memory mapping from addresses to values, and per-client request state that can represent either no request, a pending memory request (address, operation, and write value if any), or a completed read result. The system must allow each client to: (1) issue a request that transitions its state to pending with a well-formed memory request; (2) have the mediator execute a single-step memory operation for a pending request, which either updates the memory for a write or returns the current memory value for a read and moves the client to a completed state; (3) receive an acknowledgement that resets the client to idle/ready without changing memory. Specify constraints ensuring that pending requests carry a valid address in the memory address domain and that values are from the allowed value domain. The correctness properties to prove are: (a) type safety/invariant preservation — every reachable state respects the domains/types of memory, addresses, client states, and per-client request contents; (b) that executing a write updates exactly the memory location named by the request and that executing a read returns a value currently stored at the requested address; and (c) that client state transitions preserve the consistency between a client’s control state and the permitted shape of its per-client request data (e.g., pending requests must contain full request tuples, idle/done states must not contain pending-request structure). Do not commit to an implementation style; express allowed atomic transitions and invariants abstractly.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies an internal memory component that interacts with an external memory interface through request and reply actions. It models a small protocol in which each process moves through control states "rdy", "busy", and "done", stores either requests or returned values in a per-process buffer, and updates the memory state on write requests while returning a memory value on reads. The specification defines an initial condition, a next-state relation over per-process actions, a temporal specification using a stuttering-closed box action, and proves that the type invariant always holds.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a simple shared-memory controller that serializes and services memory access requests from a fixed set of clients. The model should describe the abstract behavior of an internal memory component that accepts load and store requests from clients, performs the access to the memory, and returns results or acknowledgements, while ensuring the following functional requirements and safety properties.

- There is a fixed address space with values stored in memory. Clients may issue read or write requests targeted at addresses.
- A client may only have at most one outstanding request at a time; the controller accepts a new request from a client only when that client is ready to issue one.
- When a request is accepted, the controller records it in a per-client pending slot and marks the client as busy. Acceptance does not immediately change the logical memory contents.
- The controller performs requests atomically one client at a time: for a write, the memory is updated to the new value; for a read, the controller obtains the current memory value for the requested address.
- After performing the access, the controller places the response (read value or write acknowledgement) into the client’s response slot and marks the client as completed. The client may then consume the response and become ready again.
- The controller must preserve type invariants: memory is always a total mapping from addresses to values; per-client state belongs to the expected finite set of statuses (ready, busy, done); per-client slots hold either no request, a request object, or a value/response.
- All steps must keep memory and per-client state consistent: accepting a request should not change memory, performing a request updates memory only for writes, and responding should not alter memory or pending requests beyond clearing the response when consumed.

State the set of clients, addresses, and allowed request/response formats abstractly. Specify initial conditions, the three classes of transitions (accept request, perform request, return response), and assert invariants guaranteeing the single-outstanding-request property, memory consistency, and the type invariants described above. Also specify that the system evolves under repeated nondeterministic application of these transitions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a simple memory interface vocabulary rather than a full transition system. It defines the shape of memory requests as either read requests with an address or write requests with an address and value, and it defines a distinguished value NoVal chosen to lie outside the set Val. The file declares an interface variable and several constants for send/reply relations, initialization, and basic domains, but it does not define an Init, Next, Spec, or temporal correctness property. A commented-out assumption indicates the intended typing of Send and Reply as boolean-valued operators over process, data, and old/new memory-interface states, but because it is commented out it is not part of the active syntax.
desc_intent:
Model a concurrent memory-request interface between processors and a memory controller that mediates read and write requests. The system should allow multiple processors to issue asynchronous requests to the memory interface and receive replies; requests are either reads (with an address) or writes (with an address and a value). The interface must accept requests, forward them to the memory controller, and later produce corresponding replies to the originators. It must preserve request-response matching (each reply corresponds to a previously issued request and is delivered to the same processor), and ensure replies carry the correct data for reads and reflect acknowledgement semantics for writes.

Specify the state space, possible events, and allowed transitions abstractly (without fixing particular implementation strategies such as queues or locks). Include nondeterministic choice for ordering and timing of delivery, and model fresh tokens or identifiers when needed to avoid conflating concurrent requests. Ensure safety properties: no reply is produced for a request that was never accepted, no request is lost silently, and memory-read replies return values consistent with a sequentially consistent view of writes (i.e., some interleaving of write events determines read results). Specify liveness requirements: every accepted request is eventually replied to (unless the request is withdrawn), and the interface eventually accepts new requests when processors offer them. Allow parameters for the sets of processors, addresses, and values so the model is general.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a very small wrapper specification for a memory system by instantiating another module named InternalMemory with parameters mem, ctl, and buf. It extends MemoryInterface and defines an operator Inner that is an INSTANCE of InternalMemory, then defines Spec existentially over the instance parameters and refers to the instantiated specification ISpec. The file contains no state variables, no actions defined locally, and no explicit temporal properties beyond the top-level Spec expression that delegates behavior to the instantiated module.
desc_intent:
Specify a parameterized model of a memory component together with its controller and buffer, suitable for formal verification. The model should capture an abstract memory device that supports read and write operations, a control interface that issues commands and receives responses, and an intermediary buffer that decouples controller requests from memory execution. The system must allow concurrent requests, preserve request ordering where required, and tolerate temporary buffering without violating atomicity of individual reads and writes.

Requirements:
- Define the externally visible request/response semantics: reads return the latest committed value for an address, and writes become visible to subsequent reads according to the memory consistency rules.
- Model the buffer as a FIFO queue that can hold outstanding operations; the controller may enqueue requests and later dequeue responses. The buffer must not silently drop or duplicate operations.
- Capture the handshaking/control protocol between controller and buffer and between buffer and memory: command issuance, acknowledgement, completion, and error reporting.
- Allow the memory device to perform internal processing, including optional reordering or delays consistent with the chosen consistency model, but ensure correctness properties described below.

Key correctness properties to guarantee:
- Safety: no stale read returns a value older than permitted by the consistency semantics; no data corruption; no lost or duplicated writes.
- Liveness: any issued request is eventually either completed or deterministically failed under bounded-failure assumptions; the system avoids deadlock under normal operation.
- Invariants: buffer length bounds, preservation of request identifiers, and that completed operations reflect states in the memory that are reachable from the applied operations.

Parameterize the model so different memory consistency policies, buffer capacities, and failure/recovery behaviors can be explored.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a write-through cache system layered over an internal memory interface, with the original module instantiation expanded manually because the TLC version targeted by the file could not handle INSTANCE. The system has per-processor control state, request buffers, a per-processor cache, and a memory request queue that serializes cache misses and writes to memory. It specifies initialization, state-transition actions for requests, reads, writes, queue processing, and eviction, and it asserts temporal safety properties that the type invariant and cache coherence hold under the main specification.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent write-through cache system with multiple processors issuing read and write requests to a shared memory through a simple cache and a bounded request queue. Model processors that repeatedly become ready, issue memory requests (reads or writes), wait for responses, and proceed when replies arrive. The system should include: a main memory that holds values per address; per-processor small caches that may hold a value or indicate no value; per-processor request buffers that hold the outstanding request or the returned value; per-processor control state with at least ready, busy, waiting, and done states; and a FIFO memory-queue of pending memory operations with a fixed maximum length.

The model must allow:
- A processor to send a request when ready without changing main memory immediately.
- Reads to return cached values when present; on a cache miss, a read request must be enqueued if there is space and the processor moves to waiting.
- Writes to update caches of processors that either issued the write or already have the address cached, enqueue the write to the memory queue if space, and clear the issuing processor's buffer.
- The memory queue to be processed by a memory controller that dequeues operations in order: applying writes to main memory and answering reads by updating the requesting processor's cache with the value that main memory would have after earlier queued writes.
- Eviction of individual cache lines without affecting other state.

Require safety properties:
- Type invariants: all variables always lie in their declared domains (memory, buffers, caches, control states, and queue length).
- Coherence: if two processors both have a value for the same address in their caches (not "no value"), those cached values must be equal.
- The queue and memory semantics must ensure reads that are served from the queue observe effects of earlier queued writes to the same address.

Also require liveness-friendly behavior sufficient to reason about invariants (e.g., transitions exist for making progress) but do not mandate fairness of scheduling in the specification.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a write-through cache layered over an internal memory interface. It describes per-processor cache behavior, request and response handling, read misses, writes that update both cache state and a memory queue, queued memory processing, and eviction. The spec verifies a type invariant and a cache coherence property stating that if two cached values for the same address are both valid, then they are equal; it also proves refinement or conformance to an instantiated Memory specification.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of a multicore write-through cache system with a global memory request queue and a single shared backing store. The model should represent multiple processors issuing read and write memory operations, each processor having a small private cache for addresses and a per-processor control state and request buffer. The system must queue outstanding memory requests up to a fixed queue length and process them in FIFO order to the backing store. Reads that miss in a processor’s cache should enqueue a read request and later be served from the backing store, updating that processor’s cache. Writes should be propagated (written through) to the backing store by enqueuing a write request; when a write is enqueued, cached copy values visible to other processors must be updated so caches remain coherent. Evictions may remove entries from a processor’s cache but must not occur while that processor is blocked waiting for a response to a request for the same address. The backing store’s visible state should evolve as if queued writes are applied in order; reads served from the queue should reflect the effect of prior queued writes to the same address. The specification must guarantee type-safety of all state components, the preservation of cache coherence (if two caches both hold a value for the same address they agree), FIFO semantics of the memory request queue, and that every issued request eventually receives a response (no permanent starvation), assuming the queue can make progress.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a binary hour clock in which the variable bits represents an array of binary digits encoding an hour value. The module defines a helper operator to interpret a bit array as a numeric value, then relates that interpreted value to an hour variable through a temporal invariant stating that the hour always equals the value computed from bits. The top-level formula existentially quantifies an hour variable and combines that relation with the imported HourClock instance's HC property, so the design connects a binary representation of hours to an abstract hour-clock specification.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a simple digital hour display that represents an hour value using a fixed-size array of binary digit signals. The model should treat the display as an interface that exposes a collection of binary outputs, each output holding either 0 or 1, and should relate those bit outputs to the logical hour value they encode. The system to model is the encoding and continuous correctness relation between the bit-pattern and a valid hour (0–23 or a specified hour domain). The model must capture:

- The mapping from a finite indexed set of bit signals to a numeric value, interpreting each bit as a binary-weighted digit (least significant bit at index 0).
- The constraint that the interpreted numeric value is always a member of the legal hour range; if the bit pattern does not encode a valid hour, that state must be considered illegal or flagged.
- The invariant that the bit outputs must continuously reflect some legal hour value (i.e., at all observable times the numeric decoding of the bits equals a valid hour).
- An abstract specification of an external hour source: the model should support asserting existence of an intended hour value that the bit array implements, without prescribing how the bits are produced or updated.
- Properties to verify: (1) safety — the decoded value never leaves the valid hour range, and (2) functional consistency — there exists an hour value that the bit array encodes and maintains.

Do not prescribe update algorithms for the bits; specify only the relation between bit signals and the hour they represent and the invariants required to hold at all times.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a refinement relationship between two channel instances, a low-level bit channel and a high-level channel carrying values in 1..12. The inner module introduces a state variable bitsSent and accumulates up to three transmitted bits, converting a completed bit sequence into a natural number with BitSeqToNat and forwarding it on the high-level channel. It also models an error behavior in which the low-level channel changes unexpectedly while no send or receive is occurring, forcing the high-level channel state to ErrorVal; the temporal properties define the inner behavior and then existentially hide bitsSent to obtain the overall refinement formula IR.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a two-layer communication abstraction: a low-level unreliable bit channel and a high-level reliable packet channel that the low-level layer implements by grouping bits into multi-bit data units. The model should describe processes that send and receive information through the low-level channel as sequences of bits, accumulate bits into fixed-size groups, and deliver an encoded multi-bit value on the high-level channel when enough bits have been transmitted. The system must also allow the low-level channel to nondeterministically exhibit an error that corrupts its state without performing a send or receive step, and when such an error occurs the high-level channel must be driven to a designated error value.

Requirements:
- Model the low-level communication primitive that can send a single bit or perform a receive operation; multiple low-level operations compose to represent one high-level data transmission.
- Define the encoding from a sequence of bits into a numeric data value and require that exactly when the requisite number of bits have been sent in order, the corresponding high-level data value becomes available on the high-level channel.
- Permit the low-level channel to change arbitrarily only via a special error transition; when such an error transition occurs, ensure the high-level channel is set to a special error value and no low-level send/receive action is recorded for that transition.
- Ensure safety: high-level data values must only appear as the result of completing the correct bit sequence; no spurious high-level value may appear. Ensure liveness: if bits continue to be sent without error, the model must eventually produce the corresponding high-level value after the required count of bits.
- Allow multiple independent instances of the bit-accumulation process (parameterized by the bits already sent) to run concurrently, and specify the initial conditions for both channels and accumulators.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of the main theorem from Channel.tla, which asserts that the specification Spec implies that the type invariant TypeInvariant is always maintained. The proof is structured hierarchically and uses TLAPS proof commands and backend solvers. The system being modeled is a channel, and the proof demonstrates type correctness under the specified actions and invariants.
desc_intent: Specify a formal TLA+ model of a simple reliable asynchronous channel used for sending and receiving messages between two processes. The system should allow a sender to post messages into the channel and a receiver to take messages out. Messages may be of arbitrary values drawn from a fixed universe. The channel must allow at most one in-flight message at a time (i.e., either empty or holding a single message).
