The sender may attempt to send only when the channel is empty; the receiver may attempt to receive only when the channel holds a message. The model should capture nondeterministic interleaving of send and receive actions and allow send or receive attempts to be enabled or disabled independently. Specify an initial state with an empty channel. State the safety properties: the channel content is always either empty or a single value from the message universe, and the receiver never obtains a value that was not previously sent. State the liveness expectations informally: if a send is enabled and remains enabled, eventually the message can be placed into the channel; if a receive is enabled and remains enabled, eventually the receiver can remove the message. Provide an invariant expressing the type/sanity condition on channel contents and a temporal specification combining initialization and the allowed send/receive steps. The model should be suitable for mechanical verification of the invariant.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple two-phase handshake communication channel using a single variable 'chan' that is a record with fields 'val', 'rdy', and 'ack'. The channel transmits values from the set 'Data' using a protocol where the sender updates the value and toggles the ready bit, and the receiver acknowledges by toggling the ack bit. The system ensures that the channel variable always satisfies the type invariant, and the main temporal property asserts that this invariant is always maintained throughout execution. The model is basic, with no explicit fault model or fairness conditions, and verifies safety via a single theorem.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of an unreliable asynchronous single-slot message channel that implements a simple two-way handshake for one-way data transfer. The system has a sender and a receiver that communicate through a single shared message cell holding one data value and two one-bit control signals. The sender should place a data value into the cell and toggle its send signal only when the channel is ready (i.e., when the send and acknowledge signals match). The receiver should observe a mismatch between the two control bits to detect a new message, read the data without modifying it, and toggle the acknowledge bit to indicate receipt. The channel must preserve the data value until the receiver has acknowledged it; the sender must not overwrite an unacknowledged message. The model should allow arbitrary interleaving of sender and receiver steps and nondeterministic selection of data values from a fixed data domain. Specify the initial condition that control bits are synchronized (no outstanding message) and the safety properties: control bits remain booleans, the sender only writes when allowed, the receiver only acknowledges on a detected message, and data is not lost or corrupted between write and acknowledgement. Also specify liveness properties ensuring that if the sender continuously attempts to send a fixed value, eventually the receiver will acknowledge it, and that the receiver does not starve indefinitely when messages are pending.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a composite FIFO-style communication system built by connecting a sender, an inner buffer, and a receiver through channel interfaces. The top-level module instantiates a Channel module twice, once for the input side and once for the output side, and also defines an inner module that represents a queue-based buffer with receive and send actions over those channels. The specification asserts structural channel constraints on the records in and out, constrains acknowledgement and ready fields to match, and composes the Sender, existentially quantified Buffer, and Receiver behaviors into the overall Spec; it does not include explicit fault modeling or proof scripts.
desc_intent:
Specify a formally precise model of a composed message-passing pipeline with three logical components: a sender, an intermediate FIFO buffer of unbounded (or parameterized) capacity, and a receiver, connected by two asynchronous handshake channels. The system must represent channels as pairs of handshake endpoints that support atomic send and receive handshake operations (rdy/ack style), so that a send on one side completes only when the corresponding receive occurs on the other side. The sender nondeterministically produces messages drawn from a fixed domain and injects them into the first channel. The buffer accepts incoming messages from the first channel, enqueues them, and dequeues to send to the second channel; the buffer must preserve FIFO ordering and not lose or duplicate messages. The receiver accepts messages from the second channel at its own pace. The model should allow channels and endpoints to be in arbitrary ready/acknowledge boolean states, but enforce that handshakes are matched correctly.

Specify safety properties: (1) message-order preservation between sender output sequence and receiver input sequence (FIFO), (2) no message loss or duplication (every message sent is eventually received at most once), and (3) channel handshake correctness (ack/rdy consistency and no mismatched handshakes). Specify liveness properties: every message submitted by the sender is eventually delivered to the receiver assuming fair execution of the buffer and channels, and the system does not deadlock under fair scheduling. Allow parameterization of the message domain and buffer capacity for verification experiments.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of a theorem about the HourClock specification, specifically that the invariant HCini is preserved by the system. The proof shows that if HC holds, then HCini holds always, using the temporal property []HCini. The proof is structured hierarchically and references definitions from the HourClock module, with fairness and next-state actions handled via [HCnxt]_hr.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a simple hour clock that cycles through a fixed set of hour values and is initialized to a valid hour. The model should describe a single-state variable that holds an hour value drawn from a finite, ordered set representing the hours on the clock (for example 0..11 for a 12-hour clock). The model must allow transitions that advance the hour deterministically to the next hour, wrapping from the maximal hour back to the minimal hour. Include an initialization condition that constrains the state variable to be within the allowed hour set.

Formalize the behavior as an infinite-state execution: every step must either perform the deterministic hour-advance transition or stutter (no change). The specification must assert that the initialization predicate is an invariant: any state reachable from an initial state via any number of allowed transitions must satisfy the initialization predicate (i.e., the hour value always remains within the allowed set). Also assert that the system preserves the property that the hour variable always takes a value in the finite hour set and that advancement is the only non-stuttering action. Do not prescribe implementation details; focus on the state space, allowed transitions, initialization constraints, and the invariants that must hold for all reachable states.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple 12-hour clock. The state variable 'hr' represents the current hour, which ranges from 1 to 12. The initial predicate HCini ensures that the hour starts within this range, and the next-state action HCnxt increments the hour by 1 unless it is 12, in which case it wraps around to 1. The temporal property HC asserts that the system starts in a valid state and always follows the hour update rule. The theorem verifies that the invariant HCini is always maintained.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a simple 12-hour clock that advances its hour reading once on each discrete step and wraps from 12 back to 1. The model should treat the hour as a single state component ranging over the integers 1..12. The system must always start in a valid hour value and, on every transition, either increment the hour by one when it is less than 12, or reset it to 1 when it is currently 12. No other changes to state are permitted. The specification should make clear that steps are atomic, deterministic, and repeated indefinitely.

State the safety properties that must hold: the hour value is always within the set {1,2,...,12} (invariant), and every transition conforms to the specified increment-or-wrap rule (transition correctness). Also state the liveness expectation that the clock continues to advance forever (no deadlock): from any reachable state there is always a next transition. Finally, include a proof obligation that if the initial state satisfies the valid-hour predicate, then it continues to satisfy it for all future steps (i.e., initial validity implies invariant holds globally).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the InternalMemory specification, specifically proving that the type invariant (TypeInvariant) is preserved by the system. The proof addresses the fact that TypeInvariant alone is not inductive due to the next-state expression in Do(p) accessing fields of buf[p] that are only valid when buf[p] is in MReq. To resolve this, the invariant is strengthened with BufConsistent, which ensures that buf[p] has the correct type depending on the value of ctl[p]. The main theorem proved is that ISpec implies []TypeInvariant, with the proof structured hierarchically and using TLAPS proof commands.
desc_intent:
Model a simple concurrent request/response memory-interaction protocol for a fixed set of clients (processes) that communicate with a shared memory. The model should capture clients issuing memory requests, the memory performing reads and writes, and clients receiving responses. Specify the allowed states, transitions, and the invariant properties the system must maintain; do not prescribe an implementation.

Requirements:
- Processes can be in one of three control states: ready to issue a request, busy while a request is outstanding, or done waiting to be acknowledged. While ready or done, a process' local buffer may hold either no value or a data value; while busy, the buffer must encode a well-formed memory request (an address, an operation kind — read or write — and, for writes, a value).
- A request transition moves a ready process to busy and initializes its buffer with a valid memory request.
- A memory transition executes a busy process' request: for a read, it returns the value currently stored at the requested address into the process' buffer and moves the process to done without changing memory; for a write, it updates the memory at the requested address with the provided value and moves the process to done with its buffer cleared to a valid “no value” or value encoding.
- A response transition moves a done process back to ready without changing memory or other processes' buffers.
- The model must ensure type safety: memory is always a mapping from addresses to values; process buffers are always in the appropriate domain according to the process control state; request fields (address, operation, value) are always in their expected sets.
- Prove that these type and buffer-consistency invariants hold globally for all reachable states (i.e., are inductive and preserved by every transition), and therefore always true under the system’s specification.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies an internal memory system that implements the MemoryInterface. The system models a set of processes interacting with a shared memory, where each process can issue memory requests, perform operations, and receive responses. The state is tracked by variables for memory contents, control state per process, and a buffer per process. The algorithm ensures that memory operations are performed atomically and that the control and buffer variables are updated consistently. The specification includes a type invariant to ensure variables remain within their intended domains, and a temporal property stating that the type invariant is always preserved by the system. The system interacts with an abstract memory interface via Send and Reply actions, and the fairness and stuttering are handled via the temporal box operator.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent internal memory controller that mediates read and write requests from a fixed set of clients (processors) to a shared memory array. The model should capture clients issuing requests, the controller performing requested operations on the memory, and the controller replying to clients, while separating client-visible request/response interactions from an internal memory interface used to communicate with lower-level memory machinery.

Requirements:
- The system has a finite set of addresses and values. Clients may issue either a read or write request for a particular address (writes include a value).
- Clients may be in one of a small number of states (ready to issue, request in progress, awaiting or ready to receive response). Transitions must follow a request → perform → respond pattern for each request.
- When a client issues a request, the controller must record that request and mark the client as busy; the request should be delivered to the internal memory interface (abstracted as an interaction that may update internal memory state).
- When performing a write, the shared memory array must be updated atomically at the addressed location. When performing a read, the response must contain the value read from memory at the time of service.
- After servicing, the controller must provide a reply to the originating client and return the client to the ready state.
- The model must treat the internal memory interface as an abstract component that can change state when requests are sent or replies produced; the high-level controller must not violate the interface contract.
Key correctness properties to guarantee:
- Type safety / invariants: memory is always a total mapping from addresses to values; client controller state and per-client buffers always have values from their declared domains.
- Safety of memory updates: writes update only the targeted address atomically; reads return the correct value as of service time.
- Progress: a well-formed request should eventually be performed and replied to (no permanent starvation of a queued, sent request), modulo fairness assumptions about the internal memory interface.
- No lost or spurious replies: every reply corresponds to a previously issued request and each issued request gets at most one reply.
Describe nondeterminism in ordering of concurrently issued requests, but require that each client’s request lifecycle preserves these properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a joint-action memory system by composing two hidden internal components: an environment component and a memory component. The environment tracks a readiness map and can either send memory requests or receive replies, while the memory component accepts requests into per-process buffers, updates control state, and delegates additional behavior to imported operators such as Do and Rsp from an extended module. The top-level specification existentially hides the internal variables of both components and asserts the conjunction of their temporal behaviors, with each component described by an initialization predicate and a stuttering-closed next-state formula.
desc_intent: Specify a concurrent client–memory interface with a separate environment component that models request/response readiness and a memory component that services requests and produces replies. The system should represent multiple processes (clients) that may issue memory requests asynchronously to a shared memory and receive responses or no-op replies. It must permit each client to be in a ready or not-ready state for sending a request; when ready, a client may send a request that becomes buffered and marks the client as busy, and later the memory component must perform the requested operation and produce a response. The environment must also be able to produce spontaneous replies (including an explicit "no value") to a client and restore the client's ready state. The model should allow interleaving of environment-driven request/response events and internal memory actions, and should ensure progress: whenever some component is enabled, the system can make a step (nonblocking fairness at the component level). Key correctness properties to guarantee: safety (requests are buffered atomically when sent, buffer contents reflect the last sent request per client, and clients marked busy do not overwrite their buffer until freed); response matching (every response corresponds to a previously issued request or is explicitly allowed to be a NoVal reply); and liveness (requests eventually receive a response under fair scheduling assumptions). The specification should abstract away implementation details and focus on these behaviors and invariants for all clients.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of the main theorem from Channel.tla, specifically that the specification Spec implies that the type invariant TypeInvariant is always maintained. The proof is structured hierarchically and uses TLAPS proof commands and backend solvers. The module does not define any new operators or variables, but instead focuses on proving the temporal property using the definitions from the Channel module.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of an asynchronous lossy FIFO channel used to transmit messages between a single sender and a single receiver. The model should describe nondeterministic communication over the channel: the sender may enqueue messages to send, the channel may nondeterministically drop messages, and the receiver may dequeue and accept messages. The system should allow unbounded attempts to send and receive, but the channel's buffer is modeled abstractly as a sequence of messages.

Require the following safety and liveness properties to be specified and proved:

- Type safety: every state must satisfy invariants that restrict the types of the sender's outgoing message, the receiver's last-delivered message, and the channel contents (e.g., channel is a sequence of well-formed messages).

- Message preservation property under reliable delivery: if the channel nondeterminism is restricted so that messages are not lost, then every message sent is eventually received in FIFO order.

- Loss-tolerant safety: even when drops are allowed, the receiver must only ever accept messages that were sent (no spurious messages) and must never violate FIFO order among delivered messages.

- Progress: when a message is present in the channel and the receiver is enabled, the receiver can eventually remove it (unless it is dropped first), and the sender can always attempt to send another message.

Also require a proof obligation that the type safety invariant holds initially and is preserved by all transitions of the system. Do not prescribe specific implementation actions; describe only the allowed behaviors and the invariants and liveness guarantees the specification must ensure.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a simple one-place handshake channel with a data field and two control bits, rdy and ack. The sender may send a value d only when chan.rdy = chan.ack, and doing so stores d in chan.val and flips the ready bit; the receiver may receive only when chan.rdy # chan.ack, and doing so flips the acknowledge bit. The specification defines initialization, the next-state relation, and a temporal behavior Spec asserting Init and always Next over chan, and it proves that the type invariant is always maintained.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of a single-message synchronous channel that implements reliable handshaking between a sender and a receiver using a two-state ready/ack protocol and a data payload drawn from a fixed finite set. The model should capture an initially empty channel in a well-typed state, allow a sender to place a new data value into the channel only when the sender and receiver are synchronized (i.e., when ready equals ack), and allow a receiver to acknowledge and consume a pending message only when the sender has signaled a new message (i.e., when ready differs from ack). The channel must carry exactly one data value plus two control bits representing the ready and acknowledge signals. The specification should treat the data set as a constant parameter. It must ensure safety properties: the channel state always respects the type and range constraints, the sender never overwrites an unacknowledged message, and the receiver never acknowledges when there is no pending message. It must also ensure progress liveness: whenever the sender repeatedly attempts to send a value and the receiver eventually responds, the handshake completes (the ready and ack bits alternate to transfer each message). State invariants and transition relations should be written abstractly so they can be checked for invariant preservation and eventual message transfer, without prescribing implementation details or process scheduling.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification defines a top-level FIFO module that declares a constant Message and two variables, in and out. It defines Inner(q) as an instance of InnerFIFO, and defines Spec as \EE q : Inner(q)!Spec. No assumptions, theorems, actions, temporal operators with outermost [] or <>, fairness conditions, proofs, or PlusCal constructs are defined in this file.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a single-producer, single-consumer FIFO buffer that transports messages from a sender to a receiver. The model should allow an unbounded (or optionally bounded by a parameter) sequence of messages to be enqueued by the producer and dequeued by the consumer while preserving arrival order. The system must present operations for the producer to send a message and for the consumer to receive a message; these operations may be concurrent but must respect FIFO semantics.

State the safety properties: messages are never duplicated or lost while in the buffer, the relative order of messages delivered to the consumer matches the order they were enqueued by the producer, and the consumer never receives a message that was never sent. If bounded capacity is used, the producer must be blocked or prevented from enqueueing when the buffer is full.

State the liveness properties: every message enqueued by the producer is eventually delivered to the consumer (unless the producer or consumer halts), and if the producer continues to enqueue and the consumer continues to dequeue, progress continues without starvation. Allow specification of fairness constraints to ensure progress. Also include an invariant representing buffer contents and an assertion that the sequence of delivered messages is a subsequence of the sequence of sent messages preserving order.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies an inner FIFO buffer system connecting an input channel and an output channel, with an internal queue q storing messages in transit. The module is a TLC-oriented version of another specification that originally used INSTANCE statements; here the imported channel behavior is expanded manually into prefixed operators for the input and output channels. It models channel handshaking with rdy/ack bits, queueing of received input messages, forwarding from the head of the queue to the output channel, and proves that the specification implies a type invariant stating that both channels have the expected record structure and that q is a sequence of Message values.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a single-element FIFO buffer implemented with two asynchronous rendezvous-style channels: an input channel that receives messages from a producer, and an output channel that delivers messages to a consumer. The model should treat messages as elements drawn from an abstract set and should not prescribe a particular encoding.

The system must allow the producer to place messages onto the input channel at arbitrary times, and allow the consumer to accept messages from the output channel at arbitrary times. The buffer must decouple producer and consumer: when the producer delivers a message to the input channel, the buffer may later accept it into its internal queue; when the buffer has an element available, it may place the element onto the output channel for the consumer to take. The channels should behave like single-slot handshake channels with separate ready and acknowledge signals, so sends and receives are synchronized by matching ready/ack states rather than atomic transfers.

Specify the initial states, the legal atomic transitions for the producer send, channel receive and send handshakes, buffer enqueue and dequeue operations, and the interleaving semantics. Require preservation of typing invariants (channels' fields and the queue contents), absence of message loss and creation (every message in the buffer or delivered on the output must have been previously sent by the producer), and FIFO order (messages are delivered to the consumer in the same order sent by the producer). Also require that the channels’ handshake protocol preserves mutual consistency (ready and ack alternate correctly) and that the model guarantees safety properties: no unauthorized state updates, and the queue length is always a finite sequence of messages.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the FIFO queue specification defined in the InnerFIFO module. The main theorem proved is that the specification Spec implies that the type invariant TypeInvariant is always maintained, i.e., Spec => []TypeInvariant. The proof is structured hierarchically and relies on the definitions and invariants from the InnerFIFO module, as well as proof automation from TLAPS. The proof demonstrates that the initial state satisfies the invariant and that the invariant is preserved by all possible transitions, including Send, Receive, and stuttering steps.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a two-stage FIFO messaging pipeline consisting of an input channel, an internal buffer, and an output channel. The system accepts asynchronous send events from an external sender into the input channel and asynchronous receive events by an external receiver from the output channel. The internal buffer holds messages in FIFO order between the channels. Model the following abstract behavior and correctness requirements, without prescribing implementation details:

- The system maintains three abstract components: the input endpoint (accepts incoming messages), an internal bounded/unbounded buffer that stores a sequence of messages, and the output endpoint (delivers messages). Messages are drawn from a fixed type Message.
- The input endpoint must allow messages to be enqueued into the buffer (possibly via an input channel abstraction). The output endpoint must allow messages to be dequeued from the buffer and delivered to the receiver (possibly via an output channel abstraction).
- The system must permit four kinds of atomic steps: sending into the input endpoint, receiving from the input channel into the buffer, sending from the buffer into the output channel, and receiving from the output endpoint. Also allow stuttering (no-op) steps.
- Safety property: types are preserved — at all times channels and buffer contain only values of the Message type and the buffer is a sequence (i.e., well-formed). The FIFO ordering of messages must be preserved: messages are delivered in the same order they were accepted.
- Liveness desiderata (optional to include): any message accepted into the input endpoint should eventually be delivered to the output endpoint, assuming the environment does not permanently block sends/receives.

Provide invariants expressing type correctness and FIFO semantics and prove (or set up to prove) that they hold inductively from the initial state and are preserved by each atomic step.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies an inner FIFO buffer connected between an input channel and an output channel. It instantiates a separate Channel module twice, once for the input channel and once for the output channel, and models an internal queue q that stores messages received from the input until they are forwarded on the output in first-in first-out order. The specification defines initialization, message sending into the input channel, buffering of received input messages, forwarding from the buffer to the output, receipt from the output channel, a next-state relation over these actions, and a temporal specification asserting that all behaviors start in Init and evolve by Next with stuttering allowed. It also states a theorem that Spec implies the invariant that both channel instances satisfy their type invariants and that q is a sequence of Message values.
desc_intent:
Model a reliable asynchronous FIFO buffer that connects a producer and a consumer through two unidirectional channels. The system must allow a producer to asynchronously send arbitrary messages into an input channel, the buffer to accept messages from that input channel and enqueue them at the tail, and a dispatcher to dequeue messages from the head and send them on an output channel for the consumer to receive. Channels should behave as abstract asynchronous message queues: sends append a message to a channel and receives remove a message from a channel; the buffer must interact only via these channel interfaces. The buffer itself must maintain an internal finite sequence representing queued messages and must not invent or lose messages: every message accepted from the input channel eventually appears on the output channel in the same relative order (FIFO). The system must permit interleaving of producer sends, buffer receives/sends, and consumer receives, and must be safe under nondeterministic scheduling.

Specify the initial condition, valid steps, and a temporal specification that enforces the buffer’s liveness: any message placed by the producer into the input channel is eventually accepted and delivered to the consumer, provided the consumer continues to receive. State invariants ensuring type-correctness of channels and that the internal queue always contains only messages of the allowed message type, and prove that these invariants are preserved.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the main invariant theorem of the HourClock specification. It proves that if the HourClock system (HC) holds initially, then the invariant HCini is always maintained throughout the execution. The proof is structured hierarchically and uses TLAPS proof commands and backend solvers. The design is focused on formal verification of the invariant property, leveraging the temporal logic of actions and proof steps.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a simple discrete-time hour clock module and prove a basic invariant using temporal logic.

Model a clock that cyclically advances an hour value in a fixed finite range (e.g., 0..H-1 for some positive integer H). The system operates in discrete steps: on each step the clock either advances to the next hour value (wrapping from H-1 to 0) or remains unchanged. The model should permit nondeterministic interleaving of steps but ensure time-progress is represented by repeated application of the advance-or-stay step.

State the initial condition: the hour value starts within the allowed range. Specify the transition relation that captures the allowed step (advance by one modulo H, or stay the same).

Specify the safety property to be proved: the hour value always remains within the allowed range (an invariant). Formulate this as an invariant property and show that it is preserved by the transition relation and holds initially, so it is true globally (always). Also state the liveness expectation that the system exhibits repeated transitions (temporal behavior) though no particular fairness constraints are required beyond enabling the basic temporal reasoning for invariants. The specification should be suitable for mechanized proof in a temporal logic prover.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of a theorem about the HourClock specification, specifically that the invariant HCini is preserved by the system. The proof shows that if HC holds, then HCini holds always, using the temporal property []HCini. The proof is structured hierarchically and references definitions from the HourClock module, with fairness and next-state actions handled via [HCnxt]_hr.
desc_intent:
Model a simple hour-of-day clock system that maintains an integer hour value in the range 0..23 and repeatedly advances time by one hour on each tick, wrapping from 23 to 0. The model should allow an initial state in which the hour is any valid value in 0..23. The system must offer an atomic transition that represents a clock tick and updates the hour deterministically to (hour + 1) mod 24. It must permit stuttering steps (no change) to represent idling, but the tick transition must be the only action that changes the hour.

Specify the correctness properties to verify:

- Safety: the hour value is always within 0..23 in every reachable state.
- Invariance of initial condition: any behavior starting from a state satisfying the initial-hour predicate remains such that the initial-hour predicate is preserved as an invariant (i.e., the initial-hour condition implies an invariant property that holds in all future states).
- Liveness (optional): from any state, eventual occurrence of a tick is possible (the clock does not permanently deadlock), or, alternatively, fairness assumptions ensuring eventual progress of the tick action.

Avoid committing to any concrete implementation structure; describe only the state space, the allowed state transitions, the initial-state constraint, and the properties to prove (safety invariant and the chosen liveness/fairness requirement).

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple 12-hour clock. The state variable 'hr' represents the current hour and is constrained to be in the range 1 to 12. The initial predicate HCini ensures that the hour starts within this range. The next-state action HCnxt increments the hour by 1 unless it is 12, in which case it wraps around to 1. The temporal property HC asserts that the system starts in a valid state and always takes valid next steps. The theorem proves that the invariant HCini is always maintained.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a simple 12-hour clock that advances the hour by one on each tick and wraps from 12 back to 1. The model should represent the hour as an integer in the range 1..12 and include an initial condition that the hour is always within this range. The only state change allowed is a tick that increments the hour by one unless it is currently 12, in which case it becomes 1. The specification must capture infinite execution of ticks (i.e., the tick step can occur repeatedly).

Require the following correctness properties:
- Invariance: at all times the hour value must remain within 1..12.
- Determinism of the tick step: for any state, the next hour value is uniquely determined by the current hour (no nondeterministic choices).
- Liveness/Progress: from any state, it must be possible to perform another tick (no deadlock).
- Cycle completeness: starting from any valid hour and after some number of ticks, every hour in 1..12 is reachable (the model should demonstrate that the ticking produces the full 12-state cycle).

Express these properties as temporal formulas suitable for model checking.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the InternalMemory specification, specifically proving that the type invariant (TypeInvariant) is preserved by the system under the ISpec specification. The proof addresses the fact that TypeInvariant alone is not inductive due to the next-state expression in Do(p) accessing fields of buf[p] that are only valid when buf[p] is in MReq. To resolve this, the invariant is strengthened with BufConsistent, which ensures that buf[p] has the correct type depending on the value of ctl[p]. The proof is structured hierarchically and demonstrates that the strengthened invariant (Inv) is inductive, and thus TypeInvariant is always preserved.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent request/response memory-access controller for a fixed set of clients and a shared memory. The system should allow each client to issue a memory request that is either a read or a write to a concrete address, and then later receive a response. The model must include per-client control states with a simple 3-state protocol (ready -> busy -> done -> ready) and a per-client request buffer that, while the client is busy, holds a structured memory request (address, operation, and write value for writes) and otherwise holds either a value read or a distinguished "no-value". The shared memory is a finite map from addresses to values.

The specification must enforce these requirements:
- Safety: Only well-typed values are ever stored in the buffers and memory: addresses come from the address domain and values come from the value domain; while a client is busy its buffer must represent a valid memory request; while ready or done the buffer must be either a valid value or the no-value marker.
- Atomicity of client steps: a request action atomically moves a client from ready to busy and installs a well-formed request; a service action executes a single memory operation for one busy client: on read, it returns the memory value into the client buffer and moves the client to done; on write, it updates memory at the requested address and moves the client to done, storing an appropriate value indicator in the buffer; a response action returns a done client to ready without changing memory.
- Invariant requirement: prove that the typing conditions and the buffer consistency relation (which links buffer contents to the client's control state) hold initially and are preserved by every action (i.e., they are inductive invariants under the system's transition relation).

Do not commit to a particular implementation technique (e.g., locking, interleaving order beyond single-client atomic steps); instead, state the abstract operations and the invariants that must be established and proved.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies an internal memory system that implements the MemoryInterface. The system models a set of processes interacting with a shared memory, where each process can issue memory requests, perform operations, and receive responses. The state is tracked by variables for memory contents (mem), control state per process (ctl), and per-process buffers (buf). The algorithm models request, operation, and response phases for each process, with explicit state transitions and primed variables. The main temporal property ISpec asserts that starting from IInit, the system repeatedly executes INext steps, and a theorem proves that the type invariant is always maintained. The design uses explicit state transitions and does not include a fault model.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of a simple internal memory controller that mediates memory access requests from a fixed set of clients. The model should describe the abstract state of the shared memory array, a per-client control state, and a per-client request/response buffer. The system must permit clients to issue read and write requests, have the controller perform the requested operation on shared memory, and deliver responses for reads. The protocol should enforce a clear three-phase interaction for each client: (1) a client may submit a memory request only when it is ready; (2) the controller performs the operation (writing a value or fetching a value for a read) while marking the client as busy; (3) the controller produces a response and returns the client to the ready state. The model must maintain an invariant that the memory state is always a well-formed mapping from addresses to values, every client’s control state is one of the allowed statuses (ready, busy, done), and each buffer entry is either empty, a valid memory request, or a valid response value. The specification should allow non-deterministic choice of which client progresses at each step, preserve the global memory when appropriate (requests do not immediately modify memory), and show the above type and safety properties hold invariantly.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module augments the InternalMemory specification with liveness requirements for the internal memory system. It defines the tuple of variables used for temporal subscripting, introduces two alternative liveness formulas based on weak fairness of processor actions, and then defines LISpec as the original safety specification ISpec conjoined with one of those liveness conditions. The module also states a liveness property saying that whenever a processor's control state is busy, it eventually reaches the ready state, and includes a theorem asserting that LISpec implies this leads-to property.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent shared-memory system with a fixed set of processors that can issue read and write requests to a single memory, with an internal mechanism that may buffer requests and produce responses asynchronously. The model should include: processors that can be in at least two control states (requesting/busy and ready), a memory state that holds values for addresses, per-processor outstanding requests, and an internal representation of pending operations (such as an internal memory and buffers). The system must allow processors to perform request steps and receive response steps that update both processor control states and the memory state.

Require safety properties:
- Memory updates are atomic with respect to responses: a response must reflect some valid effect of an earlier request (no phantom writes or reads).
- No two conflicting operations may corrupt the stored value (consistency of memory state).

Require liveness properties:
- For every processor, if it issues a request and becomes busy, it eventually receives a response and becomes ready again (every issued request is eventually answered).
- Progress fairness: execution should not permanently starve any processor; scheduling must treat request and response steps fairly so that neither type of step is postponed forever.

Specify the initial conditions, define legal steps for requests and responses, and state invariants and the liveness obligations to be checked (safety invariants plus the eventual-response property for each processor).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module augments a write-through cache specification with liveness conditions. According to the comments, it adds the liveness condition described for the write-through cache and uses an equivalent definition of Spec from the instanced module so that TLC can check it. The module defines fairness requirements over cache response, read, write, and memory-queue actions, including a queue condition based on queue length or the presence of a read request, and then combines these fairness conditions with the imported safety specification.
desc_intent:
Specify a write-through cache system with multiple processors sharing a single memory and a bounded memory-request queue. The model must capture processors issuing reads and writes to their private caches, caches forwarding writes immediately to the shared memory (write-through), and a coordinator that services memory requests via a FIFO or similar bounded queue. The system should include contention and potential misses: a processor read may hit in cache or miss and then enqueue a memory read request; writes from caches must update both cache and enqueue a memory-write request that will update shared memory. The queue has limited capacity; when full, new memory-write requests are blocked until space is available. The model should also allow read requests to be served directly from memory when necessary and responses to be delivered to requesting processors.

Require safety properties:
- Cache coherence: if a processor reads a location and its cache reports a value, that value must reflect the most recent write to that location that has been made visible to memory or the cache.
- Memory consistency: memory updates from write-through operations are applied in program order for each processor and become visible to other processors according to the queue-delivery semantics.
- FIFO order (or specified queue ordering): requests are dequeued and applied to memory in queue order and no request is lost or duplicated.
- Bounds: the memory-request queue never exceeds its capacity.

Require liveness properties:
- Every issued read or write request by a processor either completes locally (hit) or eventually receives a response (miss serviced) — i.e., no request is permanently stalled due to scheduling or queue interactions.
- If a read miss is pending in the queue, it will eventually be served unless the queue remains permanently full with other requests; similarly, enqueued writes will eventually be applied to memory.
- Progress under fairness: assume weak or strong fairness for relevant request-processing and response actions so that stalled processors are eventually served.

Include parameters for number of processors, cache sizes (or abstract hit/miss behavior), queue length, and an abstract memory domain of addresses and values. The specification should avoid implementation details of scheduling while enabling checking of both safety and liveness properties under bounded queue capacity.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of a theorem about the HourClock specification, specifically that the invariant HCini is preserved by the HourClock system. The proof shows that if HC holds, then HCini holds always, by proving that HCini is preserved by the next-state relation HCnxt. The proof is structured hierarchically and uses the PTL backend for temporal logic reasoning.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a 12-hour digital clock that tracks the current hour and advances time in discrete steps. The model should represent the logical behavior of the clock (not its user interface) and must expose the possible states and transitions that reflect advancing time by one hour, including wrapping from 12 back to 1.

Requirements:
- The state must include an hour component whose domain is the integers 1..12 inclusive.
- Initialization must place the clock in a valid hour state (any value in 1..12 is allowed).
- The only step allowed is an advancement of the hour by one: from h it must move to h+1 when h < 12, and from 12 it must move to 1.
- The model must permit stuttering (no-op) steps so that temporal properties about invariants can be stated in the usual way.

Correctness properties to guarantee:
- Safety: the hour always stays within 1..12 in every reachable state.
- Progress: from any state there is a finite sequence of steps that reaches every other hour value (i.e., the system is strongly connected modulo stuttering).
- Invariance: a predicate asserting that the hour is within 1..12 is an invariant (holds initially and is preserved by all steps).
- Liveness: the clock eventually visits hour 12 infinitely often (fairness condition), or, alternatively, that every hour recurs infinitely often under a fairness assumption.

Do not prescribe internal variable names or a particular specification language structure; focus on the abstract state, transitions, initialization, and the properties above.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple 12-hour clock. The state variable 'hr' represents the current hour, which ranges from 1 to 12. The initial predicate HCini ensures that hr starts within this range. The next-state action HCnxt increments hr by 1 unless it is 12, in which case it wraps around to 1. The temporal property HC asserts that the system starts in a valid state and always evolves according to HCnxt. The theorem proves that the invariant HCini is always maintained. The design is straightforward, with no fault model or concurrency, and focuses on demonstrating a cyclic counter with a simple temporal invariant.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a simple 12-hour clock counter that cycles hours from 1 through 12 indefinitely. The model should represent a single state variable holding the current hour value and must allow only legal hour values in the set {1,2,...,12}. The transition relation must advance the hour by one on each step, wrapping from 12 back to 1. The behavior must start in a state satisfying the allowed-hour constraint and then follow the defined cyclic transitions forever.

Require the following correctness properties:
- Safety: every reachable state must contain a legal hour value (no illegal numbers appear at any time).
- Liveness/Progress: the system should be defined to make a step at each transition (the hour always advances according to the rule).
- Invariant preservation: the allowed-hour constraint must hold initially and be preserved by every transition.

Additionally, define an initial condition and a next-state relation concise enough to enable model checking; include a temporal formula stating that from any state satisfying the initial condition, the allowed-hour invariant holds globally. Avoid implementation details; focus on the abstract state space, the deterministic cyclical update rule, and the properties to be verified.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the InternalMemory specification, specifically proving that the type invariant (TypeInvariant) is preserved by the system. The proof addresses the fact that TypeInvariant alone is not inductive due to the way the next-state action Do(p) accesses fields of buf[p], which are only valid when buf[p] is in MReq. To resolve this, the invariant is strengthened with BufConsistent, which ensures that buf[p] has the correct type depending on the value of ctl[p]. The main theorem proved is that ISpec implies []TypeInvariant, using the strengthened invariant Inv (TypeInvariant /\ BufConsistent). The proof is structured hierarchically and uses TLAPS proof commands and backend solvers.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a simple concurrent internal memory interface with a fixed set of clients (processes) that request reads and writes to a shared memory. The model should capture the following components and behavior (without prescribing an implementation):

- A finite set of processes that repeatedly issue memory requests, wait for the memory controller to process them, and then receive responses before issuing the next request.
- A shared memory mapping from a finite set of addresses to values.
- Per-process request buffers that can be either empty, contain a pending memory request (address, operation type, and write value if any), or contain a value returned by a read.
- A per-process control state that indicates whether the process is ready to issue a request, has a request in flight, or has completed and is waiting to be acknowledged.

Transitions to model:
- A process in the ready state may issue a request: its control becomes busy and its buffer receives a well-formed request.
- The memory controller may perform a step for a process with a pending request: for a write, the memory is updated at the requested address; for a read, the process’s buffer is set to the value currently stored at the requested address. The process moves to the done state.
- A process in the done state may be acknowledged and return to ready; its buffer becomes empty or remains a valid value slot.

Requirements and safety properties to guarantee:
- Type safety: every system state must preserve typing invariants — memory is always a total mapping from addresses to values, every buffer has only allowed contents according to the process’s control state, and buffer fields are only accessed when the buffer contains a pending request.
- Memory correctness: writes update exactly the specified address with the specified value; reads return the memory value at the requested address at the time of the memory step.
- Invariance: these properties must hold initially and be preserved by every transition (i.e., prove that they are inductive invariants).
- No illegal accesses: the model must preclude operations that read or write using an invalid address or use undefined buffer fields.

Also specify auxiliary consistency conditions that relate per-process control states to allowed buffer contents so that verification of the main invariants is straightforward.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies an internal memory system that implements the MemoryInterface. The system models a set of processes interacting with a shared memory, where each process can issue memory requests, perform operations, and receive responses. The state is tracked by variables for memory contents (mem), control state per process (ctl), and per-process buffers (buf). The algorithm models request, operation, and response phases for each process, with explicit state transitions and primed variables. The specification asserts a type invariant is always maintained, and the main temporal property (ISpec) requires that the system starts in a valid initial state and all steps follow the allowed transitions, with the type invariant holding globally. The design uses explicit state transitions and does not model faults or failures.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a simple shared internal memory service that services concurrent client requests from a fixed set of clients. The model should describe the abstract protocol between clients and a memory controller that supports read and write requests, without committing to any particular implementation technique.

The system must expose these behaviors:
- Clients may at any time issue a memory request (read or write). Issuing a request hands a request object to the memory service and marks the client as having an outstanding request; the shared memory contents do not change at the moment the request is issued.
- The memory service processes outstanding requests one client at a time: when processing a write request, the memory contents are updated at the addressed location and the client's pending request is updated to indicate completion; when processing a read request, the service reads the current value and places it into the client's response buffer.
- After processing, the client can receive a reply that delivers the read value or acknowledges the write, and the client then becomes ready to issue a new request.

Specify the initial conditions (memory initial contents, all clients ready with empty buffers) and the allowed transitions (issue, process, reply). State invariants and correctness properties that must hold at all times:
- Memory contents remain a function mapping addresses to values.
- Each client is always in one of the protocol states: ready to issue, busy/processing, or done/awaiting reply.
- Each client's buffer holds either no pending request, a request, or a response value consistent with the most recent processing action.
- The protocol preserves consistency: a completed read returns the value that was present at the addressed location at the time the read was processed; a completed write updates the memory at the addressed location to the written value.
- No client loses requests or receives spurious replies; requests are eventually either processed and replied to or the system's progress assumptions should be explicitly stated (e.g., fairness) to ensure liveness.

Do not specify implementation-level scheduling, but allow nondeterministic interleaving of clients. Include type invariants and prove that the state space respects them and that the core safety properties above are invariant.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a simple real-time framework with a single clock variable now ranging over a bounded set of natural-number time values from 0 to MaxReal. It defines an initialization predicate for time, a real-time next-state relation RTNext(v) that either advances time while keeping an auxiliary state component v unchanged or keeps time fixed while allowing v to change, and a timer transition rule TimerNext that updates a timer variable t based on whether an action A occurs or is disabled. The specification also defines a fairness condition RTFairness(v) requiring weak fairness of time-progress steps above every real threshold, but it does not define a complete top-level Spec operator in this file.
desc_intent:
Model a real-time transition system with a discrete real-valued global clock that can only advance forward up to a known maximum value. The system consists of a control state evolving by discrete actions and a clock that continuously advances between discrete steps. The model must allow two kinds of steps: (1) internal time progress where the control state stays the same and the global time variable strictly increases to a later real value, and (2) discrete control transitions where the control state changes instantaneously while the global time does not advance. Time progress must never decrease and must always remain within the bounded real domain [0, MaxReal].

Include timed guards and deadlines on actions by associating with each enabled discrete action a per-action timer measuring elapsed time since the action became enabled. For each action, specify a minimum enabling time (an action cannot occur until its timer has reached at least a given lower bound) and a maximum enabling time (the action must either occur or the timer reset before exceeding an upper bound). When an action fires or becomes disabled, its timer resets to zero; while it remains enabled and time advances, its timer accumulates the real time elapsed.

Express fairness for time: ensure that time is not indefinitely prevented from advancing (time-progress fairness), so that for any requested future instant there is eventual time advancement consistent with the continuous time progress rule.

State the key correctness properties to verify: (1) Safety: discrete transitions respect their timing guards and deadlines; timers never exceed their declared upper bounds; and the clock stays within the allowed domain. (2) Liveness: enabled actions that are allowed by their minimum-delay constraints eventually occur before their maximum deadline or become disabled; and time can always progress (no unfair starvation of time advancement). Provide the model so that these properties can be checked with model checking or temporal logic proofs.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification defines a real-time memory-related wrapper around an internal memory specification. The top-level module introduces a positive real-time bound constant Rho, defines an inner module in which a response action forces a process control state to become "rdy", and requires that every process satisfy a real-time bound RTBound on that response action together with the imported internal-memory specification ISpec. The top-level property RTSpec existentially quantifies the internal state variables mem, ctl, and buf and states that there exists an instance of the inner real-time internal-memory specification satisfying RTISpec; the file uses imported real-time operators but does not itself define transition-system variables or proofs.
desc_intent:
Specify a real-time shared-memory interface with multiple processes that may issue requests and expect a timely ready response. Model an abstract memory component that interacts with a finite set of processes through request/ready handshake control but leave implementation details of the memory internal operations unspecified. The specification must describe the observable state of the memory, per-process control state, and any request or buffer structures necessary to represent outstanding operations.

The system must guarantee that whenever any process reaches a state representing that it has made a request and is not yet in the ready state, the memory will bring that process to the ready state within a bounded real-time delay proportional to a positive real constant ρ. That is, for every process and every time it becomes "waiting-for-ready," there must exist a real-time bound (a numeric constraint using ρ) ensuring the transition to ready occurs within that bound. The model should include a global notion of real time and express deadlines and timing constraints relative to that clock.

Additionally, ensure safety properties: the memory never produces an invalid ready signal (ready only when appropriate), and buffer and memory internal invariants are preserved across transitions. Express liveness: every legitimate request is eventually acknowledged within the specified real-time bound. Do not prescribe any concrete internal algorithm for memory servicing—only require the above correctness and timing properties for all processes.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a real-time wrapper around an existing write-through cache specification. It extends the underlying cache model with an additional variable lastP and a scheduling discipline that uses a computed position order to control which process may take certain expensive actions, specifically read misses and writes, while preserving other cache and memory queue actions. The specification assumes real-time parameters Delta, Epsilon, and Rho are positive reals satisfying a timing bound, and it asserts a real-time temporal specification RTSpec that combines initialization, a next-state relation, bounded-response timing constraints via RTBound, and the RTnow clocking condition; it finally states a theorem that this real-time specification implies the instantiated RTMemory real-time specification.
desc_intent:
Specify a parametric real-time write-through cache-coherence system with N processors sharing a main memory, where every processor has a private write buffer and may issue reads and writes to addresses. The specification should model the logical states of caches, buffers, memory, and a memory operation queue, and capture the timing constraints for operations without prescribing an implementation.

The model must allow processors to perform reads, writes, cache evictions, and receive responses, and it must permit background memory queue read/write operations. Introduce a notion of progress ordering among processors so that at most one processor that is “next” according to that ordering can start a read-miss or a write that modifies the global state; other processors may still perform local or non-conflicting actions.

Require real-time bounds: every memory-queue operation and every externally visible processor action (read miss, write commit, ordinary read, response) must satisfy specified upper bounds on their real-time latency (three positive real constants: a bound for memory-queue operations, and a tighter bound for per-processor visible actions). The bounds must be chosen so that the sum of worst-case delays across interfering processors plus queue delays is no greater than a recovery bound Rho (a global real constant), expressed as an inequality relating the constants and N.

Guarantee safety properties: coherence (no two processors observe conflicting versions of the same address), write-through semantics (writes become visible to memory according to the memory queue), and absence of illegal enabled conflicts (a processor may not start a read-miss or write if any higher-priority processor is currently allowed to proceed). Guarantee liveness/progress under the timing assumptions: operations subject to the real-time bounds complete within the specified delays and the system makes continual progress (no permanent starvation).

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a real-time hour clock by combining a real-valued time variable with an underlying hour-clock module. The outer module introduces a continuously increasing real-valued variable now and assumes a positive timing tolerance constant Rho; an inner module defines a timer variable t that is reset when the underlying hour clock advances and otherwise accumulates elapsed real time. The specification asserts timing bounds showing that the hour clock advances no later than 3600 + Rho seconds and, when it advances, no earlier than 3600 - Rho seconds, and the top-level behavior combines the inherited hour-clock behavior, monotonic real time, and the existence of an inner timer instance satisfying these real-time constraints.
desc_intent: Model a real-time hour clock that advances an abstract hour counter whenever a continuous real-valued global time reaches approximate one-hour intervals. The system must represent a real-valued monotonically increasing global time source and an hour counter that increments only when a one-hour epoch has elapsed, within a bounded timing jitter. The clock must guarantee that between successive hour increments the real time increases continuously and strictly, and that each increment occurs when the elapsed real time since the last increment is within a specified tolerance of exactly 3600 seconds. The tolerance is a positive constant: each hour tick must happen no earlier than 3600 − tolerance and no later than 3600 + tolerance after the previous tick. The model should permit arbitrary dense real time progress and fairness so that time can always advance beyond any given real value and hour increments are not starved by time progression. The specification must assert invariants capturing the timing bounds, liveness guaranteeing that hour ticks continue to occur as time progresses, and that the hour counter advances by exactly one on each tick. Abstract away scheduling/internal algorithmic details; focus on the real-time semantics, timing constraints for ticks, monotonicity of time, and the safety and liveness properties described.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines real-time temporal constraints over actions by introducing an explicit real-valued time variable `now` and auxiliary timer behavior. The operator `RTBound(A, v, D, E)` specifies that there exists a timer `t` which is reset when action `A` occurs or when `A` becomes disabled in the next state, otherwise advances by the elapsed real time `now' - now`, while also enforcing an upper bound `E` and a lower bound `D` relative to occurrences of `A`. The operator `RTnow(v)` constrains `now` to range over the reals, to increase monotonically through a stuttering-insensitive next-state action `NowNext`, and adds a weak fairness condition ensuring time can always progress past any real threshold.
desc_intent:
Specify a real-time system that enforces bounded-response timing for an action: model a system with a global continuously increasing real-valued clock and one or more discrete actions that may be enabled and eventually taken. The model should capture the passage of real time between discrete steps and allow nondeterministic scheduling of the actions subject to timing constraints.

Requirements:
- Time is represented by a real-valued clock that can always advance to any larger real value; time does not decrease and does not stagnate forever.
- Whenever the specified action becomes enabled, the system must ensure the action executes within a given upper bound E on real-time delay from the moment it first becomes enabled.
- While the action remains enabled, the elapsed real time since it became enabled must never be less than a given lower bound D before the action occurs (i.e., the action cannot occur sooner than D after becoming enabled).
- The model must express these bounds existentially via a logical "timer" value: there exists a nonnegative timer that resets to zero when the action occurs or is no longer enabled, increases with real time while the action remains enabled, and is always bounded above by E and below by D when the action fires.
- Liveness should guarantee that time can always progress and that weak/strong fairness conditions ensure the action will eventually occur respecting the timing bounds when enabled.

State the properties to be verified: time monotonicity, nonZeno progress (time can always advance), the upper-bound response property (action occurs within E), the lower-bound delay property (action does not occur before D), and the existence and correct update behavior of the timer that enforces those bounds.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a standard TLA+ representation of bags (multisets) as functions from elements to positive natural numbers, where the domain contains exactly the elements present in the bag and the function value gives the multiplicity. It provides operators for recognizing bags, converting between sets and bags, bag membership, empty bags, bag union and difference, subbag comparison, the set of all subbags, image construction over bags, cardinality, and counting copies of an element. The module is a pure mathematical library module rather than a transition-system specification: it has no variables, actions, or temporal properties, and its comments note that most operators are overridden by TLC except for SubBag.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of multisets (bags) and their algebraic operations and properties. The model should treat a bag as a finite collection of elements each with a positive integer multiplicity. It must provide operations to convert between finite sets and singleton-count bags, to test element membership and to query the multiplicity of an element (returning zero for absent elements). Include bag union (elementwise addition of multiplicities), bag difference (subtracting multiplicities but removing elements whose resulting multiplicity is zero or negative), and construction of a bag from a collection of bags by taking for each element the sum of multiplicities across the collection. Provide a way to map elements through a function into a new bag, combining multiplicities of elements that map to the same target. Include an operation that enumerates all sub-bags of a given bag (all bags whose multiplicities are pointwise less-or-equal and that only contain elements from the original bag). Define a bag cardinality operator that returns the total number of items counting multiplicities.

State precise invariants and correctness properties: closure of all operations within the type of finite bags; commutativity and associativity of bag union; monotonicity of union and mapping operations w.r.t. pointwise ordering; correctness of difference relative to multiplicity subtraction and element removal; that converting a set to a singleton-count bag and back preserves the set; and that mapping then taking cardinality equals summing multiplicities of preimages. Ensure all definitions handle empty bags cleanly and that all domains and sums are well-defined and finite.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines the standard finite-set operators `IsFiniteSet` and `Cardinality`. It characterizes finiteness by the existence of a finite sequence whose elements cover the set, and it defines cardinality recursively over subsets by removing one chosen element at a time until the empty set is reached. The file contains no state variables, no actions, and no temporal specification; it is a pure mathematical utility module with comments explaining that TLC overrides these operators in Java.
desc_intent: Model a specification of finite sets over an abstract universe and algorithms that operate on them. The specification should define what it means for a set to be finite by relating sets to finite sequences (or lists) that enumerate their elements, and it should provide a way to compute the size (cardinality) of any finite set. The model must also capture and verify basic closure properties: unions, intersections, set difference, and powersets of finite sets should themselves be finite, and the cardinality operator must satisfy expected algebraic identities (for disjoint unions, cardinality of union = sum of cardinalities; cardinality of a singleton = 1; removal of an element reduces cardinality by one when the element is present). Include properties ensuring that the enumeration of a finite set can be chosen without duplicates and that every element of the set appears at some position in the sequence. The model must reject or leave undefined cardinality for infinite sets. Specify invariants and temporal properties to prove that any algorithm that builds or reduces a finite set preserves finiteness and updates cardinality correctly. Finally, state liveness/termination requirements for constructive procedures that enumerate or compute cardinality (they must terminate producing a finite sequence or a number when given a finite set).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a dummy replacement for the standard TLA+ Integers module. It extends Naturals and provides placeholder definitions for integer-related operators, with comments explaining that tools such as TLC are expected to override these definitions with real implementations. The module defines the integer set Int as the empty set and defines the prefix negation operator in terms of subtraction, serving as a structural specification stub rather than a complete algorithmic system.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of an abstract integer arithmetic module built atop a more general real-number foundation. The model should treat integers as a subset of a richer numeric domain and expose the integer operations and relations needed by higher-level algorithms. Ensure the model defines integer values, negation, subtraction, addition, multiplication, ordering, and conversion to and from the underlying real-type values, and precisely specify their semantics in terms of the real-number foundation.

Require that all integer operations are closed: applying any defined integer operation to integers yields an integer. Require that integer arithmetic obeys the standard ring axioms (associativity, commutativity where appropriate, distributivity), negation is the additive inverse, and subtraction is defined consistently with addition and negation. Require that equality and ordering on integers coincide with equality and ordering restricted from the underlying real domain, and that integer-to-real embedding preserves arithmetic and ordering. Specify totality of comparison operators and that no operation produces non-integer or undefined results.

State invariants expressing these properties and include theorems to show consistency of the integer subset with the real foundation (e.g., embedding is injective and homomorphic). Describe expected proof obligations and correctness properties the formal model must guarantee without prescribing implementation.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a dummy placeholder specification for the standard Naturals module rather than an algorithm or distributed system. It defines placeholder versions of natural-number-related operators such as arithmetic, comparisons, and ranges, with comments explaining that real tools are expected to override them with proper implementations. The file contains no state variables, no transition system, no temporal behavior, no fault model, and no verified safety or liveness properties; its notable design decision is that most operators are given trivial or symbolic definitions solely as stand-ins.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of arithmetic on natural numbers and integer division suitable for proving basic algebraic properties and reasoning about ranges. The model should represent a discrete numeric domain (natural numbers and integers) with the usual operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, exponentiation, ordering (≤, <, ≥, >), integer ranges, integer division (quotient) and remainder. It must ensure that addition, multiplication and exponentiation are closed and associative/commutative where appropriate, and that ordering is a total order compatible with arithmetic. Define integer ranges as finite sets of consecutive integers given endpoints.

Crucially, specify integer division and remainder so that for any nonnegative divisor d > 0 and any dividend a, there exists a unique quotient q and remainder r such that a = d*q + r and 0 ≤ r < d. The quotient must be an integer and the remainder nonnegative and strictly smaller than the divisor. Provide properties linking division and modulo to ordering and arithmetic (e.g., a = d*(a div d) + (a % d), and relationships when a < d or when a is a multiple of d).

State invariants and theorems to verify uniqueness of quotient, correctness of remainder bounds, closure properties, and that ranges defined by endpoints contain exactly the intended integers. Also require proofs (or the ability to check proofs) of these properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module axiomatizes the Peano natural numbers using three parameters: a carrier set N, a distinguished zero element Z, and a successor function Sc. The main operator PeanoAxioms states that zero is in N, successor maps N to N, every non-zero element is the successor of some element, and every subset of N containing zero and closed under successor is all of N. The module then assumes existence of such a structure and defines Succ, Nat, and Zero by CHOOSE expressions to extract a particular successor function, its domain as the naturals, and a corresponding zero element.
desc_intent:
Model the natural numbers as an abstract Peano structure and specify the essential properties and operations needed for reasoning about arithmetic and induction. The model should treat a set of numbers, a distinguished zero element, and a successor function as primitive and must enforce the Peano axioms: zero is a member of the set; the successor is a total injective function from the set to itself; every nonzero element has a unique predecessor (i.e., an element is a successor iff it is not zero); and the set is the smallest set containing zero and closed under successor (induction principle). 

Specify the usual derived notions: the set of natural numbers, equality and inequality, the notion of predecessor where defined, and finite iteration of successor to represent natural-number addition by repeated successor. Define addition and multiplication as total operations on the natural numbers using these primitives (addition as iterated successor; multiplication as repeated addition). Require that addition and multiplication satisfy expected algebraic laws: associativity and commutativity of addition, identity zero for addition, associativity and commutativity of multiplication, distributivity of multiplication over addition, and zero annihilates multiplication.

Specify and prove the induction principle and basic correctness properties: closure of operations within the naturals, injectivity of successor, no predecessor for zero, and that every natural number is reachable from zero by a finite number of successor steps.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module axiomatizes and then selects a model of the real numbers on top of a Peano-style natural-number foundation imported from the Peano module. It defines a predicate IsModelOfReals(R, Plus, Times, Leq) expressing algebraic, order, and completeness properties of a real-number structure, proves existentially that some such model exists, then chooses one witness RM and introduces derived operators for Real numbers, infinities, arithmetic, ordering, subtraction, division, integers, and exponentiation. The specification is not a transition-system or fault-tolerant protocol model; instead it is a mathematical TLA+ theory module with no variables, no actions, and no temporal behavior, focused on abstract construction and characterization of reals and extended-real-like values.
