The model should describe processes (proposers/replicas) that propose inputs, read and write per-process blocks on a fixed set of disks, and progress through phases for preparing and accepting proposals. Disks store per-process disk blocks with ballot and metadata fields; processes can read blocks from disks and write blocks to subsets of disks. The protocol must allow a process to adopt a value based on majority information seen on disks and on reads performed by other processes, while preventing two different values from being chosen.

Requirements:
- Liveness-like progress: when a value has been output by any process, that value must be discoverable as already chosen by majority evidence on disks (a chosen value corresponds to some ballot with majority support).
- Safety: at most one input value can be chosen system-wide; once a value is chosen, all process outputs must either be that value or remain undecided.
- Invariants about ballots and inputs: ballot numbers must be monotonic where required; block ballot 0 must indicate "no input"; metadata ballots dominate ordinary ballots as appropriate.
- Read/write quorum intersection: any two majority disk sets intersect so information needed to prevent conflicting choices is preserved.
- Correct handling of incomplete reads: a proposer that cannot see a majority of relevant blocks must be prevented from deciding a conflicting input; if a proposer advances to accept a value it must either be provably backed by a max-ballot value in observed blocks or rely only on disks that indicate higher ballots preventing conflict.
- Outputs are only produced in the final phase and only if chosen evidence exists.

Include formal definitions for majority sets, the set of all observed input values, the notion of blocks read and written, and predicates characterizing when a value is considered chosen (based on a ballot and majority of disks). The model should be suitable for model checking and proving the stated invariants and safety property.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple Synod-style consensus abstraction over a set of processes 1..N, where each process has an input from Inputs and eventually may produce an output. The top-level module introduces an inner module that carries the actual state machine: it initializes each process output to a distinguished non-input value, tracks the set of all current inputs, and allows either a choice step that copies a selected value into an output or a failure-like step that changes a process input. The overall specification hides the internal variables chosen and allInput existentially, and it checks the temporal behavior of the inner system via the invariant-style initialization plus a boxed next-state relation without explicit fairness conditions.
desc_intent:
Specify a distributed consensus-style protocol for N processes that repeatedly attempt to choose values from a finite set of possible inputs. The system must model an environment in which each process always has an input value (drawn from a given set of Inputs) and an output slot that may either hold a chosen value or indicate “no decision yet.” The protocol should allow processes to do two kinds of steps: (1) decide (or adopt) a value for its output, either by proposing a previously unchosen input from among the inputs present in the system or by adopting a value that was already globally chosen by a prior decide step; and (2) fail or reset its own output and change its current input value nondeterministically to any value in Inputs, thereby possibly introducing new inputs into the set of values seen by processes.

Model the global auxiliary notion of the set of all input values currently present among processes; that set must evolve whenever a process changes its input. Initially every process has some input value and every output slot is undecided (no decision made), and no global chosen value yet exists.

The specification must capture fairness-free nondeterministic execution (actions can be chosen arbitrarily) and require the following correctness properties:
- Safety (Agreement): if two processes have decided (their outputs are set to a concrete value), they must have the same decided value.
- Validity: any value that ever becomes a decided output must be a value that has been present as some process’s input at some point.
- Stability of chosen value: once a global chosen value exists, future decisions by other processes may adopt that same value but cannot introduce a different globally adopted value.
- Liveness variant (optional): characterize how failures and input changes can prevent progress; state whether eventual decisions for all non-failing processes are required or left unspecified.

Do not prescribe implementation details such as particular variables, choice operators, or step-by-step algorithms; describe only the allowed state components and the invariant and temporal properties the model must enforce.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the Echo algorithm for constructing a spanning tree in an undirected connected graph starting from a single initiator. The graph is modeled by a set of nodes and a Boolean neighborhood relation R, with assumptions that R is irreflexive, symmetric, and connected; communication is modeled by per-node inbox sets containing message records. The PlusCal algorithm is included together with its TLA+ translation, and the specification verifies safety-style properties such as type correctness, absence of a parent for the initiator, parent-neighbor consistency, parent-child consistency, and ancestor properties at termination, as well as a termination temporal property stating that all processes eventually reach Done.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a distributed Echo (wave) algorithm that constructs a spanning tree in a connected undirected network starting from a single designated initiator. Model each node as an independent process that communicates by asynchronous point-to-point messages with its neighbors. The model must allow arbitrary message delivery order and interleaving, but messages are neither duplicated nor spontaneously created. The initiator must start the wave by sending a probe to all its neighbors. A non‑initiator, on receiving its first probe, must record the sender as its parent and forward the probe to all its other neighbors; subsequent probes are treated as replies or ignored for further forwarding. After a node has exchanged messages with all its neighbors (i.e., received exactly one message from each neighbor), a non‑initiator must send an acknowledgment to its parent. The initiator completes when it has received acknowledgments from all neighbors.

Require the model to guarantee the following correctness properties:
- Safety: no node ever chooses a parent that is not one of its neighbors; the initiator never chooses a parent.
- Parent–child consistency: if a node records another node as parent then the parent eventually records it as a child (and eventually every recorded parent–child relation corresponds to the child having informed that parent).
- Termination: every node eventually completes the protocol (terminates).
- Spanning tree: when all nodes have terminated, the parent relations form a rooted, acyclic spanning tree that includes every node with the initiator as the unique root and an ancestor relation that is irreflexive.
Also specify basic type invariants (message formats, mailbox contents, neighbor sets) and permit checking of the above properties under arbitrary connected undirected topologies and a single designated initiator.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines basic relational properties and operations for relations represented as binary Boolean functions over a set S. It provides predicates to check if a relation is reflexive, irreflexive, symmetric, asymmetric, transitive, and connected over a set. It also defines operators to compute the transitive closure and reflexive transitive closure of a relation, using recursive LET-bound operators and function constructors. The module is intended as a reusable library for reasoning about relations, and does not specify a particular algorithm or system, nor does it include temporal properties or proofs.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of binary relations on a finite universe and the standard relation-theoretic queries and closures that must be guaranteed. The model should treat a relation as a Boolean predicate over ordered pairs drawn from a given finite set. It must provide predicates to determine whether a relation is reflexive, irreflexive, symmetric, asymmetric, and transitive with respect to a designated finite domain.

Additionally, specify operators that compute the transitive closure of a relation over the domain and the reflexive-transitive closure. The transitive-closure operator must be defined so that it yields the least relation containing the original one and closed under composition (i.e., whenever (x,y) and (y,z) are in the closure, (x,z) is in the closure), and it must be computable in a finite number of steps for finite domains. The reflexive-transitive closure must additionally include all identity pairs.

Finally, specify a predicate that tests whether the relation induces a single strongly connected component on the domain (every element can reach every other element through zero or more steps along the relation). State the intended semantics and correctness properties (closure operators are monotone and idempotent and satisfy the usual characterizations) without prescribing a particular implementation strategy.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the Dijkstra-Scholten distributed termination detection algorithm for a diffusing computation initiated by a distinguished root node. The system maintains a dynamic spanning tree of active nodes, with nodes sending base messages, receiving acknowledgments, detaching from the tree when inactive and childless, and the initiator declaring termination when it becomes inactive and has no remaining children. The specification includes a PlusCal algorithm and its TLA+ translation, models bounded message counts for state-space exploration, assumes a finite node set with an initiator in that set, and verifies both a safety property that termination implies quiescence and a liveness property that quiescence leads to eventual termination under weak fairness of each process action.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of Dijkstra–Scholten termination detection for a diffusing distributed computation initiated by a single designated root. Model a fixed finite set of processes (nodes) that communicate by asynchronous point-to-point messages of two kinds: application (base) messages that propagate work and acknowledgement messages used to notify parents when children are done. The system begins with only the initiator active; other nodes become active only upon receiving a base message. Nodes may send base messages to any other node to create new activity, record who sent them their activating base message as their parent (thus building a dynamic spanning tree of active nodes), and later return acknowledgements to that parent when they and all their descendants become passive. A node that receives a base message and already has a parent must immediately send an acknowledgement back to that sender instead of adopting it. Leaf nodes that are passive and have no active children detach from the tree by sending an acknowledgement to their parent (or, if the parent is the initiator itself and becomes passive with no children, allowing the initiator to declare global termination).

Require the model to bound message counts for state-space finiteness but faithfully capture possible reactivation (a node can be reactivated after detaching) and concurrent interleavings. Specify the main correctness properties:
- Safety: termination may be declared only when the entire system is quiescent (no node active and no pending messages).
- Liveness: if the system reaches quiescence, termination will eventually be declared.
Also specify basic invariants (well-formed types, message-count bounds) and fairness assumptions needed to guarantee liveness of enabled actions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models the Dijkstra-Scholten tree algorithm for detecting termination of a diffusing distributed computation over an arbitrary directed process graph. Processes can be active or idle, computation messages flow along graph edges, acknowledgments flow in the reverse direction, and an overlay parent relation is maintained dynamically to form a tree of non-neutral processes rooted at the leader. The spec assumes asynchronous unordered but lossless message delivery, no Byzantine failures, and verifies safety and liveness properties including counter consistency, an overlay-tree invariant, the fact that if the leader is neutral then all other processes are neutral, and the leads-to property that if the computation has terminated then the leader eventually becomes neutral.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of a distributed termination-detection protocol that implements the Dijkstra–Scholten tree algorithm over an arbitrary directed process network. Model a fixed finite set of processes and a fixed directed communication graph in which the distinguished leader has no incoming computation edges. Processes execute an independent computation and may be either busy (active) or idle; busy processes can send application (computation) messages to neighbors, and receiving a computation message makes the recipient busy. Messages (both computation and control/acknowledgment messages) are delivered asynchronously, unordered, and reliably (no loss or duplication). Control messages travel in the opposite direction of computation edges so that any sender of computation can receive acks.

The specification must capture the dynamic construction of an overlay parent relation: when an otherwise neutral process first receives a computation message, it associates that sender as its parent and only relinquishes that parent when it becomes neutral again. Each computation message must eventually be acknowledged to its sender; a process may delay sending an acknowledgment for a message from its parent until doing so would make it neutral. Neutrality means: the process is idle, has no outstanding acks to send for messages received, and has received acknowledgments for all computation messages it sent. The protocol must preserve the invariant that non-neutral processes form a directed tree rooted at the leader.

State the safety property that the leader can become neutral only when the entire system has no pending computation messages and all processes are idle. State the liveness property that if the global computation terminates (every process idle and no computation messages in transit), then eventually the leader becomes neutral (i.e., termination is detected). Also assert consistency relations between local counters and in-transit message counts so that bookkeeping for sent, received, and acknowledged messages is conserved.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module contains TLAPS proofs for the synchronous termination detection specification defined in the imported module SyncTerminationDetection. It proves safety properties such as type correctness, correctness of termination detection, and quiescence, and also proves a liveness property showing that once the system is terminated and detection has not yet occurred, the DetectTermination action can lead to terminationDetected becoming true. The file is proof-oriented rather than algorithm-defining: it extends the base specification and TLAPS, uses invariance and temporal proof rules, and introduces one lemma characterizing the enabledness of the DetectTermination action.
desc_intent:
Specify a synchronous termination-detection protocol for a distributed computation running on a fixed set of processes connected by reliable point-to-point channels. The model should describe process-local states and a global notion of whether a process is "terminated" (it has no internal work and has sent no outstanding messages) and a global flag indicating whether termination has been detected. The system must allow processes to perform local actions that send and receive messages, locally become terminated, and perform a dedicated detection action that can set the global detection flag when the system is in a safe termination state.

Requirements:
- Initially no process is terminated and the termination-detected flag is false.
- Processes may asynchronously send and receive messages; message channels have reliable FIFO delivery semantics (or equivalent reliable delivery) and messages in transit prevent global termination.
- A process may change its local status to terminated only when it has no pending local work and has no outstanding outgoing messages.
- Termination detection must be enabled precisely when every process is terminated and no messages are in transit.
- Once termination is detected, the detection flag becomes true and remains true forever (safety).
- If the system reaches a state where all processes are terminated and no messages are in transit, then under weak fairness for the detection action the detection flag will eventually be set (liveness).
- Type and invariant constraints should ensure well-formed process states and channel contents.

State the safety properties (type correctness, detection correctness, monotonicity of the detected flag) and the fairness/liveness property that detection eventually occurs when the system is quiescent.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module contains TLAPS proofs about a high-level TLA+ specification of asynchronous termination detection. It proves type correctness, safety, stability/quiescence, and a liveness property by reasoning about the imported specification's predicates and actions such as Init, Next, DetectTermination, Terminate, RcvMsg, and SendMsg. The module itself is proof-oriented: it introduces lemmas and theorems over the imported state machine, reduces an ENABLED fairness premise to a state predicate, and uses PTL and ExpandENABLED to discharge temporal reasoning obligations.
desc_intent:
Specify an asynchronous distributed termination-detection protocol for a fixed set of processes communicating by message passing. The model should express processes that can be active or passive, send and receive messages asynchronously, and transition between active/passive states based on internal computation and message handling. The system must detect global quiescence: when every process is passive and no in-flight messages remain, some designated detector eventually learns this fact. The model should capture as requirements:

- Safety: The detector must never declare termination unless the system is actually quiescent (no active processes and no outstanding messages).
- Liveness: If the system reaches a quiescent state, the detector must eventually detect and declare termination (progress despite asynchrony).
- Type and invariants: process states and message counts remain within expected domains and any bookkeeping variables used to detect termination maintain consistency across transitions.
- Asynchrony and fairness: message delivery is asynchronous and non‑lossy; fairness assumptions (weak fairness for the termination-detection action or for enabled detection steps) required to guarantee eventual detection should be stated explicitly.
- Stability: once termination is correctly detected, the detected state remains true thereafter.

Do not constrain the solution to a particular implementation technique (e.g., token circulation, credit/reduction counters, or spanning tree); instead, specify the abstract behaviors, state predicates (active/passive, in-flight messages, detected flag), transitions allowed (send, receive, local compute, detect), and the correctness properties above so various termination-detection algorithms can be validated against them.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines an instrumented and configurable variant of the EWD998 channel-based termination-detection specification for use with TLC trace generation and statistics collection. It adds feature-flag controlled optimizations to token passing, constrains initial simulation states to realistic ones, and defines a behavior specification in which system steps and environment steps evolve under the inherited variables from the base module. The file also configures TLC to run in generation mode, disables deadlock checking because termination is expected, records when termination occurs, and writes per-behavior measurements such as action counts and delay between environment termination and detection to a CSV output.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a distributed termination-detection protocol for a unidirectional token-passing ring of N processes. The system should allow processes to be active or inactive, to send ordinary messages that can activate other processes, to maintain local counters of sent work, and to circulate a special probe/token message that carries an ownership id, a cumulative counter, and a color bit used to detect outstanding work. The protocol must support an initiator that occasionally starts probe rounds to determine global quiescence, and processes that on receipt of the token update the token’s cumulative count and color based on local state. Model optional protocol variants controlled by a set of feature flags that can permit (1) passing the token even when the holder or token is “tainted”, (2) using local or incoming taint information to decide passing, and (3–4) aborting a token round early by returning the token immediately to the initiator when the holder or the token is black. The model must allow an external environment to perform arbitrary message sends and activations to represent workload.

Require the specification to guarantee safety and liveness properties: (a) the detection is sound—when the protocol signals termination, there are no active processes and no messages in transit; (b) detection is eventual—if the system truly becomes quiescent, an initiated probe eventually causes the initiator to detect termination; and (c) absence of false positives—the protocol must not report termination while activity remains. Also require metrics collection: count rounds, probe and token actions, sends/receives, and the number of steps between the environment becoming quiescent and the initiator detecting termination to compare efficiency across feature-flag variants.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module contains TLAPS proofs for the EWD998PCal specification, which is a PlusCal translation of Dijkstra's EWD998 token ring algorithm. In this version, the per-node 'pending' counter and the global 'token' are replaced by a single 'network' variable holding a per-node bag of messages (either payload 'pl' messages or the unique 'tok' message). The refinement mapping recovers the original EWD998 variables from 'network'. The module proves the safety part of the refinement, specifically that the PCal spec refines the original EWD998 spec (Spec => EWD998Spec), focusing on type correctness and the preservation of the unique token property. The proofs include inductive invariants, bag-level reasoning, and per-disjunct case analysis for each possible node action, but the full step-refinement theorem is left as a stub (OMITTED) due to the complexity of the required bag-level lemmas.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a distributed token-based termination detection protocol for a fixed ring (or sequence) of N processes with asynchronous message passing. The system maintains per-process message queues (bags) that may hold either ordinary payload messages or a single unique token message that moves among processes. The model must capture: process-local state (active/inactive, color white/black, local counters), per-process bags of messages, and a globally unique token that carries a numeric counter and a color bit. Initially exactly one process holds the token (with q = 0 and color = black) and all message bags are empty; all processes are inactive and counters are zero.

Model actions for (at least): sending a payload to another process (which increments a sender counter and appends a payload message to the recipient’s bag), receiving a payload (decrementing a counter and possibly changing activity/color), passing the token to the next process (updating token position, q, and token color), and initiating probe/termination when appropriate. Messages are nondeterministically delivered and may be added/removed from per-process bags; ensure bags preserve typing and the token remains unique.

State the correctness properties to prove:
- Safety: at all times exactly one token exists in the system (unique token invariant), and all message bags contain only well-typed messages.
- Refinement: the abstract variables (per-process pending counts and the token tuple) recovered from the bags and token witness correspond to a known abstract specification of EWD998-style termination detection.
- Liveness/specification goal: when all processes become inactive and there are no payload messages outstanding, the protocol eventually reports global termination (token-based detection succeeds).

Do not presuppose a specific implementation; leave the algorithmic steps abstract as actions that manipulate process-local state and per-process message bags subject to the typing and uniqueness constraints above.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines an SVG-based animation layer for Dijkstra's EWD998 distributed termination detection algorithm, specifically for a ring of nodes that exchange messages and circulate a colored token with an accumulated queue count. It is not the base algorithm itself; instead, it extends an existing channel-based specification and visualizes current and next-state information such as node activity, node color, message counters, token position and color, in-flight versus arriving messages, and global status such as running, terminated, or termination detected. The design emphasizes deterministic rendering, modular visual components, debugger watch support, and TLC alias support for frame-by-frame animation generation.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of Dijkstra’s EWD998 distributed termination-detection protocol for a unidirectional ring of asynchronous processes. Model processes that asynchronously send and receive indistinct "work" messages and a circulating token used to detect global quiescence. The model must capture: process local state (active vs. inactive), a per-process taint flag that marks whether the process has become "black" (tainted) since last pass of the token, per-process counters that track messages sent minus messages received, and asynchronous FIFO channels between neighbors that can hold messages in flight. The token must carry a color (white/black) and an integer accumulator representing the sum of counters or queue contributions observed while the token traverses the ring. Processes may become active by performing local work that sends messages to other processes; they become inactive when they have no local work to perform. Message delivery is asynchronous and may be delayed arbitrarily but preserved (no loss or duplication). The token circulates sequentially around the ring; each process, when receiving the token, updates the token color/accumulator based on its taint and counters and may reset its taint and counters per the algorithm’s rules.

State the correctness properties to verify:
- Safety: Termination detection is only declared when all processes are inactive, all channels are empty, and the accumulators indicate no outstanding messages (i.e., global quiescence).
- Liveness: If the system actually reaches global quiescence (all processes idle and no messages in channels), then the token eventually completes a circulation that causes the algorithm to detect termination.
- No false positives: The algorithm must never declare termination while any message is still in flight or any process is active.
- Preservation: Message counts and channel contents evolve consistently with sends and receives (conservation of messages).

Include parameters for ring size and unbounded but finite channel capacities, and allow nondeterministic scheduling of process actions and message delivery. The specification should not assume synchronous steps or global clocks.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a TLC scripting specification that orchestrates multiple nested TLC runs of another specification, EWD998_opts.tla, in order to collect statistics and write results to a CSV file. It defines a finite set of feature flags and node values, constructs a CSV filename using the current Java time, writes CSV headers, builds a command line for invoking TLC recursively, and then assumes successful execution of nested runs over all subsets of features and all chosen node values. The specification is not modeling the protocol itself directly; instead, it models an experiment driver that uses IO utilities and TLC-side effects to execute simulations and classify outcomes such as assumption, safety, and liveness violations.
desc_intent:
Model a family of distributed system experiments that explore how variants of a token-based probe protocol behave under different node counts and feature subsets. The model should represent a network of identical processes (nodes) that can send and receive messages, initiate probes, pass a token, and deactivate/reactivate components. It must support parametrization by:
- the set of participating nodes (varying sizes),
- a selection of optional features that alter behavior or enable/disable protocol actions,
- multiple randomized or enumerated runs per configuration for statistical collection.

The system should simulate asynchronous message delivery with no global clock, allowing arbitrary interleavings and possible message loss or delays if a feature set specifies such faults. It must allow a process to initiate a probe, forward or respond to probes, pass a token to coordinate activity, and deactivate itself while preserving safety invariants. Correctness properties to guarantee for all configurations and runs:
- Safety: no two nodes concurrently hold conflicting authoritative state (e.g., at most one token holder, no duplicate probe initiations causing inconsistent decisions).
- Integrity: messages and probes, when processed, lead to well-formed state transitions; deactivated nodes do not corrupt global invariants.
- Progress/Liveness under fair scheduling when required by enabled features: probes eventually terminate and tokens are eventually passed or reclaimed, absent permanent faults.
- Termination or stable quiescence detection: the protocol can detect when no further meaningful actions remain.

Additionally, the model should produce per-run statistics (counts of probe initiations, token passes, sends/receives, deactivations, and execution length) for each node and feature combination for later analysis.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines an options and measurement wrapper around the underlying EWD998 termination-detection specification. It introduces feature flags for several algorithm variants, constrains the randomized initial states and environment behavior for TLC generation mode, and defines an alternative system/environment composition used for simulation and data collection. It also records statistics at termination and when termination is detected, using TLC, CSV, and IO utilities, while assuming probabilistic generation mode and disabling deadlock checking because the modeled algorithm is assumed to terminate.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a distributed termination-detection protocol for a fixed-size ring of processes that execute asynchronous work and communicate via point-to-point messages. The model should capture that each process can be either active or inactive, can hold local messages pending delivery, and may send or receive messages that generate further work. Processes may spontaneously become inactive, and messages may be delivered nondeterministically. The protocol must allow a process (an initiator) to periodically start a probe consisting of a circulating token that collects information about activity and outstanding messages to decide global termination.

Require the model to support a family of independent optional protocol features that alter token-handling and initiation rules: (a) allowing an active holder of the token to pass it under certain taint conditions (token or holder marked), (b) allowing early abort of a token round by returning the token immediately to the initiator when a holder is marked, (c) allowing early abort when the token itself is marked, and (d) allowing the initiator to start a probe only when it is inactive. These options must be parameterizable so experiments can enable any subset.

The specification must define termination as every process inactive with no pending messages, and termination-detection as the initiator concluding termination via a successful probe. Key correctness properties: safety — the initiator must never detect termination unless the system is actually terminated; liveness — if the system becomes quiescent, some probe eventually detects termination (assuming random scheduling); and preservation of message-count invariants ensuring the token correctly accounts for outstanding messages so detection is reliable. The model should permit statistical experimentation (randomized scheduling and initial states) to measure how feature choices affect time and number of probes until detection.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a generic operator MapThenFoldSet for folding over a set S by first mapping each element x in S through a function f, then combining the results using a binary operator op, starting from a base value. The folding order is determined by a user-supplied choose function, which selects an element from a set; if op is not associative and commutative, the result may depend on the choice order. The comments explain that this is a generalization of simpler fold operators for sets, functions, and sequences, and provide an example usage. No temporal properties or state variables are present; this is a pure functional operator for set processing.
desc_intent:
Specify a declarative model of a generic fold-over-a-finite-set operation that maps each element through a mapping function and then combines the mapped values with a binary operator to produce a single result. The model should treat the input collection as an unordered finite set and must allow nondeterministic choice of the next element to process. The fold must start from a given initial accumulator value, apply the mapping to each selected element, and combine that mapped value into the accumulator with the binary operator until every element of the set has been processed exactly once.

Require the model to capture the dependence of the final result on three aspects: the mapping function, the binary operator, and the order in which elements are chosen. Specify the constraints under which the final result is independent of the nondeterministic choice order: namely, when the binary operator is associative and commutative (and any type/domain requirements needed for its application). Express correctness properties including: termination (the process finishes after a finite number of steps for any finite input set), determinism of result under the stated algebraic conditions (same result for any choice order when operator is associative and commutative), and preservation of elements (each input element is mapped and combined exactly once). Also state typestate requirements (operator well-defined on mapped outputs and accumulator) and examples of expected outcomes for concrete choices of map, operator, base, and input set.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a collection of operators for reasoning about functions in TLA+, including restriction, range, pointwise operations, inverses, and properties such as injectivity, surjectivity, and bijectivity. It provides definitions for restricting a function to a subset of its domain or to values satisfying a predicate, checking if one function is a restriction of another, and constructing the range of a function. The module also defines operators for constructing sets of injections, surjections, and bijections between sets, as well as checking for their existence. Additional operators include pointwise combination of functions and folding over function values. The module is utility-focused and does not specify a distributed algorithm or system, nor does it include temporal properties or fault models.
desc_intent:
Model a library of total finite functions between sets and the common operations and predicates used to reason about them. The model should treat functions as finite mappings from a finite domain to values and provide operators to: restrict a function to a subset of its domain or to the domain elements whose images satisfy a predicate; compute the image (range) of a function or of a subset of its domain; apply a binary operator pointwise to two functions with compatible domains; compute an inverse mapping that maps values back to representative domain elements (and a special case returning the inverse on the whole range); and fold a commutative, associative binary operation over the values of a function (optionally restricted to a set of indices).

Specify predicates and sets to characterize injective, surjective, and bijective mappings between two sets, and predicates that assert existence of at least one injection, surjection, or bijection. Include an operator that checks whether one function is a restriction of another (domain subset and identical values where both defined).

The model must ensure these operators behave consistently with standard mathematical definitions: restrictions preserve values on kept domain elements; range and inverse are dual (inverse applied to the function’s range yields a left-inverse picking some preimage for each value); pointwise application only references indices common to the first function’s domain; fold is well-defined independent of evaluation order when the binary operator is associative and commutative. State the expected preconditions for each operator and the key correctness properties (e.g., range(Restrict(f,S)) ⊆ Range(f); composition of Inverse with original yields identity on the range up to choice; Injection implies |Range| = |Domain|, Surjection implies Range = target set).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a smoke-test harness specification that orchestrates repeated TLC simulations of another specification, SmokeEWD998.tla, and records outcomes to a CSV file. It defines a CSV filename using the current Java time, writes the CSV header at startup via an ASSUME statement, constructs a Java command line for invoking TLC, and then uses a quantified ASSUME to execute many nested runs over combinations of bug flags and random process counts. The module is not itself a transition-system specification with variables or temporal behavior; instead, it is a scripting-style TLA+ model that uses IOUtils, CSV, and TLC operators to drive external execution, classify exit codes such as assumption, invariant, and property violations, and log them.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a distributed system that explores how independent faults affecting processes lead to safety or liveness violations, and collect statistics about which fault combinations cause which outcomes. The system consists of a small finite set of identical processes that interact by exchanging messages or taking local steps; some steps may be nondeterministic. A test harness repeatedly selects subsets of one or more faults to inject simultaneously; a fault is any deterministic, reproducible deviation from the nominal behavior of a single process (for example: delay of a step, omission of a message, wrong message content, crash, or arbitrary state corrupt). Each trial runs the system to completion (or to a bounded length) under the chosen set of faults and reports one of: clean run (no property violated), assumption violation (precondition or environment assumption broken), safety invariant violation, or temporal-property (liveness) violation.

Model the selection of fault combinations uniformly from all nonempty subsets of a fixed fault set and allow multiple independent trials with different random seeds. Ensure the harness records, for each fault set and trial outcome, which class of outcome occurred. Specify correctness properties: (1) Safety invariants must hold in all executions without faults; (2) when faults are injected, the model must correctly classify executions into the four outcome categories; (3) trials must be independent and reproducible given the same seed and fault set; (4) the statistics collection must deterministically reflect the result of each trial (no lost or duplicate recordings). Include a bounded execution length to ensure termination of each trial.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a utility predicate for reasoning about finite functional graphs represented by a relation or function r over a set S. The main operator, IsSimpleCycle, characterizes when repeatedly following r from a chosen start node visits exactly the elements of S, using a finite sequence built over 1..Cardinality(S). The module is a helper-style specification with no variables, actions, temporal behavior, fairness, or proofs; it relies on imported modules for integers, sequences, finite-set cardinality, and function-domain/range operators.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a deterministic functional graph cycle detector and validator for a finite set of nodes. The model should treat the system as a function that maps every node to exactly one successor (a total function on a finite nonempty vertex set). The model must capture the notion of a single simple directed cycle that visits every vertex exactly once: there exists an ordering of the vertices such that following the successor function repeatedly from any starting vertex yields that ordering cyclically and returns to the start after exactly N steps (where N is the number of vertices). The model must permit arbitrary finite nonempty vertex sets and arbitrary total successor mappings, and must characterize precisely when such a mapping constitutes a Hamiltonian directed cycle (simple cycle covering all vertices).

State the correctness properties to verify:
- Existence property: if the mapping is claimed to be a simple cycle, then every vertex has a unique predecessor and unique successor, and repeated application of the mapping from any vertex visits all vertices before returning to the start after N steps.
- Uniqueness property: there is no smaller positive k < N such that k repeated applications of the mapping return to the start for every vertex (i.e., the cycle length equals the vertex count).
- Safety property: no vertex is repeated before all distinct vertices have been visited.
Also require invariants expressing finiteness and totality of the mapping, and provide an artifact suitable for model checking of these properties over arbitrary finite vertex sets.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a TLAPS proof module for the safety properties of the specification in the extended module clean. It proves that the imported specification Spec implies the invariants []TypeOK, []primerPositive, and []preservationInvariant, and adds an explicit assumption that the unconstrained constants DNA and PRIMER are natural numbers so arithmetic facts can be used in the proofs. The file is proof-oriented rather than algorithm-defining: it contains assumptions, one helper lemma about natMin, and three main theorems with structured proofs over the imported actions heat, cool, anneal, extend, and stuttering via UNCHANGED vars.
desc_intent: Model a simple biochemical protocol that manipulates four nonnegative integer resources representing counts of primer, template, hybrid (paired primer-template), and DNA product. The system repeatedly performs one of a small set of atomic operations that conserve or reassign these counts under natural-number semantics. Specify the initial state allowing arbitrary natural-number values for the four resources. The allowed atomic operations are: (a) a heating step that transfers all hybrid into separate primer and template counts and clears hybrid, possibly producing DNA; (b) an annealing step that pairs up to the minimum available of primer and template, moving that many units into hybrid while decreasing primer and template; (c) an extension step that converts all current hybrid into DNA product and clears hybrid; and (d) a no-op that leaves state unchanged. The model must ensure all values remain natural numbers throughout execution and that annealing only pairs a positive number up to the available minimum. Express the main correctness properties to prove: (1) a type-safety invariant that primer, template, hybrid, and DNA stay in Nat; (2) a positivity invariant ensuring primer count never becomes negative; and (3) a conservation invariant that the quantity template + primer + 2*(DNA + hybrid) is preserved by every step. Do not commit to a particular implementation; allow nondeterministic choice among the operations.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof of the type-correctness invariant for the system specified in stages.tla. The main property proved is that the type-correctness invariant TypeOK is preserved by the system's specification Spec, i.e., Spec => []TypeOK. The proof is structured hierarchically and checks that all state transitions maintain the Nat-typedness of the relevant variables, using assumptions about the constants and properties of the natMin function. The proof leverages definitions and actions from the extended stages module and uses TLAPS proof commands and structure.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a simple staged reaction system that manipulates three nonnegative integer quantities representing available substrate, available catalyst, and bound complex. The system evolves in discrete steps; each step performs exactly one of a small set of atomic stage types: (1) a heating stage that leaves counts unchanged except possibly satisfying pre/postconditions of the stage; (2) a cooling stage that similarly may change state according to its intended semantics; (3) an annealing stage that transfers some nonnegative amount from both substrate and catalyst into the bound complex simultaneously; (4) an extension stage that models growth of the bound complex; or (5) a no-op stage that leaves all three counts unchanged. The annealing stage must choose a nonnegative integer amount k not exceeding the smaller of the current substrate and catalyst counts, then decrease both substrate and catalyst by k and increase the bound complex by k. All counts must remain in the natural numbers at all times.

Model initial conditions allowing arbitrary natural-number values for the three quantities subject to any declared constant bounds. Specify a safety invariant ensuring that every reachable state satisfies the natural-number typing constraint for all three quantities. Also specify progress/step constraints that each action is executable only when its preconditions hold and that state updates preserve the invariant. Do not encode implementation details; state only the allowed stage kinds, their required effects, and the invariant properties the model must guarantee.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models Lamport's distributed mutual-exclusion algorithm from the 1978 paper "Time, Clocks and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System". It represents a set of processes that communicate by pairwise FIFO message queues, using logical clocks, request messages, acknowledgements, and release notifications to coordinate entry into a critical section. The specification defines the initial state, the process actions for sending and receiving protocol messages, a next-state relation, and a temporal specification `Spec == Init /\\ [][Next]_vars`; it also states safety-oriented predicates such as type correctness, a bounded-network property for model checking, a clock bound state constraint helper, and the mutual exclusion invariant `Mutex`.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of a distributed mutual‑exclusion algorithm in which N processes coordinate solely by exchanging timestamped messages over pairwise FIFO channels. The model should describe asynchronous message passing where processes have local logical clocks that advance on sending and on receiving messages, and where messages are of three kinds: request (carrying the sender’s timestamp), acknowledgement, and release. Each process may request access to a single shared critical section, must broadcast its request to all other processes, collect acknowledgements from every peer, and defer entry until it can determine by timestamps (and tie‑breaking by process id) that its request has priority over every other outstanding request. While in the critical section a process must prevent others from entering; on exit it must broadcast a release so others update their view.

Require the following correctness properties:
- Safety (mutual exclusion): at most one process may be in the critical section at any time.
- Progress liveness under fair delivery assumptions: a requesting process that continues to send/receive messages and whose messages are eventually delivered should eventually enter the critical section provided no permanent crashes occur.
- Nonblocking acknowledgements: receiving a request eventually causes an acknowledgement to be sent (subject to fair scheduling).
- Logical clock monotonicity and message causality: clocks increase correctly so timestamps reflect causal order and are used consistently to compare requests.
- Channels are FIFO between each pair and bounded to keep model checking finite.

Do not commit to specific variable names, program text, or a particular coding of broadcast; model the protocol requirements and invariants abstractly.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines reusable TLA+ operators for adding an auxiliary stuttering variable `s` to an existing specification, as described in the paper "Auxiliary Variables in TLA+". It provides action transformers that wrap an existing subaction `A` with optional pre-stuttering or post-stuttering behavior, using a record-valued control variable `s` whose fields identify the action, its execution context, and a countdown value. The module also defines conditions ensuring that the decrement function driving stuttering eventually reaches a bottom element, including an alternative version intended to be easier for TLC to evaluate on finite models. The file contains no complete system spec of its own; rather, it is a library module meant to be instantiated by another specification, and it includes comments describing a modification that strengthens context checking during stuttering steps.
desc_intent: Model a system that augments an existing state-machine specification with controllable stuttering steps that may be inserted either before or after individual transitions. The model should treat the original system as a black box described by its state variables, an initial condition, and a next-state relation made up of alternative subactions. For any chosen subaction, the stuttering mechanism must be able to do the following: when enabled, optionally interpose a finite nonzero number of internal stuttering transitions before the subaction, or perform the subaction and then optionally interpose a finite nonzero number of internal stuttering transitions afterward. Each stuttering run must be parametrized by a stutter counter drawn from a well-founded, totally ordered domain with a specified minimum; each stuttering transition decrements the counter according to a specified function and stops when the minimum is reached. The stuttering augmentation must preserve the original observable behavior when the stuttering counter is at its sentinel value (i.e., not stuttering), must not change original state variables except during the concrete subaction or during stuttering steps that are explicitly allowed to leave them unchanged, and must ensure that concurrent execution of other subactions cannot corrupt the intended stuttering run (the stuttering context must be matched). Specify the invariant ensuring every counter sequence reaches the minimum (no infinite stuttering), and require that the augmented system refines the original specification (trace inclusion of observable variables) and maintains safety and liveness properties of the original when stuttering is ignored.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a TLAPS proof layer for a spanning-tree protocol specification imported from the module spanning. It proves the safety property `Spec => []SntMsg`, where `SntMsg` states that a non-root process whose parent is not yet set has sent no messages. The proof strengthens the invariant with `SentMeansCanSend` and `PrntDomain`, then shows the combined invariant is inductive over `[Next]_vars`; comments also note a design issue in the imported spec's `TypeOK` regarding non-symmetric neighbor relations, so this proof avoids relying on that invariant.
desc_intent:
Model a distributed spanning-tree construction protocol running on a fixed set of processes with a distinguished root. The system maintains for each process a parent reference (which may be unset), a directed set of outstanding messages between ordered pairs of processes, and local information needed to propose parent assignments and send messages. The protocol must allow a process to send messages only when permitted by the protocol’s send predicate; messages are asynchronous and represented as pairs indicating sender and recipient. A process whose parent is not yet set must not be allowed to originate any outgoing message unless it is the root. When a process receives a message from another process, it may adopt that sender as its parent (if its parent is unset), and adoption must set the parent to a concrete process identifier (not to the sentinel meaning “no parent”). The model should permit actions that leave state unchanged, allow message sends that add a new ordered pair to the message set, and allow parent updates that modify only that process’s parent. Specify initial states, safety properties, and the state-transition relation at an abstract level (not implementation code).

Key correctness properties to guarantee:
- Safety: At all reachable states, every message in the message set was sent by either the root or by a process whose parent is already set (i.e., non-root processes with unset parents have sent no messages).
- Domain: The parent mapping is always defined for every process and any assigned parent is a valid process identifier (not the “no parent” sentinel when set).
- Inductiveness: The invariants above must be preserved by all protocol actions (sending, parent update, and stuttering/idle steps).

Also specify types and a precise state space so the invariants can be mechanically checked and proved.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a distributed spanning-tree construction over a graph of processes, where processes communicate by recording sent messages in a shared set and adopt a parent when they receive a message. Initially every process has no parent, no process has reported, and no messages have been sent; a process may send to a neighbor if it is the root or it already has a parent, and an unparented non-root process may adopt as parent a sender from which it has received a message. The specification includes a weak fairness condition for the main step relation, a type correctness invariant, a termination property asserting eventual parent assignment for all non-root processes, and a safety-style property stating that once a parent is assigned it never changes.
desc_intent: Specify a protocol that constructs a spanning tree rooted at a designated root process in a connected undirected network of processes. Model each process as an asynchronous agent that can send point-to-point messages along existing network links and can record a chosen parent. The system must start with no parent assignments and no sent messages. Only the root or a process that already has a parent may send a message over a link. When a process without a parent receives a message from a neighbor, it may adopt that neighbor as its parent. Once a process adopts a parent, it must record that fact and may no longer be in the unparented state. Messages may be sent repeatedly but self-consistency of parent choices must be preserved with respect to the network topology (a chosen parent must be a neighbor). The specification should guarantee eventual termination: eventually every non-root process has selected a parent that is one of its neighbors. Key safety properties: (1) parent pointers are always either a special “no parent” value or a neighbor; (2) once a process has a parent, that stored parent value persists (no spontaneous change); (3) no process other than the root ever sends messages while it remains unparented. Key liveness property: every non-root process eventually becomes parented. Also require a type invariant for messages (messages are pairs of processes) and for parent and acknowledgement status. Do not prescribe message delivery ordering or timing beyond eventual progress assumptions sufficient to ensure termination.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies and proves a simple arithmetic fact over natural numbers: for every natural number x, the sum x+x is even. It defines predicates Even and Odd in terms of the remainder modulo 2, then states the target theorem both directly and as a named theorem T1. The file contains TLAPS proofs, including a one-step proof using Z3 and a more explicit stepwise proof by case distinction on whether x is even or odd.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of arithmetic parity for natural numbers and prove that doubling any natural number yields an even number. The model should include the domain of natural numbers and a formal definition of "even" and "odd" based purely on remainder modulo 2. It must express the property that for every natural number n, the sum n + n is even. The specification should state this as a universal correctness property and provide the logical facts needed to prove it: (a) every natural number is either even or odd, (b) parity arithmetic rules for addition modulo 2, and (c) closure of the operations within the naturals. The proof obligations should be structured so an automated SMT or decision procedure can discharge the main theorem, but the specification must also support a hand-checkable case-splitting proof distinguishing even and odd cases. Do not prescribe a particular proof tool or algorithm; instead require the model to be amenable both to automated solvers and to manual case reasoning. Finally, include lemmas that relate remainder properties to sums (for example, how remainders of summands compose under addition modulo 2) and state as the main invariant that doubling preserves evenness for all naturals.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module models an abstract two-peer TCP finite state machine based on RFC 9293, focusing on connection-state transitions rather than low-level protocol details such as sequence numbers. It represents per-peer TCP control block existence, per-peer connection state, and in-flight network messages as sequences, and models user-triggered actions, protocol-driven state transitions, and reset behavior. The specification checks a state invariant about agreement on the ESTABLISHED state when no messages are in flight, and a liveness property that a peer in SYN-SENT eventually reaches ESTABLISHED, LISTEN, or CLOSED. The design explicitly includes RFC note-inspired transitions such as the FIN-WAIT-1 to TIME-WAIT shortcut and a reset action applicable broadly across states, and it adds weak fairness both for system steps and for a specific user close action to avoid getting stuck in SYN-SENT.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of the TCP connection state machine (as used for a single TCP connection between two peers) that captures connection establishment, data-termination handshake, and abnormal reset behavior. The model must represent two endpoints that exchange discrete control messages (SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK, FIN, ACK-of-FIN, RST) over an unreliable FIFO-like channel per direction, allowing messages to be in flight and to be delivered, consumed, or cause state transitions. Represent endpoint control blocks (existence of a TCB) and the standard TCP finite states: CLOSED, LISTEN, SYN-SENT, SYN-RECEIVED, ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSING, CLOSE-WAIT, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT. The model should allow user-initiated operations (active open, passive open, send that triggers a SYN, and close) and spontaneous network-triggered events (receipt of the above messages), as well as sending RSTs according to the protocol's intent.

Required correctness properties:
- Safety: if neither direction has in-flight messages and one endpoint is ESTABLISHED, the other must also be ESTABLISHED.
- Progress/liveness: an endpoint that begins an active open should eventually reach one of the terminal/steady states appropriate for establishment (ESTABLISHED or a state denoting failure such as CLOSED or LISTEN), assuming fair scheduling of user actions and network deliveries.
- Proper termination: after orderly close sequences, both endpoints should eventually delete their TCBs and reach CLOSED (TIME-WAIT must eventually transition to CLOSED for endpoints that enter it).
- RST semantics: receipt of RST should move an endpoint to LISTEN or CLOSED as appropriate; peers may send RSTs from states that justify abortive close and transition to TIME-WAIT as per the RFC rationale.

Abstract away sequence numbers and payload data; model only control-message semantics, TCB existence, state transitions, and in-flight message queues.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a recursive bitwise AND operation over integers and introduces an infix operator `&` as a wrapper around that recursive definition. The implementation is intended to be used with a Java operator override in TLC, as explained by the comments, and the comments also document the expected TLC behavior when the override is present or missing. The specification is not a transition-system model with variables or temporal properties; instead, it provides a mathematical/operator-level definition of bitwise conjunction using arithmetic decomposition by powers of two.
desc_intent:
Specify a system that models the bitwise AND operation on nonnegative integers and verifies its expected algebraic and bit-level properties. The model should treat integers as sequences of bits (infinite or sufficiently large finite width) and define bitwise AND as combining corresponding bit positions with logical conjunction. It must accept arbitrary nonnegative integers as inputs and produce an output integer whose binary representation has a 1 in a given position exactly when both inputs have a 1 in that position.

The specification must state and verify these correctness requirements:
- Bit correspondence: for every bit index i, the i-th bit of the result equals the logical AND of the i-th bits of the two inputs.
- Commutativity: a & b = b & a.
- Associativity: (a & b) & c = a & (b & c).
- Identity element for all-ones mask of sufficient width: a & allOnes = a, when allOnes has ones in every bit position considered.
- Monotonicity with respect to bitwise inclusion: if bits(a) ⊆ bits(b) then a & c ⊆ b & c (interpreted per-bit).
- Bound and zero behavior: a & 0 = 0; result ≤ min(a, b).
- Decomposition: the value equals the sum over bit positions of 2^i times the bitwise conjunction at i.

Additionally, include properties to ensure the model handles finite-width representations consistently (specify width or semantics for higher bits) and supports reasoning about division, modulo, and shifting operations used to extract bits.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models the Tower of Hanoi puzzle using three towers represented as sequences of natural numbers, where each number denotes a disk size. The initial contents of the three towers are provided by the constants A, B, and C, and the state variable towers stores the current configuration as a 3-tuple of sequences. The spec defines when a move is legal, how a move updates the towers, and a Next action that nondeterministically chooses a legal move. It also includes state invariants checking that the tower structure remains well-typed, that no new disk values are introduced, that the total number of disks remains constant, and a predicate NotSolved describing the negation of the solved configuration.
desc_intent:
Model the classic Tower of Hanoi puzzle as a state-machine over three pegs holding a finite set of distinct disks of different sizes. The system must start from an arbitrary initial distribution of the disks across the three pegs (with each peg’s contents given as an ordered stack, smallest represented by the smallest identifier), and allow only legally valid single-disk moves. A legal move picks the top disk from one peg and places it on the top of a different peg, with the constraint that a disk may be placed only on an empty peg or on a larger disk. Only one disk may move at a time.

Specify the state space, an initial state predicate capturing arbitrary initial stacks, and a next-state relation capturing all and only the above legal single-disk moves. Require invariants ensuring: the set of disks present on all pegs never changes (no new or lost disks), the total number of disks is constant, and the representation of each peg is always a well-formed ordered stack of disk sizes. Specify a liveness or reachability goal asserting that from the initial state there exists a sequence of legal moves that achieves a target configuration in which all disks reside on a designated peg in strictly increasing size order (smallest on top). Optionally allow specifying which peg is the destination and require termination when the goal is reached.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models the Towers of Hanoi puzzle with a parameterized number of disks D and towers N. Towers are encoded as natural numbers whose bit patterns represent which power-of-two disk values are present on each tower, and the actions move a smallest available disk from one tower to another when the destination permits it. The spec defines an initial state, a next-state relation over legal moves, a safety-style invariant about preservation of the total disk sum, a type condition over tower values, and a temporal specification Spec asserting Init /\ [][Next]_vars; it also defines NotSolved so TLC can search for a counterexample trace reaching the solved configuration.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of the generalized Tower of Hanoi puzzle with D disks and N pegs. The system state should represent which disks are located on which peg (no implementation detail of encoding required). Initially all disks are stacked on a single designated source peg in size order (largest at bottom, smallest at top). A step of the system moves exactly one disk from one peg to another under the standard legal-move constraints: a disk can be moved only if it is the topmost disk on its current peg, and it may be placed only on an empty peg or on top of a larger disk. Moves are atomic and preserve the total set of disks and their identities.

Model all possible sequences of legal moves (including sequences that do not make progress toward a goal). Specify the correctness properties to check:

- Invariance: the multiset of disks across all pegs is constant (no duplication or loss).
- Safety: every move respects the “topmost” and “no smaller-on-larger” constraints.
- Liveness / eventual reachability: there exists a sequence of moves that reaches the goal configuration in which all disks are stacked in order on a designated target peg, and provide a bound on the minimum number of moves needed (2^D - 1) as an expected optimal length.
- Optionally, state and check that when N < 3 the goal is unreachable for D > 1, and for N ≥ 3 the goal is reachable.

Do not prescribe a particular encoding of pegs or disks; focus on the abstract state, legal move relation, initial and goal states, and the properties above.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the TCommit protocol, specifically for the theorem that TCSpec implies that always (TCTypeOK and TCConsistent) hold. The proof is structured hierarchically and refers to definitions and operators from the TCommit module, as well as using the TLAPS proof system. The proof demonstrates that the invariant Inv (which is TCTypeOK and TCConsistent) is preserved by the protocol's initialization and next-state actions, and that the temporal property holds globally.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of a two-phase commit protocol for a distributed transaction coordinator and a fixed set of resource managers. The model should describe the allowed states of each participant, the coordinator’s decisions, and the two high-level actions: asking resource managers to prepare and then deciding to commit or abort. It must capture the safety-critical invariants that every state transition must preserve: (1) each resource manager’s state is always one of a small, well-defined set of protocol states (type safety); (2) no two resource managers can end up in conflicting terminal outcomes (for example, one committed while another aborted) — i.e., the protocol must maintain global consistency of final decisions; and (3) decisions to commit may occur only when all resource managers have signaled preparedness to commit, while aborts may be taken when any resource manager refuses to prepare. The model should allow for stuttering steps and for actions that leave the global state unchanged. The specification must express an initial condition and a next-state relation such that starting from the initial state, every reachable state satisfies the type-safety and global-consistency invariants at all times (safety property). Do not commit to any particular implementation mechanism (for example, avoid encoding a specific program loop or per-participant code); instead describe the abstract protocol behavior and the invariants to be proved over its state-transition relation.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module contains TLAPS proofs about a two-phase commit specification imported from the TwoPhase module. It proves that the temporal specification TPSpec implies the type correctness invariant TPTypeOK and also implies the safety property TC!TCConsistent, which states that no resource managers can end in conflicting committed and aborted decisions. To prove consistency, the module defines a strengthened inductive invariant Inv that tracks transaction manager state, prepared messages, decision messages on the wire, and the relationship between local RM states and messages, then proves the invariant is inductive and implies the target consistency theorem.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a two-phase commit protocol (one transaction manager coordinating several resource managers) and state its required safety properties.

Model a system with a single coordinator (transaction manager) and a fixed set of participants (resource managers). Participants can be in states like "working", "prepared", "committed", or "aborted". The coordinator can be in states like "init", "committed", or "aborted". Communication is asynchronous via a shared message set; messages include "Prepared(rm)", "Commit", and "Abort". Participants may send Prepared messages, receive Commit or Abort messages, or decide locally to abort. The coordinator decides to Commit only after it has knowledge that every participant is prepared; it decides to Abort otherwise, and then broadcasts the decision.

Require the model to guarantee these correctness properties:
- Type safety: all state variables and messages always conform to their declared types and domains.
- Consistency (agreement): it is impossible for one participant to end up committed while another ends up aborted in the same execution.
- Coordinator-decision fidelity: when the coordinator's state is "committed" (resp. "aborted"), a Commit (resp. Abort) message has been broadcast; when in "init", no decision messages have been broadcast.
- Prepared-message integrity: any participant listed as known prepared by the coordinator must have actually sent a Prepared message; any Prepared message in the message set implies the sender is not still "working".
- Commit prerequisites: a Commit message is broadcast only after every participant has sent Prepared.
- Abort characterization: if a participant is aborted, then either an Abort message was broadcast or that participant never sent a Prepared message.

Do not prescribe implementation details; leave nondeterminism for message delivery and the ordering of independent actions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple bounded FIFO queue of messages. The system starts with an empty sequence, allows sending a message from a fixed message range when the queue length is below a fixed size bound, and allows receiving by removing the head element when the queue is non-empty. The file is designed to stress TLC under anomalous conditions by generating a large state space, and it also states and checks a safety property that every element currently stored in the queue belongs to the allowed Messages set.
desc_intent:
Model a bounded FIFO message queue system used by a single producer and single consumer where the queue holds at most a fixed number of messages drawn from a fixed finite message set. The model should describe the abstract states of the queue (its contents as a sequence), and the two kinds of atomic operations that may change the state: an enqueue that appends a message to the tail if the queue is not full, and a dequeue that removes the head element if the queue is not empty. The specification must allow nondeterministic choices of which message to enqueue (from the finite set) and of when either operation occurs, but must never allow enqueues beyond the capacity or dequeues from an empty queue.

Formally state safety properties to be checked: (1) message integrity — every element in the queue is always a valid message from the allowed finite set, and (2) capacity safety — the queue length never exceeds the fixed capacity. Also require liveness properties expressing that whenever the queue is non-full and the environment continually attempts to enqueue, eventually an enqueue can occur, and whenever the queue is non-empty and the environment continually attempts to dequeue, eventually a dequeue can occur (i.e., no permanent starvation under continuous requests). Finally, allow checking for state-space explosion behavior by making the message set and capacity parameters adjustable so that experiments can measure memory, disk, and handle usage of the model checker.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a simple message-shuffling system with four constant message values M0 through M3. The system maintains a set of messages on the left, a set on the right, an iteration counter, and a send count; a Send step moves one message from left to right and increments count, while an Iteration step is enabled when left is empty and moves all right-side messages back to left while incrementing the iteration number. The temporal specification asserts initialization followed by arbitrary Next steps, and the file also defines an invariant stating that the union of left and right always equals the full Messages set, together with a temporal property [] Inv. The design also includes symmetry-related helper definitions using Permutations(Messages), a fixed iteration definition, and a view tuple.
desc_intent:
Specify a system that models a two-stage message transfer process between two buffers over a fixed number of rounds. The system maintains a multiset-like collection of distinct messages initially all placed in the first buffer and an empty second buffer. Repeatedly, individual messages may be moved atomically from the first buffer to the second buffer until the first buffer is empty; when the first buffer becomes empty, the contents of the second buffer are swapped to become the new first buffer and the second buffer is reset to empty, and a round counter increments. The system runs for a predetermined number of rounds and then stops making progress.

Formalize the state as the two buffers and a round counter plus a global message-transfer counter. Require that only messages from the initial finite set may ever appear in either buffer and that no message is duplicated or lost: at every state the union of the two buffers equals the original set of messages. Ensure individual moves transfer exactly one message from the first buffer to the second and increment the transfer counter; ensure the swapping transition occurs only when the first buffer is empty and increments the round counter. Specify safety properties (invariant that the multiset of messages is preserved, and that no duplicates are introduced) and liveness properties (eventual completion of each round and termination after the given number of rounds). Allow reasoning about symmetry under permutations of message identifiers.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module models heaps, objects, and promise-like objects in an object-capability style setting, including resolved and unresolved promises and actions that resolve or garbage-collect them. It defines the shape of objects, heaps, eventuals, promises, and heap well-formedness conditions such as absence of dangling pointers and acyclicity of promise chains, and it assumes semantic properties of an abstract method evaluator Eval. The file contains state-level structure definitions and three heap-updating actions for resolving when-promises, resolving non-when-promises, and garbage collecting resolved promises, but it does not define a full temporal specification or liveness/fairness properties.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a heap-based promise (future) system with garbage collection, where objects live at heap addresses and may contain fields that are values, object references, or sequences thereof. The system must support promises that can be unresolved or resolved; unresolved promises encode either a “when” continuation that waits on another promise’s resolution or a normal continuation that waits on the identity of an object (itself represented by a promise). When a promise becomes ready to be resolved, its associated continuation (a method) is executed using the heap and the resolved input; the continuation produces a result (a value or an object id) and may update the heap. Resolution updates the promise object to a resolved state with the produced value.

Model rules for: (1) when-style promises that fire when their argument promise resolves, invoking the continuation with that argument’s value; (2) non-when promises that fire when the object-id promise resolves, invoking the continuation with the resolved object identity; and (3) safe garbage collection of promises that are resolved and no longer reachable from any live object (reachability should treat promise-internal links specially so that promise links do not create spurious reachability).
