The module proves an inductive invariant capturing typing, the relation between flags and control locations, and mutual exclusion, and it also defines a refinement mapping to an abstract lock specification via an INSTANCE of Lock. In addition, it states a liveness property asserting that a process waiting at label a3 eventually reaches the critical section cs.
desc_declarative_claude:
Peterson's mutual-exclusion algorithm for two processes is specified here, taken from a parallel-programming course. Two processes, numbered 1 and 2, share a boolean array `c` (indicating intent to enter the critical section) and an integer `turn` (indicating whose turn it is). Each process cycles through labels `a0` through `a4` and `cs`: it signals intent (`a1`), yields the turn to the other process (`a2`), waits until the other process is not interested or the turn is its own (`a3`), executes the critical section (`cs`), and then clears its intent flag (`a4`). The specification `Spec` is the initial condition `Init` combined with the always-enabled stuttering next-state relation `[][Next]_vars`.

The module defines `TypeOK` as a type-correctness invariant and `Inv` as an inductive invariant with three conjuncts: `c[p]` is true exactly when process `p` is at labels `a2` through `a4`, any process in the critical section or releasing it either holds the turn or the other process is still in the acquiring phase, and mutual exclusion holds (no two processes are simultaneously in `cs` or `a4`). TLAPS proofs establish that `TypeOK` is always satisfied, that `Inv` is inductive, and that `Peterson` refines an abstract `Lock` module via a state mapping (`pc_translation` and `lock_translation`), confirming that the concrete algorithm correctly implements the abstract lock specification `LSpec`.
desc_intent: Specify Peterson's mutual-exclusion algorithm for two processes. Two processes compete to enter a critical section, coordinated by a shared turn variable and a pair of Boolean flags indicating each process's intent to enter. Each process repeatedly: signals its intent, yields the turn to the other process, waits until either the other process is not interested or the turn belongs to it, executes the critical section, then retracts its intent. The specification must satisfy two correctness properties. First, mutual exclusion: at most one process may be in the critical section at any time. Second, the algorithm must refine an abstract lock specification, meaning the concrete protocol correctly implements the higher-level notion of acquiring and releasing a lock. An inductive invariant should be provided and proved: it captures the relationship between each process's flag and its program location, and the condition that any process in the critical section either holds the turn or the other process has not yet signaled intent. Both the inductive invariant and the refinement mapping to the abstract lock must be formally verified using TLAPS.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the non-blocking atomic commitment (NBAC) algorithm with crash failures, based on Raynal 1997, using a TLA+ encoding. The system models processes that vote YES or NO, exchange messages, may crash, and observe a local failure detector that can nondeterministically report whether some process has crashed. The specification defines initialization, per-process steps combining message receipt, failure detector updates, and local transitions, and verifies structural properties such as type correctness and a validity condition relating unanimous YES votes to possible commit outcomes.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies the Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment (NBAC) protocol with crash failures, based on Raynal's 1997 algorithm. It models N processes (parameterized by the constant N) that must reach a commit or abort decision in a distributed system where processes may crash.

Each process has a program counter (`pc`) ranging over states `"YES"`, `"NO"`, `"SENT"`, `"ABORT"`, `"COMMIT"`, and `"CRASH"`. Supporting variables track the global set of sent messages (`sent`), each process's received messages (`rcvd`), and a per-process failure detector flag (`fd`) that nondeterministically reports whether any process has crashed.

Initially, each process votes either YES or NO (or all YES under `InitAllYes`), with no messages sent or received. In each step, a process nondeterministically receives a subset of sent messages, updates its failure detector reading, and then takes one of several actions: broadcast its vote (`UponYes` or `UponNo`), transition to a decision state (`UponSent`), crash (`UponCrash`), or do nothing. The `UponSent` action commits only if the failure detector reports no crashes and YES messages have been received from all processes; otherwise it aborts.

The temporal specification `Spec` uses `Init` and the next-state relation `Next`, augmented with a weak fairness condition ensuring that non-crashed processes eventually send their votes and attempt decisions. The model is checked at `N = 2` with the `TypeOK` invariant enforcing well-typed state. The `Validity` property asserts that a commit decision is only possible when all processes initially voted YES.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of the Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment (NBAC) protocol for a distributed system of N processes that may crash, following Raynal's 1997 formulation. Each process begins with an initial vote of either YES or NO. Processes broadcast their vote and then decide to either COMMIT or ABORT based on what they receive and what a local failure detector reports. A process commits only if it has received YES votes from all processes and its failure detector reports no crashes; it aborts if it detects a crash or receives any NO vote. Processes may crash at any time, permanently. The failure detector at each process may nondeterministically report crashed or all-correct at any step. Message delivery is reliable but asynchronous: a process's received set grows monotonically as a subset of all sent messages.

The specification must enforce the following correctness properties: type safety across all variables, and validity — meaning that if any process commits, then all processes must have initially voted YES (equivalently, if any process voted NO, no process may commit). The system should be specified with weak fairness so that non-crashed processes that can vote or decide will eventually do so.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is an Apalache type-annotation wrapper around another TLA+ specification, introduced by an INSTANCE of nbacg_guer01 so that the original module remains unchanged. It declares the constant N and the state variables used by the wrapped protocol, including sent counters, received counters, failure flags, and a program-counter function pc. The file itself does not define the algorithm, transition relation, or temporal properties syntactically at the module top level.
desc_intent: Specify a TLA+ model of a synchronous round-based distributed agreement protocol for N processes that tolerates crash failures. The system repeatedly executes rounds in which each non-faulty process broadcasts a binary vote (Yes/No), receives votes from other processes, updates local counters recording how many Yes and No values it sent and received (including counts that reflect messages from crashed processes as failures), and decides when safety and liveness conditions allow termination. The model should capture that processes may crash (permanently stop participating) at arbitrary points, but the number of crashes is bounded by some f < N. Messages are delivered reliably within a round (no reordering across rounds) but a crashed sender may omit sending. The protocol must ensure agreement (no two non-faulty processes decide differently), validity (if all non-faulty processes start with the same input value then any decision equals that value), and termination (all non-faulty processes eventually decide despite up to f crashes). Specify counters and flags for sent/received Yes/No and for detected failures as part of the state abstraction, but do not prescribe a particular implementation. Include an invariant expressing that once a decision value is chosen by any non-faulty process, no other non-faulty process can decide the opposite. Also formalize progress: if the number of non-faulty processes exceeds a threshold sufficient for the protocol (e.g., >2f when required), then all non-faulty processes eventually decide.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a parameterized asynchronous non-blocking atomic commitment algorithm with failure detectors, based on the algorithm discussed in Guerraoui's paper on failure-sensitive agreement problems. The model tracks how processes initially vote YES or NO, may crash, may become suspected by a failure detector, send messages, receive messages, and eventually either abort or commit. It defines a transition system with weak fairness for non-stuttering process actions, specialized initial conditions where all processes vote YES or all vote NO, a type invariant, and temporal properties for agreement, abort validity, commit validity, termination, and eventual commit.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a parameterized, counter-abstraction model of the Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment (NBAC) algorithm with failure detectors, based on Guerraoui (2001). It models N processes (instantiated at 3) that each begin by voting YES or NO, then send their vote to all others, receive votes, and eventually decide to either COMMIT or ABORT.

Rather than tracking individual messages, the spec uses integer counters: `nSntYes` and `nSntNo` count votes sent by correct processes, while `nSntYesF` and `nSntNoF` bound votes that faulty (crashed) processes may have sent. Each process maintains per-process receive counters `nRcvdYes` and `nRcvdNo`. The `pc` array tracks each process's local state through the statuses YES, NO, SENT, ABORT, COMMIT, or BYZ (crashed). The `someFail` array represents a perfect failure detector: a process is suspected only if it truly crashes.

Key actions include `SendYes`/`SendNo` (a non-suspected process broadcasts its vote), `Receive` (a SENT process incrementally receives messages), `Commit` (a SENT process commits having received N YES votes and no NO votes), `AbortSent` (abort upon receiving any NO), `AbortNoYes` (a suspected process aborts before sending), and `Crash` (marking a process as BYZ and adjusting faulty-message bounds). Three specifications—`Spec`, `SpecYes`, and `SpecNo`—combine different initial conditions with weak fairness over all non-crash actions. The model checks a `TypeOK` invariant and four temporal properties: agreement (no two processes decide differently), abort validity (a NO vote prevents any commit), commit validity (unanimous YES with no suspicions prevents aborts), and termination (crash-free and suspicion-free runs eventually reach a decision).
desc_intent:
Specify a parameterized TLA+ model of the asynchronous Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment (NBAC) algorithm with failure detectors, for N processes. Each process initially votes either YES or NO. Correct processes broadcast their vote; faulty processes may crash at any time, potentially before or after sending their vote, and the failure detector reports (possibly prematurely) which processes are suspected. A process that has sent its vote then receives votes from others and decides to either COMMIT or ABORT. A process aborts immediately if it suspects any failure or receives any NO vote; it commits only if it receives YES from all N processes and no NO vote.

The specification must satisfy four correctness properties. Agreement: no two correct processes decide differently (one COMMIT and one ABORT must never coexist). Abort validity: if any process votes NO, no process ever commits. Commit validity: if all processes vote YES and none is suspected, no process aborts. Termination: if no process ever crashes and no process is ever suspected, every process eventually reaches a decision. Consider three initialization scenarios — arbitrary votes, all YES, all NO — and check all properties under weak fairness of non-crash actions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module provides Apalache-specific type annotations and concrete constant values for an underlying spanning-tree specification imported via INSTANCE spanning. It declares constants for a process set, distinguished root and no-parent values, and a neighbor relation, along with variables representing parent pointers, reporting flags, and messages. The file itself does not define the algorithm dynamics or temporal properties; instead, it supplies typed parameters and concrete sample values while keeping the original spanning specification separate.
desc_intent:
Model a distributed algorithm that constructs a spanning tree over a fixed undirected network of processes. The system should start with a designated root process and other processes with no parent. Processes communicate by exchanging messages along network links. The algorithm must elect parent pointers so that, when it stabilizes, every process except the root has a parent that is one of its neighbors, the root has no parent, and the parent pointers form a connected, acyclic structure (a tree) spanning exactly the set of processes. The protocol should tolerate asynchronous message delivery but assume reliable channels (no message loss or duplication). Processes may concurrently send and receive messages; they can update their parent choices based only on local state and messages from neighbors.

Specify liveness and safety properties: safety guarantees that no two processes will have parents that create a cycle and that every parent pointer is always a neighbor; once stabilized the parent relation is a spanning tree rooted at the designated root. Liveness guarantees eventual convergence: from any reachable state, the system eventually reaches a stable configuration in which no further parent changes occur and the spanning-tree property holds. Also require that messages eventually quiesce (no infinite message generation after stabilization). Describe initial conditions, permitted message types abstractly, and the correctness invariants above—do not prescribe a particular protocol implementation.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking wrapper around the imported module sums_even. It introduces a finite bound MaxNat and defines NatOverride == 0 .. MaxNat, together with assumptions that MaxNat is a natural number and that T1 holds. The file itself contains no state variables, actions, temporal specification, or proofs; it primarily constrains constants for checking the underlying imported specification.
desc_intent: Specify a concurrent system that repeatedly produces pairs of nonnegative integers and checks whether their sum is even, for all numbers in a bounded natural range. The system should allow multiple independent producers to generate pairs (x, y) where each value ranges over 0..Max, and each produced pair is submitted to a checker component. The checker must nondeterministically select pairs to verify and record whether the sum x + y is even. The system must guarantee safety: every recorded verification must correctly reflect the parity of the sum (i.e., be true iff the sum is even). It must also guarantee liveness: for any pair that is continuously offered for verification, the checker eventually examines and records it. The system should be able to run indefinitely, but values are bounded by the given Max value. Include an invariant that the checker never records an incorrect parity, and an eventuality property that every offered pair is eventually recorded. Model nondeterministic scheduling between producers and the checker and allow multiple outstanding unverified pairs. Do not commit to a particular implementation; state only the intended behaviors, constraints, and correctness properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a TCP specification imported from the `tcp` module. It introduces two peers and constrains the initial state so that one node starts in `"SYN-SENT"` after an active open while the other starts in `"LISTEN"` after a passive open, with an initial `"SYN"` segment in the network toward the listening side. It also defines additional state constraints that forbid retransmission by requiring adjacent network messages to differ, and forbid any further active opens, passive opens, or sends after the initial setup, reflecting a finite-state design choice suitable for TLC exploration.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a two-party TCP three-way handshake connection establishment between exactly two endpoints. Model the protocol behavior at the level of connection states, message transmission and delivery, and retransmission suppression, without committing to a particular implementation. The model should allow one endpoint to perform an active open and the other to do a passive open; the active endpoint initially sends a SYN and the passive endpoint initially listens and replies. The system must represent messages in transit and support non-deterministic message delivery and processing order, but must forbid duplicate identical adjacent messages in any single channel to model that retransmissions do not produce immediately repeated identical copies on the same link.

The model must ensure that after a finite sequence of message deliveries and appropriate local actions both endpoints reach the established connection state, provided the network does not permanently drop all required messages (i.e., liveness under fair delivery assumptions). It must guarantee safety properties: no endpoint transitions to the established state without the correct preceding handshake semantics (SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK), and no unexpected simultaneous multiple active open events occur beyond the initial scenario. Also require symmetry of the two peers so the specification is invariant under swapping their identities. Include invariants asserting valid per-endpoint TCP state progression, consistency of connection existence between peers, and absence of immediate duplicate messages on a channel.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a modified two-phase commit protocol with a transaction manager, multiple resource managers, and a backup transaction manager that can take over if the primary transaction manager becomes hidden after deciding. The resource managers move among working, prepared, committed, aborted, and failed states; the transaction manager decides commit or abort based on global conditions, and optional failures are controlled by the constants RMMAYFAIL and TMMAYFAIL. The spec defines the initial state, the next-state relation, weak fairness for all processes, an eventual termination property, and invariants for type correctness, consistency of decisions, and absence of committed resource managers in NotCommitted.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a fault-tolerant two-phase commit (2PC) protocol involving a set of resource managers (RM), a primary transaction manager (TManager), and a backup transaction manager (BTManager). The constants RM, RMMAYFAIL, and TMMAYFAIL control the participating RMs and whether failures are enabled; in the model configuration, RM has three members and both failure flags are TRUE.

Each resource manager progresses through states "working", "prepared", "committed", "aborted", or "failed", tracked in `rmState`. The transaction manager state `tmState` takes values "init", "commit", "abort", or "hidden". Resource managers may prepare, decide to commit or abort based on `tmState`, or fail (at most one RM may be in the failed state at a time). The primary TManager waits until either all RMs are prepared (or one has already committed) to issue a commit, or until some RM is aborted or failed (and none committed) to issue an abort; if TMMAYFAIL is TRUE, it then hides its decision by setting `tmState` to "hidden". The BTManager monitors for a hidden TManager decision and reissues the commit or abort, thereby recovering from TManager failure. All three process families run under weak fairness, ensuring that enabled actions are eventually taken. The temporal property Termination asserts that all processes eventually reach their done states.

The checked invariants are TypeOK (all state variables hold legal values) and Consistency (no two RMs ever reach conflicting commit and abort decisions simultaneously). The constant NotCommitted is defined but not listed as an invariant in the configuration.
desc_intent: Specify a two-phase commit protocol with a backup transaction manager. The system involves a configurable set of resource managers and a primary transaction manager, where both the resource managers and the primary transaction manager may optionally be configured to fail. Each resource manager begins in a working state and may prepare, decide to commit or abort based on the transaction manager's decision, or fail. The primary transaction manager monitors the resource managers and, once all are prepared (or one has already committed), issues a commit decision; if any has aborted or failed and none has committed, it issues an abort decision. After broadcasting its decision, the primary transaction manager may fail by hiding its state. A backup transaction manager watches for this failure and, if the primary's decision is hidden, re-issues the appropriate commit or abort decision so that resource managers can proceed. All three participant types must be modeled with fair scheduling. The key safety property is consistency: no two resource managers must ever reach conflicting decisions, meaning one must never commit while another aborts. The type correctness of all state variables must also be maintained as an invariant. The specification should also exhibit termination, guaranteeing that all processes eventually finish.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a thin wrapper around another specification, TCommit, adding Apalache type annotations and a concrete helper definition for the resource manager set. It declares a constant RM and a variable rmState, then instantiates TCommit without any explicit substitutions. The only top-level behavior defined locally is a concrete set RMVal containing three string identifiers, while the actual commit protocol logic and temporal properties are inherited from the instantiated module and therefore are not extracted here.
desc_intent:
Specify a distributed transaction commit coordinator and a set of resource managers participating in a two-phase commit-like protocol. The model should describe an arbitrary finite set of participants and a coordinator that drives commit or abort of a single transaction. It must allow participants to vote to commit or to abort and to transition through states such as initial, prepared, committed, and aborted. The coordinator may decide to commit only if all participants have prepared; otherwise it must abort. The system must tolerate asynchrony: messages between coordinator and participants may be delayed, duplicated, or lost, but not corrupted. Participants must be able to recover after crashes by using persisted state to reach a consistent final decision. The specification should capture message exchanges for prepare, vote, commit, and abort, and the possibility of timeouts that cause the coordinator or participants to take recovery actions.

Key correctness properties to guarantee:
- Safety: No two participants reach conflicting terminal decisions — once any participant commits, no participant may abort the transaction; once any participant aborts, no participant may commit.
- Agreement: All non-faulty participants eventually decide on the same outcome (commit or abort) in executions without indefinite message loss.
- Validity: Commit is decided only if every participant voted to commit; if any participant voted abort then abort is decided.
- Termination/Liveness under fairness conditions: If messages are eventually delivered and parties eventually recover, the protocol reaches a terminal state where every non-crashed participant has decided.

Do not prescribe a particular implementation detail such as exact message buffering or timeout values; specify the abstract states, message types, allowed transitions, and the above invariants and liveness requirements.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models the Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol for distributed transactions, focusing on the behavior of resource managers (RMs) as they transition through various states: working, prepared, committed, and aborted. The model defines the possible actions each RM can take (Prepare and Decide), and specifies the protocol's next-state relation as the disjunction of these actions for all RMs. The specification asserts type correctness and consistency invariants, ensuring that no two RMs can reach conflicting decisions (i.e., one committed and one aborted), and verifies these invariants as properties of the protocol. The model does not explicitly include faults or failures beyond the abort/commit logic, and does not model a coordinator or message passing.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a simplified, single-node view of the Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol for a set of resource managers (RMs). The constant `RM` names the participating resource managers, and the single variable `rmState` is a function mapping each RM to one of four states: `"working"`, `"prepared"`, `"committed"`, or `"aborted"`.

Initially every RM is in the `"working"` state. Each RM may take one of two actions: `Prepare` transitions it from `"working"` to `"prepared"`, while `Decide` allows it either to commit (moving from `"prepared"` to `"committed"`, but only when all RMs are already prepared or committed) or to abort (moving from `"working"` or `"prepared"` to `"aborted"`, but only when no RM has yet committed). The overall next-state relation requires that some RM performs one of these two actions. The temporal specification `TCSpec` is the initial condition conjoined with a stuttering-tolerant always-`TCNext` formula, with no fairness requirements. The model-checking configuration instantiates `RM` as the three-element set `{r1, r2, r3}` and checks two invariants: `TCTypeOK`, asserting that `rmState` remains a well-typed function into the four allowed states, and `TCConsistent`, asserting that no two RMs ever reach conflicting decisions—that is, no RM is aborted while another is committed. Deadlock checking is disabled.
desc_intent: Specify a simple single-phase atomic commit protocol for a fixed set of resource managers. Each resource manager begins in a working state and may independently prepare (signaling readiness to commit) or abort at any time before a final decision is reached. A prepared resource manager may commit only once all resource managers have reached at least the prepared state. The system must satisfy two key safety invariants: type correctness (every resource manager is always in one of the four states: working, prepared, committed, or aborted), and consistency (no two resource managers ever reach conflicting decisions, meaning it is impossible for one to have committed while another has aborted). There is no liveness requirement; deadlock freedom need not be checked. The protocol should be verified with three concrete resource managers.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models the Two-Phase Commit protocol, where a transaction manager (TM) coordinates a set of resource managers (RMs) to implement atomic transaction commit. The protocol is simplified: RMs spontaneously issue 'Prepared' messages, and 'Prepare' messages from the TM to RMs are ignored. Additionally, 'Abort' messages from RMs to the TM are omitted; instead, the TM may spontaneously decide to abort. The model focuses exclusively on safety properties, specifying what is allowed to happen, and omits liveness properties. Communication is modeled by a set of sent messages, with no message loss or removal, and the protocol's type correctness and implementation of a higher-level transaction commit specification are verified.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies the Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol, in which a single transaction manager (TM) coordinates a set of resource managers (RM) to reach a consistent commit or abort decision. The constant RM is the set of participating resource managers, instantiated in the model as {r1, r2, r3}.

The state is tracked by four variables: `rmState`, a function mapping each RM to one of `"working"`, `"prepared"`, `"committed"`, or `"aborted"`; `tmState`, the TM's state drawn from `{"init", "committed", "aborted"}`; `tmPrepared`, the set of RMs from which the TM has received Prepared messages; and `msgs`, the monotonically growing set of all messages ever sent. Messages are either per-RM `"Prepared"` messages sent from an RM to the TM, or broadcast `"Commit"` or `"Abort"` messages sent by the TM.

The TM actions are: receiving a Prepared message from an RM (adding it to `tmPrepared`), committing once all RMs have prepared (broadcasting a Commit message), and spontaneously aborting (broadcasting an Abort message). The RM actions are: preparing (sending a Prepared message), spontaneously choosing to abort without messaging, receiving and acting on a Commit message, and receiving and acting on an Abort message. The specification `TPSpec` is the initial condition conjoined with the always-enabled stuttering-closed next-state relation. Only safety is specified; no fairness or liveness properties are included. The module asserts two theorems: that `TPTypeOK` is an invariant, and that `TPSpec` implements the abstract Transaction Commit specification from module `TCommit`.
desc_intent:
Specify the Two-Phase Commit protocol in TLA+. A single transaction manager (TM) coordinates a fixed set of resource managers (RMs) to reach a consistent commit-or-abort decision. Each RM begins in a working state and may either prepare (signaling readiness to commit) or spontaneously choose to abort. The TM collects Prepared messages from RMs; once it has heard from all of them it may broadcast a Commit decision, or at any point while still in its initial state it may spontaneously broadcast an Abort decision. Upon receiving the TM's broadcast, each RM moves to the corresponding committed or aborted state. Model message passing as a grow-only set of sent messages, so receiving a message is equivalent to that message existing in the set.

The key safety invariant is type correctness: RM states are drawn from a fixed four-value set, the TM state from a three-value set, and all messages conform to their expected structure. Beyond type safety, the specification must implement the Transaction Commit correctness condition: no two RMs ever reach different final decisions, and an RM may only commit if every RM has prepared. The specification covers safety only; no liveness properties are required.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module appears to be a minimal or test TLA+ specification, likely auto-generated or used for model checking infrastructure. It defines a constant set containing the numbers 1 and 2, and a constant expression using a function ExprOfMaxLen with argument 3. There is an ASSUME block that prints a tuple containing a string literal and the previously defined constant expression. The module extends RemoveRedundantParens and TLC, suggesting it is intended for use with the TLC model checker. No temporal properties, state variables, or algorithmic behaviors are specified.
desc_intent:
Model a nondeterministic generator and evaluator of short expressions over a fixed small domain. The system should repeatedly construct expressions up to a bounded syntactic depth and then evaluate them to produce values in a known finite set. Requirements:

- The expression language: allow a finite set of atomic values and a set of compositional operators that produce new expressions; the maximal expression size is a given constant bound. The generative process must be able to produce any syntactically valid expression up to that bound.

- The evaluation semantics: provide a deterministic evaluation mapping from expressions to values in the finite domain. Evaluation must be total for all generated expressions (no runtime errors or undefined results).

- The control behavior: repeatedly choose an expression to evaluate; choices may be nondeterministic but must respect the size bound. The system may log or report each expression together with its evaluated value.

- Correctness properties to verify:
  - Coverage: every syntactically valid expression of size ≤ bound is reachable by some execution.
  - Type/Domain safety: every evaluation result belongs to the specified finite set of values.
  - Determinism of evaluation: evaluating the same expression always yields the same value.
  - Termination of each evaluation step: evaluation of any expression completes in finitely many steps.

- Parameters: the finite domain of values and the size bound should be model parameters so different instances can be checked.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a very small TLC-oriented wrapper that defines a constant expression checking whether `ObjSeq1` satisfies `IsTPSpec`, and then issues an `ASSUME` that prints a tuple containing a marker string and that computed value. It does not define any state variables, transition actions, initialization predicate, or temporal specification of a system execution. The file appears to be a model-evaluation helper module rather than a full algorithm specification, and it relies on definitions imported from extended modules rather than introducing its own system behavior.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a system that evaluates and tracks the validity of a constant expression against a known specification predicate. The model should represent a set of constant expressions (including complex structured expressions), a designated target predicate that determines whether a candidate expression satisfies the intended specification, and a verification check that asserts membership of each candidate in the set of expressions that meet the predicate.

The system must accept a finite collection of constant expressions as inputs, compute which of them satisfy the target predicate, and produce a report that pairs each expression with a boolean result indicating success or failure of the predicate check. The model must allow the target predicate itself to be an abstract, configurable condition so that different specifications can be substituted without changing the rest of the model.

Require invariants expressing that (1) every reported success corresponds to an expression that truly satisfies the predicate, (2) no expression that satisfies the predicate is reported as failure, and (3) the reporting function is total over the input collection (i.e., every input expression gets a result). Additionally, require a safety property forbidding any false positives and a liveness property ensuring that every input eventually receives a result. Include the ability to assume or print a combined diagnostic value containing a fixed string and the boolean verification outcome for model-checking and debugging.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the mapping between TLA+ and PlusCal (PCal) code regions, focusing on the syntactic correspondence between regions in the TLA+ specification and their representation in PlusCal. It defines data structures for locations, regions, and translation objects (TPObject), and provides predicates to check well-formedness and ordering of these objects in sequences. The specification includes detailed invariants for matching parentheses, token ordering, and the structure of translation sequences, supporting the correctness of TLA-to-PlusCal translation tools. The design is intended for use in debugging and verifying translation mappings, with additional constructs for simplified debugging scenarios.
desc_intent: Specify a formal model of a mapping between regions of a source specification language and regions of generated code. The model should represent a linear sequence of annotated elements that mark (a) delimiters that open and close nested source-language syntactic units, (b) tokens that identify specific source-language regions considered "important", and (c) explicit separators that indicate non-adjacent successive units. The system must enforce that delimiters are properly nested and balanced, that token regions appear in strictly increasing source order, and that the matching open/close delimiters enclose tokens and other delimiters consistently with nesting depth. When two top-level sibling syntactic units are intended to be successive in the generated code, they must be considered adjacent unless an explicit separator appears between their enclosing delimiters; such separators carry a numeric nesting-level that indicates how many surrounding syntactic levels are involved in the non-adjacency. The model must relate nesting depth to where separators are allowed and ensure separators only occur between a closing and a following opening delimiter. Key correctness properties to guarantee: well-formedness (non-empty sequence, starts and ends with delimiters, no negative nesting depth, final depth zero), tokens strictly ordered by source location, correct matching of delimiters (each open matches a unique later close and enclosing locations are non-decreasing), and that separators only appear at syntactically valid positions with an appropriate depth annotation. Additionally, state invariants expressing that within any matched pair, all immediate top-level child pairs are ordered and, if not adjacent, separated by a separator whose depth reflects their enclosing context.
