desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies and model checks a fast mutual exclusion algorithm for N processes, originally written in PlusCal and translated to TLA+. Each process repeatedly tries to enter a critical section using shared variables x, y, and an array b of intent flags, together with local state j and failed to coordinate retries and detect failed attempts. The specification defines the initial state, individual control-location actions, a global Next action, a standard temporal Spec with weak fairness for every process action, a mutual exclusion invariant, and a liveness property asserting that some process enters the critical section infinitely often.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies Lamport's Fast Mutual Exclusion algorithm for N processes (numbered 1 to N), where N is a natural-number constant instantiated at 2 in the model-checking configuration.

Each process runs an infinite loop attempting to enter a critical section using three shared variables: `x` (last writer of a "claim" register), `y` (a "winner" register initialized to 0), and `b`, a Boolean array of N flags indicating whether each process is competing. Each process also has local variables `j` (a loop counter) and `failed` (a flag indicating it lost the race). The protocol proceeds in labeled steps: a process raises its flag and writes its identity to `x`; if `y` is nonzero it backs off and waits for `y` to clear; otherwise it writes `y` and checks whether `x` still holds its identity. If not, it clears its flag and waits for all other flags to drop, then checks whether `y` still belongs to it; if not, it waits for `y` to be zero and marks itself as failed. A process that did not fail enters the critical section, then clears `y` and its flag before looping. The temporal specification `Spec` includes weak fairness for every process. The safety invariant `Invariant` asserts mutual exclusion: no two distinct processes are simultaneously in the critical section with `failed` false. The liveness property `Liveness` requires that some process is repeatedly in the critical section. The model also tracks, via TLC postconditions, that exactly 292 reachable states satisfy `SomeoneInCS` and 16 satisfy `Contention`.
desc_intent: Write a TLA+ specification for Lamport's Fast Mutex algorithm for N processes competing for a critical section. Each process repeatedly attempts to acquire the lock using two shared registers and an array of per-process flags. The entry protocol works in two phases: a process first announces its interest and writes its identity to a shared variable, then checks a second shared variable to decide whether to proceed directly or fall back to a waiting loop. If the fast path is taken but another process may have interfered, the process clears its flag, waits until every other process's flag is clear, then checks whether it still holds the second shared variable; if not, it waits for the second variable to become zero before retrying. Only one process may occupy the critical section at a time. After completing the critical section, the process clears the shared coordination state and its flag before restarting. The key safety property is mutual exclusion: no two processes may be in the critical section simultaneously. The liveness property is that some process must infinitely often succeed in entering the critical section. The model should be checked with weak fairness for each process and instantiated with a small concrete value of N.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies Fischer's timed mutual exclusion algorithm for N synchronizing processes, together with a separate ticking process that decrements per-process timers. The specification is written as a PlusCal algorithm with an included TLA+ translation, and it models timing using constants Delta and Epsilon plus a large sentinel value Infinity. It checks a mutual exclusion invariant, states a liveness property saying that some process is infinitely often in the critical section, and includes a TLC-based check of named state counts. The comments explicitly note that a bug should be found when N > 1 and Delta >= Epsilon, highlighting the timing-sensitive design of the algorithm.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies Fischer's real-time mutual exclusion algorithm for N processes, translated from PlusCal into TLA+. The algorithm uses a shared variable `x` (initially 0) and a per-process countdown timer array to coordinate entry into a critical section.

Each of the N processes (indexed 1..N) loops through labels a–f: it waits until `x` is zero (label c), sets its timer to `Delta` and writes its own identity into `x` (label d), then sets its timer to `Epsilon` and waits until that timer expires (label e). After the timer reaches zero, the process re-checks whether `x` still equals itself (label b); if so, it enters the critical section (`cs`) and resets `x` to 0 on exit (label f). A separate Tick process (process 0) decrements all finite timers by one in a single atomic step, but only when every timer is strictly positive. Constants `Delta` and `Epsilon` represent timing delays; correctness requires `Delta < Epsilon`. The specification uses weak fairness on every process and on Tick.

The checked invariant `Invariant` asserts mutual exclusion — no two distinct processes are simultaneously in the critical section. The liveness property `Liveness` requires that some process is in the critical section infinitely often. The config instantiates N=3, Delta=2, Epsilon=3, and a postcondition verifies exact TLC state-count statistics for `SomeInCS` and `ClaimLock`, flagging that a violation is expected when Delta ≥ Epsilon.
desc_intent: Specify Fischer's mutual exclusion algorithm for N timed processes sharing a single integer variable used as a lock. Each process repeatedly attempts to enter a critical section by first waiting until the shared variable is zero, then setting a local timer to a delay Delta and writing its own identifier into the shared variable, then resetting the timer to a smaller delay Epsilon and waiting for that timer to expire before re-checking that the shared variable still holds its identifier. A separate global clock process decrements all active timers by one each step, but only when every timer is strictly positive. The key timing parameters are Delta and Epsilon: mutual exclusion is guaranteed only when Delta is strictly less than Epsilon, and a violation should be detectable when Delta is greater than or equal to Epsilon with more than one process. The safety property to verify is mutual exclusion: no two distinct processes may be in the critical section simultaneously. The liveness property to verify is that some process enters the critical section infinitely often. Fairness must be assumed for all processes and the clock.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a regression test for a PlusCal translation issue involving a top-level comma inside an INSTANCE ... WITH clause located in a PlusCal define block. The translated specification models a trivial one-step algorithm with a program counter pc and a variable x, where the single step assigns x to Inner!Sum from an instantiated module and then moves pc to "Done". The temporal behavior is captured by an initial condition, a Next action consisting of the Step action or terminating stuttering, a standard safety-style specification [][Next]_vars, and a liveness property asserting eventual termination.
desc_intent:
Specify a model of a simple program that initializes a numeric state and then performs a single computation by calling a reusable component to obtain a value. The system should represent two distinct phases: initialization and a single computation step that uses the component's result to update the program state, after which the program terminates (but the model should allow stuttering after termination to avoid deadlock). The reusable component should be treated as an external module instance that supplies a deterministic numeric result computed from parameters or constants supplied at instantiation time; the main program must invoke that component and incorporate its result into its state update.

Requirements:
- The model must initialize the program state to a known integer value and start in a state ready to perform the computation step.
- During the single computation step, the program must obtain the component's numeric output and assign that value to the program state, then transition to a terminated control state.
- After termination, the system may stutter indefinitely without changing state.
- The component's output must be parameterizable by fixed constants provided at instantiation, and the overall system must allow reasoning about the final possible values of the state given those parameters.

Correctness properties to verify:
- Safety: the program's state after the computation is one of the expected numeric values determined by the component and its parameters.
- Liveness: the program eventually reaches the terminated control state (the computation step occurs).
- No unexpected state changes occur after termination (stuttering only).

Model the system abstractly without prescribing an implementation of the component beyond its deterministic numeric result and its instantiation parameters.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a small PlusCal program with one fair process that calls two procedures in sequence: an addition procedure and a procedure that converts the resulting integer to a string. The translated TLA+ specification represents procedure calls explicitly using program counters, per-process local-variable functions, and a stack of activation records used to emulate procedure return behavior. It verifies both termination-style liveness properties and fairness-based progress, and it includes assertions that the integer passed to the string conversion is 10 and that the final output string is "10".
desc_declarative_claude:
A small PlusCal/TLA+ playground module that models a single-process sequential computation using two procedures with simulated return values. The system has one process (`main`, process id 1) and two procedures, `add` and `to_string`, whose results are communicated back via the shared global variable `retval`. A second global variable `output` holds the final result.

The process executes four labeled steps: it calls `add(3, 7)`, which stores `10` in `retval`; then calls `to_string(retval)`, which asserts its argument equals `10` and stores the string `"10"` in `retval`; then copies `retval` into `output`; and finally asserts that `output` equals `"10"`. Procedure calls are managed through an explicit stack variable, following PlusCal's standard translation. The specification includes weak fairness on the main process and both procedures, ensuring progress. The temporal property `Termination` (and the equivalent `Liveness` property checked by the model) requires that the process eventually reaches the `Done` state. The two embedded `Assert` calls serve as inline safety checks during model checking, verifying the intermediate and final values of the computation.
desc_intent: Write a TLA+ specification that demonstrates procedural composition with simulated return values in PlusCal. Model a single sequential process that calls two procedures in sequence: one that adds two integers and stores the result in a shared return-value variable, and another that converts an integer to its string representation (only needing to handle the specific value 10) and likewise stores the result. The process should call the addition procedure with arguments 3 and 7, pass the numeric result to the conversion procedure, store the final string result in an output variable, and assert that the output equals the string "10". The specification should guarantee liveness: the process must eventually reach a completed state. This is primarily a demonstration of how PlusCal procedures can fake return values through shared variables, and correctness is verified through runtime assertions confirming intermediate and final values are as expected.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a recursive quicksort algorithm over an array of length ArrayLen, modeled first in commented PlusCal and then as the generated TLA+ translation. The algorithm chooses a pivot nondeterministically within the current subarray and then nondeterministically replaces the array by a permutation that preserves elements outside the subarray and partitions the subarray so that all values at or before the pivot are less than or equal to all values after it. The translated model uses explicit control state pc together with a stack of procedure frames to represent recursive calls to QS. The specification defines Init, Next, and Spec with weak fairness on Next, and it asserts a termination property stating that eventually pc reaches "Done". The final test state checks that the resulting array is a permutation of the initial array and is sorted in nondecreasing order.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a recursive quicksort algorithm operating on a finite integer array, expressed as a PlusCal algorithm that has been translated to TLA+. The constant `ArrayLen` determines the length of the array, which is also the range of its integer values.

The state consists of global variables `Ainit` (the initial array, chosen nondeterministically from all functions mapping `1..ArrayLen` to `1..ArrayLen`) and `A` (the working array), plus procedure-call machinery: `pc`, `stack`, `qlo`, `qhi`, and `pivot`. Initialization picks any such array and sets `A` equal to it.

Execution begins at `main`, which calls the recursive procedure `QS(1, Len(A))`. Each call proceeds through labeled steps: `qs1` checks whether the subrange `[qlo..qhi]` has more than one element and, if so, nondeterministically selects a pivot index and a permutation of `A` that leaves elements outside `[qlo..qhi]` unchanged and satisfies the partition invariant (all elements in `[qlo..pivot]` are at most all elements in `[pivot+1..qhi]`). Steps `qs2` and `qs3` recursively call `QS` on the left and right sub-arrays respectively, using the explicit `stack` to save and restore procedure context. Step `qs4` performs the return.

After the top-level call completes, the `test` step asserts that `A` is a permutation of `Ainit` and that `A` is fully sorted in non-decreasing order. The temporal specification `Spec` combines the initial condition, the always-enabled next-state relation, and weak fairness. The checked property is `Termination`, requiring the process eventually reaches `"Done"`.
desc_intent: Write a TLA+ specification for a recursive quicksort algorithm operating on a fixed-length array of integers. The array should be initialized nondeterministically as a mapping from index positions to values within the same range. The algorithm sorts the array in place using a partition-then-recurse strategy: given a subarray range, nondeterministically choose a pivot index within that range, rearrange the subarray (leaving elements outside the range untouched) so that all elements on the left of the pivot are no greater than all elements on the right, then recursively sort each half. The nondeterminism in both pivot selection and partitioning should be modeled abstractly — any valid partitioned permutation of the subarray is acceptable. The specification must guarantee two correctness properties: liveness, meaning the algorithm always terminates, and safety, meaning that upon termination the final array is a permutation of the original and is sorted in non-decreasing order across all index pairs. The constant controlling array length should be configurable so the model can be checked for small sizes such as 4 or 5.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a PlusCal model of an in-place quicksort-style algorithm over arrays of length N whose entries range over 1..N. The algorithm maintains a set S of subarray intervals still to be processed, repeatedly chooses an interval, nondeterministically selects a pivot position, and then nondeterministically replaces the current array by a permutation of itself that satisfies the partition ordering constraints around that pivot. The translated TLA+ specification defines the initial state, a single control-location action qs1, the overall next-state relation, a standard temporal specification with weak fairness on Next, and an eventual termination property asserting that the program counter eventually reaches "Done".
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a nondeterministic quicksort algorithm operating on an array of natural numbers, expressed as a PlusCal macro-based algorithm translated into TLA+.

The single constant `N` determines the array length. The variables are `Ainit` (the initial array, chosen nondeterministically from all functions `1..N → 1..N`), `A` (the working array), `S` (a set of index-range pairs representing subranges still to be sorted), `pivot` (the most recently chosen pivot index), and `pc` (the program counter).

Initially, `A` equals `Ainit` and `S` contains the single interval `⟨1, N⟩`. The single action `qs1` repeatedly picks an unsorted subrange `I` from `S`. If the subrange has more than one element, it nondeterministically selects a pivot index `piv` within the range, then nondeterministically rearranges `A` to any permutation that leaves elements outside `[I[1], I[2]]` unchanged and ensures every element on the left of the pivot is at most every element on the right. The subrange is then replaced by the two sub-intervals on either side of the pivot. If the subrange is a singleton, it is simply removed. The algorithm terminates when `S` is empty.

The temporal specification `Spec` is `Init ∧ [][Next]_vars` with weak fairness on `Next`. The configuration checks the liveness property `Termination` (`<>(pc = "Done")`), asserting that sorting always completes, with `N = 4`. No explicit sorting-correctness safety invariant is included in the module.
desc_intent: Specify a TLA+ model of the Quicksort algorithm operating on an array of integers. The system begins with an arbitrary array of length N (where N is a positive natural number) whose values are drawn from 1..N. Sorting proceeds by maintaining a set of index-interval pairs that still need to be partitioned. On each step, one unsorted interval is chosen nondeterministically: if the interval contains more than one element, a pivot index within it is chosen nondeterministically and the subarray is rearranged (nondeterministically among all valid rearrangements) so that every element to the left of the pivot is no greater than every element to the right, while elements outside the interval are unchanged; the interval is then replaced by the two sub-intervals on either side of the pivot. If an interval has length one or zero, it is simply removed. The algorithm terminates when no intervals remain. The key correctness property to verify is liveness: the algorithm must always eventually terminate. A permutation helper should be used to characterize valid rearrangements of the array during partitioning.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies and model checks a recursive mergesort algorithm translated from a PlusCal procedure into TLA+. It models sorting arrays of values in 1..N for all lengths up to ArrayLen, using an auxiliary buffer b and an explicit call stack to represent recursive procedure calls. The specification checks termination under weak fairness of Next and asserts a safety property that when the program counter reaches "Done", the array is sorted in nondecreasing order.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies Lamport's PlusCal encoding of Robert Sedgewick's merge sort algorithm, translated into TLA+. It is intended as a model-checked executable test rather than a design-level specification of a concurrent system.

The single constant `ArrayLen` bounds the size of the input. The algorithm initializes the global array `a` nondeterministically as any function from `1..N` to `1..N` for any length `N` between 0 and `ArrayLen`, and allocates a scratch buffer `b` of the same length. The procedure `mergesort(l, r)` is recursive: it computes a midpoint, recursively sorts the left and right halves, copies each half into `b` (the left half forward, the right half in reverse), and then merges them back into `a` via a single pointer traversal. Local variables `i`, `j`, `k`, and `m` track indices; the call stack is modeled explicitly with a sequence variable `stack`.

The temporal specification `Spec` combines the initial condition, the always-enabled next-state relation (with stuttering allowed at termination), and weak fairness on all variables. The liveness property `Termination` asserts that `pc` eventually reaches `"Done"`. The safety invariant `Invariant` requires that once execution finishes, `a` is sorted in non-decreasing order across its entire domain.

The configuration fixes `ArrayLen = 2` and checks both `Termination` and `Invariant`. A `POSTCONDITION` named `PossibleCounts` additionally verifies, via TLC coverage counters, that exactly 12 states where sorting is complete and exactly 8 merge-step transitions were observed during model checking.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of the merge sort algorithm, as transcribed from Sedgewick's "Algorithms" (2nd edition, page 166), operating on integer arrays of length up to some configurable maximum. The algorithm sorts an array by recursively splitting it into halves, copying elements into a temporary buffer array in a specific mirrored pattern, and then merging back from the buffer into the original array. The input array is nondeterministically chosen at startup from all arrays of any length between zero and the configured maximum, where both indices and values range over natural numbers up to that length.

The specification must guarantee two correctness properties. First, a safety invariant: upon termination, the array must be sorted in non-decreasing order — that is, for every pair of indices x and y in the array's domain, x less than y implies the element at x is no greater than the element at y. Second, a liveness property: the algorithm must always eventually terminate. The model should be parameterized by a maximum array length constant and should be validated with that constant set to 2, confirming the exact number of states satisfying the "sorted" termination condition and the number of merge-step transitions observed during model checking.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking companion to a MultiPaxos specification and adds TLC-oriented helper definitions plus two top-level correctness theorems. It defines symmetry-related permutation helpers and a constant ballot bound, then states a type-correctness invariant over messages, replica node states, pending and observed sequences, and request/acknowledgment cardinalities. It also defines a linearizability condition over observed client events by extracting request and acknowledgment positions, computing results and write order constraints, and asserting that once the system has terminated there exists a command order consistent with both sequential semantics and real-time ordering.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a replicated consensus protocol that provides multi-slot consensus (multiple independent instance slots) for proposing and learning values. The model should represent a set of proposers, acceptors, and learners interacting by exchanging messages to reach agreement on a value for each slot. The system must permit multiple rounds (ballots) and must support quorums of acceptors whose votes determine that a value is chosen for a given slot and ballot.

The model should capture these requirements and correctness properties:

- Safety (consistency): For every slot, at most one value can be learned (or chosen) by learners — once a value is chosen for a slot, no other distinct value can become chosen for that slot.
- Nontriviality (validity): Any value learned for a slot must have been proposed by some proposer for that slot.
- Stability (persistence): Once a value is learned for a slot it remains learned thereafter (learned sets are monotonic).
- Progress under favorable conditions: If proposers make proposals and a majority/quorum of non-faulty acceptors participate, some proposed value will eventually be chosen for a slot (liveness under partial synchrony or sufficient synchrony assumptions).
- Quorum intersection: The model should enforce that any two quorums intersect (so that previously chosen values are preserved when newer ballots are used).

Model the state abstractly (messages in transit, proposers’ current ballots, acceptors’ highest promised ballots and per-slot votes, learners’ learned values) and specify allowable actions for proposers, acceptors, and learners (sending/receiving prepare/accept messages, updating ballots and votes, learning chosen values). Do not prescribe a specific implementation of leader election; instead allow multiple proposers and multiple concurrent ballots. Formalize chosen as the existence of a quorum of matching acceptor votes for the same slot and ballot. State invariants and temporal properties that ensure the safety and nontriviality requirements above, and include an eventuality property that under reasonable assumptions guarantees progress for some slot.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking wrapper around a MultiPaxos specification. It adds type-correctness and consensus-oriented checking operators over the imported state from the underlying MultiPaxos module, and it instantiates a separate ConsensusMulti specification to compare the learned values against an abstract consensus interface. The file verifies that the MultiPaxos specification implies a type invariant, implies the instantiated consensus specification, and also implies two invariant-style properties: nontriviality and per-slot consistency. The comments note that some checks are intended only for very small constant instances because of state-space blowup, while simpler invariants can be checked on larger instances.
desc_intent:
Model a replicated multi-slot consensus protocol (Multi-Paxos style) for a fixed set of replicas, a fixed set of slots (sequence positions), and a fixed set of values. The model should capture the interaction between proposers/replicas that prepare and accept proposals and learners that may learn values for each slot. It must allow replicas to propose any value from their per-slot proposal sets and to exchange messages for Prepare, PrepareReply (including information about previously voted proposals), Accept, and AcceptReply. The system should permit concurrent proposals and multiple rounds/ballots per slot, including ballots that may be superseded, but must ensure the usual safety and liveness expectations below.

Specify the following correctness requirements:
- Nontriviality: any value that becomes learned for a slot must have been proposed for that slot.
- Stability: once a value is learned for a given slot it remains learned for that slot thereafter (learned sets are monotonic).
- Consistency (Agreement): at most one distinct value can be learned for any given slot (learners never decide two different values for the same slot).
- Validity of replies: prepare replies must faithfully report prior accepted/voted proposals from the responder.
- Message and state typing invariants: all messages and local state components conform to declared domains (ballot numbers, slot indices, value sets, statuses).

Do not prescribe a particular implementation detail; allow the specification to include arbitrary reliable message passing (message loss acceptable if specified), persistent local state for ballots and accepted votes, and nondeterministic scheduling of actions and message delivery.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a small model-checking wrapper around a Paxos Commit specification. It extends PaxosCommit, instantiates module TCommit as TCommitSpec, defines TCommitSpecProperty as TCommitSpec!TCSpec, and states the theorem that PCSpec implies TCommitSpecProperty.
desc_intent: Specify a formal TLA+ model of a transaction commit service implemented atop a consensus protocol. The model should describe a distributed system of clients and a set of acceptors (or replicas) cooperating to decide whether to commit or abort individual transactions. It must capture the interaction of a coordinator (or proposer) and learners that propose and learn a single final decision per transaction via a consensus instance; multiple independent transactions may be decided concurrently. The model must require safety properties: (1) Agreement — no two non-faulty learners decide different outcomes for the same transaction; (2) Validity — if every participant initially votes to commit, the final decision may be commit; if any honest participant votes to abort, the outcome can be abort; (3) Integrity — once a learner decides a commit or abort, that decision is final and does not change; and (4) Nontriviality — decisions are only commit or abort (no spurious values). It must also express liveness under suitable assumptions: if a majority of acceptors remain responsive and messages are eventually delivered, then every transaction proposed by a correct coordinator will eventually be decided. The specification should abstract from low-level implementation details and instead state the roles, message types, state transitions, and the invariants/temporal properties that ensure the commit service refines the abstract transaction-commit specification.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking wrapper around an underlying abstraction module, restricting the server set, term range, and log bounds to make exploration finite. It defines a concrete symmetric server set of three nodes, bounds terms to 2..4, sets the start term to the minimum of that range, and constrains log lengths via bounded sequences and an explicit length constraint. The file does not define a full temporal specification itself; instead it provides configuration-style helper operators and type constraints intended to be used with the imported abstraction, with symmetry reduction through permutations of the server set.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of a replicated-state-machine (RSM) leader-based consensus protocol for a small cluster of fixed servers. The model should describe how servers maintain and exchange logs of commands and agree on committed decisions across multiple terms. The system must allow leaders to propose and append entries to their local logs, allow followers to accept or reject append requests, enable term changes via elections, and support log truncation/repair when a follower's log diverges. Include mechanisms for leader election, log replication, commit index advancement, and safety during leader changes (including preventing committed entries from being lost).

The model must guarantee these correctness properties:
- Safety: once a command is committed at a particular index in some term, every server’s log at that index eventually contains the same command and term, and that value never changes (no committed entry is overwritten).
- Leader completeness: a leader that completes an entry has that entry present on a majority of servers.
- Log matching: if two logs contain the same entry at the same index and term, then all preceding entries are identical.
- Term monotonicity: terms are nondecreasing on each server, and leadership is only attributable to the highest-known term.
- Liveness under partial synchrony: assuming a stable period where a majority of servers can communicate, some leader eventually commits new entries.

Model should allow bounded message loss, message reordering, and server crashes/recoveries, and support reasonable bounds on log lengths and term numbers to enable model checking. Do not prescribe internal variable names or concrete algorithmic steps; focus on the protocol goals and invariants to verify.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines an alternative initial state for a multi-node reads model by extending an existing base specification and adding a new initial predicate. The alternative state initializes ledger branches and history so that two transactions are already committed, as indicated by the comment and by the pre-populated response and committed-status records in the history sequence. The module then defines a temporal specification that starts from this alternative initial state and evolves according to the imported action MCNextMultiNodeReadsAction, using the standard stuttering form [][MCNextMultiNodeReadsAction]_vars.
desc_declarative_claude:
This module is a model-checking wrapper that extends `MCMultiNodeReads` and provides an alternative initial state for verifying multi-node read behavior in a distributed ledger system (modeled after a consensus-based system such as CCF).

Rather than starting from an empty state, `InitAlt` begins with two transactions already committed: the ledger has two branches with entries at views 1 and 2, and the history record already contains request and response events for both transactions along with their committed status receipts. The temporal specification `MCSpecMultiNodeReadsAlt` pairs this alternative initial state with the same next-state relation (`MCNextMultiNodeReadsAction`) and variables used by the parent module. The configuration fixes `HistoryLimit` to 11 and `ViewLimit` to 3, disables deadlock checking, and checks twelve safety invariants inherited from `MCMultiNodeReads`. These invariants cover correctness properties such as serializable reads across committed read-write transactions, uniqueness of transaction identifiers and sequence numbers, consistency of observations against sent requests, and that invalidated transactions are never observed by committed ones. The module's purpose is to exercise the same invariants as `MCMultiNodeReads` but from a non-trivial pre-committed starting point, increasing the portion of the reachable state space explored within the given bounds.
desc_intent: Specify a distributed ledger system that supports multiple nodes maintaining branches of the ledger and handling read/write transactions. The model should represent multiple nodes that can independently accept transactions, execute reads that observe previously committed transactions, and communicate commit status so that transactions become visible across nodes. The system must allow transactions to be proposed, processed, and either committed or not; committed transactions must be durable and visible to later read operations according to an ordering consistent with commits. Reads may query a node’s local branch and must return a set of observed transaction identifiers that reflect a prefix of the committed history available at that node at the time of the read. The model should permit starting from an initial condition where some transactions are already committed and visible on one or more branches. Correctness properties to guarantee: safety — once a transaction is reported committed, its effects are never lost and subsequent reads that observe that commit must not contradict it; monotonic visibility — any read that occurs after another read or commit on the same node must observe at least the same set of committed transactions (no rollback of observed commits); and consistency across nodes — if a transaction is committed systemwide, all nodes eventually make it visible to reads (liveness: eventual visibility). Additionally ensure that reads return observed sets that are internally consistent with the ordering of committed transactions (no observing a later commit while missing an earlier committed predecessor). The specification should abstract away protocol internals and focus on the observable behavior and these properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a bounded model-checking wrapper for a multi-node reads specification. It extends two other modules and adds a combined next-state action that allows either the underlying multi-node transition or read-only transaction request/response actions, then defines a standard safety-style temporal specification using Init and a boxed next-step formula. The file itself contains no local state declarations, constants, fairness, proofs, or PlusCal algorithm; it serves as a small composition layer over actions defined elsewhere.
desc_intent:
Specify a concurrent distributed-memory system that supports atomic multi-node read-only transactions in the presence of ordinary multi-node read-write transactions. The model should represent multiple nodes that each store disjoint sets of keys, clients that may issue either read-only transactions spanning many nodes or standard read-write transactions, and a communication medium delivering messages between nodes and clients with bounded or asynchronous delays. The system must allow read-only transactions to contact multiple nodes to obtain consistent snapshots without blocking or interfering with concurrent updates beyond standard read-commit semantics.

Require the specification to capture liveness of transaction processing (requests are eventually handled and responses delivered under fair scheduling) and safety properties: serializability (all transactions observe a total order equivalent to some sequential execution), atomicity of read-only transactions (each read-only transaction returns values that reflect a single global snapshot), and write-atomicity with respect to reads (no read observes a write that did not commit in the serialization order). Also require absence of lost or duplicated committed updates, and that reads return only values produced by some committed write. The model should permit modeling of retrying, timeouts, and message reordering, and include invariants to prove that read-only transactions do not violate consistency even when concurrently executing with read-write transactions.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a bounded model-checking wrapper for a MultiNode specification by restricting part of the behavior with an explicit bound on the number of view changes. It extends existing modules and adds a constant ViewLimit, then defines bounded action variants that guard inherited actions with checks on the lengths of ledgerBranches and history. The module defines a combined next-state action and a temporal specification MCSpecMultiNode == Init /\ [][MCNextMultiNodeAction]_vars, but it does not introduce its own fairness, proofs, or PlusCal algorithm.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of a bounded, multi-replica consensus and ledger-replication system that supports view changes and limited state growth. The model should describe multiple independent nodes that maintain per-node ledgers and histories, communicate via message passing, and may perform local actions such as proposing and committing ledger entries, responding to status requests, and truncating local ledgers as part of recovery or garbage collection. The system must allow view changes (leader changes), but enforce a global upper bound on the total number of view changes that can occur during any execution. It must also bound the length of per-node history structures so responses that produce status-invalid outcomes cannot grow without limit.

Specify the safety and liveness properties to verify: safety must enforce that committed ledger prefixes are consistent across non-faulty nodes (no two nodes permanently disagree on committed entries), and that truncation or recovery never leads to loss of commitment: once an entry is committed, it remains present in every later ledger state of non-faulty nodes. Liveness must ensure progress under eventual synchrony: if a majority of nodes are non-faulty and messages are eventually delivered, then new proposals are eventually committed. Include invariants that express the bounds on view-change count and history length, and model message and failure behaviors needed to check these properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a bounded model-checking wrapper around a single-node read system specified elsewhere. It adds history-bound guards to the read-only transaction request and response actions, and combines them with an existing single-node next-state action from another extended module. The temporal property defined here is a simple safety-style specification stating that the system starts in Init and then evolves according to the stuttering closure of MCNextSingleNodeReadsAction over vars.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a single-node transaction processing system that supports both read-only transactions and regular (read-write) operations, with bounded history to prevent unbounded growth. The model should describe a node that receives requests, processes them, and produces responses, tracking a history of transactions and responses up to a configurable limit. It must allow concurrent interleaving of incoming requests and outgoing responses while ensuring the node never records more history entries than the bound.

The specification should capture the actions for: accepting a read-only transaction request, producing a read-only transaction response, performing ordinary node actions that represent the internal processing and state updates for read-write operations, and advancing the system step when none of these occur. The system must preserve safety properties: responses correspond only to previously accepted requests, read-only responses return values consistent with the node’s state at some linearization point, and the history length invariant is maintained (never exceeds the configured cap). Also specify liveness assumptions or fairness to ensure requests that are admitted will eventually receive responses, subject to the bounded history constraint. Provide a clear definition of initial conditions and the transition relation that enforces these requirements.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a system with three concurrent clients (c1, c2, c3) operating on a single table with three keys. All clients share the same primary key, which is set to 1 for each client, indicating symmetry among them. The spec is intended for TLC model checking, as noted in the comments, and leverages symmetry reduction by defining a symmetry set over the clients. The module extends OptimizedCommitTS (presumably containing the main protocol logic) and TLC (for model checking support). No temporal properties, actions, or proofs are defined in this file; it serves as a configuration and parameterization layer for the underlying protocol.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a concurrent transactional key-value store that supports optimistic commit with timestamp ordering and multiple clients issuing transactions concurrently. The model should include a fixed set of keys and a fixed set of clients; multiple clients may target the same primary key, making some clients symmetric from the system’s point of view. Transactions consist of read and write sets and must acquire timestamps and/or version numbers used to validate and order commits.

The model must capture nonblocking execution of transactions by clients (they may proceed independently), optimistic validation at commit time, and a commit protocol that assigns commit timestamps and resolves conflicts deterministically so that at most one conflicting write sequence is accepted. It must model transient states during validation and commit so that races and concurrent commits are possible.

Key correctness properties to verify:
- Serializability: the effect of committed transactions must be equivalent to some serial order consistent with commit timestamps.
- Atomicity: each transaction either commits all its writes or none (no partial commits visible).
- No lost updates: if a transaction commits a write to a key, subsequent reads after the commit reflect that write unless overwritten by a later committed transaction.
- Progress: a client that repeatedly retries its transaction in the absence of continuous conflicting commits will eventually commit (liveness under fairness).
- Symmetry preservation: behavior and verification should respect client symmetry when clients are identical except for identity.

Do not prescribe the internal algorithmic details (e.g., exact message passing, locks) beyond optimistic timestamp-based validation and commit ordering; leave those choices for the specification to refine.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking wrapper module that extends the MultiUser specification and defines several top-level property operators referring to instantiated specifications from that extended module. It introduces a constant-valued operator const_17385913267612000 set to the range 1..2, likely corresponding to a model parameter for user identifiers. The file itself does not define system state variables or transition actions; instead, it collects correctness properties such as SingleUser2!Spec, SingleUser3!Spec, and parameterized SingleUserP(2)!Spec formulas, including quantified variants over singleton sets.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a logical timestamp allocator used by a distributed system component that issues monotonically increasing timestamps from a bounded domain. The system receives requests for timestamps and must assign each request a timestamp that is strictly greater than any previously assigned timestamp, subject to an upper bound on the timestamp space. The model should allow two distinct constant label values representing available timestamp identifiers. The allocator must never issue a timestamp equal to or greater than a fixed numeric limit. Concurrent requests may be presented, and the model must capture interleavings and nondeterministic scheduling of request arrivals.

Model goals and required properties:
- Safety: Every assigned timestamp is unique for the lifetime of the modeled run and strictly increases with respect to the previously issued timestamp for that logical sequence of assignments.
- Bound enforcement: No issued timestamp may violate the numeric upper bound constraint.
- Liveness (weak): If requests continue to arrive and the bound has not been reached, the allocator should be able to issue further timestamps (i.e., the model should not deadlock while issuance is still possible).
- Fairness: The model should permit all requests to eventually be served under fair scheduling when the bound allows issuance.

Avoid prescribing an implementation strategy; instead describe the state elements (current highest timestamp, set of available labels) and interactions (request, assign) and the correctness properties above to be checked.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a minimal wrapper module named SmokeBitwise that extends the BitwiseTests module and contains no additional declarations, definitions, actions, temporal properties, or proofs. It consists only of the module header, an EXTENDS clause, and a separator line.
desc_intent:
Model a concurrent test harness that verifies bitwise operations across multiple independent worker processes interacting with a shared test oracle. The system should generate pairs of random input values, apply a suite of bitwise functions (including but not limited to AND, OR, XOR, NOT, left and right shifts, and combinations thereof) to each pair, and record both expected results (computed by a reference oracle) and actual results produced by worker computations. Ensure workers may run concurrently, may fail transiently, and may deliver results out of order. The specification must capture non-deterministic scheduling, message delivery delays, and possible duplication or loss of worker outputs, while assuming the oracle’s computations are reliable.

Specify correctness properties: for every completed test case where a worker result is accepted, the recorded actual value must equal the oracle’s expected value; if a mismatch is detected it must be flagged and can be used to drive a failing trace. Guarantee eventual completion: under fair scheduling and reliable persistence of accepted results, every submitted test case will either be verified as correct or reported as failed. Include invariants to ensure no test case is silently lost (either verified or failed) and temporal properties expressing that mismatches lead to a visible error state and that correct computations are eventually acknowledged.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models Conway's Game of Life on an N by N finite grid. The state consists of a single variable grid mapping each position in the set of board coordinates to a Boolean value indicating whether the cell is alive or dead, and the next-state relation computes the standard Life update rule from neighbor counts. The spec defines helper operators for summing values over a finite set, handling boundary cells outside the board as dead, and counting live neighbors; it verifies behavior through an initial condition and a temporal specification of repeated Next steps with stuttering allowed. There is no fault model, fairness condition, proof structure, or PlusCal algorithm in this file.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies Conway's Game of Life on a finite N×N toroidal-free grid, where N is a natural number constant (set to 4 in the model-checking configuration).

The single variable `grid` maps every position in the N×N grid (represented as pairs of integers from 1 to N) to a Boolean value, where TRUE means a cell is alive and FALSE means it is dead. The `Init` predicate allows any arbitrary initial assignment of live and dead cells across the grid. The `Next` action advances the entire grid by one generation simultaneously: a cell is alive in the next state if and only if it is currently alive with exactly 2 or 3 live neighbors, or currently dead with exactly 3 live neighbors — the standard Game of Life survival and birth rules. Cells outside the 1..N boundary are treated as permanently dead via the `sc` scoring function, which returns 0 for out-of-bounds or dead cells and 1 for live ones. The `score` function sums the contributions of the eight cardinal and diagonal neighbors to count live neighbors. The temporal specification `Spec` is `Init` conjoined with the always-enabled stuttering-tolerant next-state relation `[][Next]_vars`, with no fairness constraints. The only checked property is the type invariant `TypeOK`, asserting that `grid` remains a function from positions to Booleans.
desc_intent:
Model Conway's Game of Life on a finite N×N toroidal board and specify its safety and liveness requirements.

The model should represent a square grid of N by N cells, each cell either alive or dead. Time advances in discrete synchronous steps where, at each step, the state of every cell is updated simultaneously according to the standard Life rules: a live cell survives only if it has 2 or 3 live neighbors; a dead cell becomes alive only if it has exactly 3 live neighbors. Neighbor counting wraps around the edges (toroidal topology) or alternatively provide an option to model non-wrapping boundaries that treat out-of-range neighbors as always dead.

Specify the initial state as an arbitrary assignment of alive/dead to all cells. Require the model to allow nondeterministic initial configurations and to evolve according to the deterministic update rule.

State and verify these correctness properties:
- Type correctness: the grid always maps each grid position to a boolean value.
- Update determinism: given a state, the next state is uniquely determined by the neighbor counts and the Life rules.
- Invariance: the set of live/dead labels remains within the boolean domain throughout execution.
- Conservation/monotonicity properties for given patterns: ability to assert and check that recognized still lifes remain unchanged, oscillators return to their initial configuration with a fixed period, and glider patterns translate with the expected period and velocity on the chosen topology.
- Progress property: for any finite configuration eventually reaching a previously seen state implies a fairness assertion for periodic behavior (formulate as liveness: there exist repeated states or cycles reachable from some initial configurations).

Allow the option to check bounded model properties (for given N and bounded time horizon) and to state invariants for proving absence of illegal transitions or miscounted neighbors.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines two helper operators over the state space or data structures provided by the imported Reachable module. It chooses a successor function from Nodes to subsets of Nodes such that every node has exactly two successors, and it defines a set of finite sequences over an arbitrary set S whose lengths are bounded by the cardinality of Nodes. The module contains no variables, no actions, no temporal specification, and no proofs; it is a small structural helper module rather than a complete transition-system specification.
desc_intent: Specify a model of a finite directed graph network together with a nondeterministic assignment of each node’s outgoing neighbors, and characterize reachability properties of nodes under that assignment. The system should allow any finite set of nodes and permit each node to have exactly two distinct outgoing neighbors chosen from the node set. Also allow exploration of all possible choices where some nodes may have no edges (i.e., consider sequences of nodes of length up to the number of nodes as possible paths). The model must express reachability: given the chosen outgoing-neighbor relation, a node u is reachable from node v if there exists a finite path following outgoing edges from v to u. Specify operations that nondeterministically pick a valid outgoing-neighbor relation and then evaluate which nodes are mutually reachable, which nodes are reachable from a given source set, and which nodes are reachable from some but not all starting nodes. Guarantee that the specification can check the existence of configurations meeting predicates such as “every node has exactly two successors,” “some node is reachable from every other node,” and “a node is reachable from some but not all other nodes.” Include invariants and temporal properties to assert correctness of reachability computations.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies a simplified version of Leslie Lamport's Fast Paxos consensus protocol. The specification assumes a unique coordinator, omits explicit modeling of failures (since agents restore state from stable storage), and allows all agents to communicate directly. The protocol models both fast and classic rounds, with special handling for quorum intersection and value selection in the presence of collisions. The specification defines the main protocol actions, type invariants, and a non-triviality safety property, and it verifies that consensus is achieved only on values that have been proposed.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a simplified version of Leslie Lamport's Fast Paxos protocol, extending a base Paxos module. It assumes a unique coordinator (eliminating Phase 1), full connectivity among agents, and stable storage for all replicas. The system is modeled over four replicas, three values, five ballots (with ballots 1 and 3 designated as fast), and classic quorums and fast quorums each consisting of all size-3 subsets of the four replicas.

The protocol distinguishes fast rounds from classic rounds. In a fast round, the coordinator broadcasts a special "any" P2a message, allowing acceptors to propose their own values directly in P2b replies. A fast decision is reached when an entire fast quorum agrees on a single value. If a collision occurs (multiple values proposed in a fast quorum), a subsequent classic round resolves it: the coordinator must choose the majority value among fast-quorum responses if one exists, or any proposed value otherwise, then proceeds with standard Paxos Phase 2a/2b. Classic decisions require a classic quorum to agree on the same ballot. The variable `cValue` tracks the coordinator's chosen value during collision recovery. The temporal specification `FastSpec` is a safety+liveness formula combining the initial condition, a stuttering-tolerant next-state relation, and strong fairness on both `FastDecide` and `ClassicDecide`. The checked invariants are `FastTypeOK` (type correctness) and `FastNontriviality` (only proposed values are decided), and the model also verifies `PaxosConsistency` (at most one value is ever decided).
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of the Fast Paxos consensus algorithm for a system of replicas that may propose and agree on one value per instance. The model should capture two kinds of rounds: “fast” rounds that allow proposers to broadcast proposals directly and require larger quorums, and “classic” rounds that use a coordinator-driven prepare/accept pattern with majority quorums. Do not prescribe an implementation; instead state what the algorithm must accomplish and the invariants it must maintain.

Requirements:
- Model proposers, acceptors, and a coordinator role abstractly; allow concurrent proposals and messages between them.
- Fast rounds: proposers may initiate a fast round that signals “any” value may be accepted, and acceptors may respond with their current proposed value. A value is decided in a fast round when a fast quorum of acceptors report the same value.
- Classic rounds: when conflicts exist (multiple values proposed in a preceding fast round), a coordinator must be able to run a classic round. The coordinator must choose a value according to safety rules: if the fast-quorum responses include a value held by a strict majority of that fast quorum, that value must be chosen; otherwise the coordinator may pick any value from those proposed. Classic acceptance follows the usual majority acceptance rule and decision occurs when a classic quorum accepts the same value.
- Safety properties: (1) Agreement — no two different values can both become decided (in any combination of fast/classic rounds). (2) Nontriviality — only values that were actually proposed by some acceptor can be decided. (3) Valid conflict-resolution rule — when resolving collisions the coordinator must respect the majority-in-quorum rule described above.
- Liveness assumptions: do not model crashes explicitly, but allow asynchronous message delivery; specify fairness conditions sufficient to ensure progress of decision steps when required quorums and messages eventually occur.
- Quorum structure: allow parameterization of replica set, fast-quorum sets, and classic quorum sets, with constraints ensuring intersection properties required for safety (fast quorums intersect each other and intersect classic quorums appropriately).

State clearly the consensus goal (single chosen value per instance) and the correctness invariants above; avoid committing to particular message formats or algorithmic steps.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a thin wrapper that supplies Apalache type annotations for another specification, `bcastFolklore`, via an `INSTANCE` declaration. It declares constants and variables with structured comments indicating intended integer, string, set, and function types, but it does not define any behavior, actions, temporal specification, or proof obligations of its own. The file therefore models no standalone algorithm directly; instead, it provides typed declarations intended to be used together with the instantiated module while keeping the original specification free of tool-specific annotations.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of a distributed reliable broadcast protocol for a system of N processes, up to F Byzantine faults but with at most T crash failures counted separately, that ensures eventual agreement among all non-faulty processes. The model should treat processes as independent agents that can send and receive messages asynchronously over unreliable channels (messages may be delayed, duplicated, or reordered but not corrupted), and processes may crash permanently. The system must support broadcasting values from any process and implement the following properties:

- Validity: If a correct (non-faulty) process broadcasts a value v, then every correct process eventually delivers v.
- Integrity: No correct process delivers more than one value for a given broadcast instance, and if a value v is delivered by a correct process and the broadcaster was correct, then v is the value actually broadcast by that broadcaster.
- Agreement: If any correct process delivers a value v for a given broadcast instance, then every correct process eventually delivers v (agreement on delivered value).
- Termination/Liveness: Every correct process eventually either delivers a value for each broadcast initiated by some process, or irrevocably determines that no value will be delivered because the broadcaster crashed before sending.

Capture faults as two types: crash (process stops taking steps) and arbitrary omission/delay in communication; do not model malicious Byzantine behavior beyond omission/crash. Specify fairness assumptions needed for liveness (e.g., weak fairness of enabled send/receive actions or eventual reliable delivery of sent messages). Include invariants that express safety (integrity and agreement) and a temporal property for liveness (validity and termination). The model should allow parameterization by N, T, and F.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a buffered random-access file implementation together with an abstract RandomAccessFile refinement target and shared array/file utilities. The main module specifies the buffered object's internal fields, the effects of seek, read, write, flush, and setLength, and a collection of internal invariants about how the in-memory buffer relates to the logical and on-disk file contents. It verifies both safety-style invariants and refinement properties: the whole behavior refines an abstract RandomAccessFile spec, and each concrete operation refines its abstract counterpart. The model is single-threaded and does not use an explicit fault model; instead, underspecified file contents are represented using an ArbitrarySymbol value to keep the model checkable. The file also includes a TLC configuration section selecting constants, symmetry, aliasing, invariants, and properties for model checking.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a buffered random-access file, corresponding to `BufferedRandomAccessFile.java`, and verifies that it correctly refines a simpler `RandomAccessFile` abstraction defined in a companion module.

The system models an in-memory write buffer of fixed size `BuffSz` sitting in front of an underlying disk file. The buffered layer tracks six fields: `dirty` (whether the buffer has unflushed writes), `length` (logical file length), `curr` (current logical position), `lo` (the starting disk offset of the buffered region), `buff` (the in-memory buffer contents), and `diskPos` (the actual disk head position). The disk itself is represented by `file_content` and `file_pointer`. The five internal invariants (Inv1–Inv5) assert consistency between the logical file view, the buffer, and the on-disk state. The logical file content (`LogicalFileContent`) is defined by overlaying the buffer onto the disk contents.

The actions are `FlushBuffer` (writes the dirty buffer to disk), `Seek` (repositions `curr`, flushing and refilling the buffer when the new position falls outside the buffered window), `SetLength` (truncates or extends the file), `Read1`/`Write1` (single-byte read/write), and `Read`/`WriteAtMost` (multi-byte bulk operations). The specification (`Spec`) is `Init` plus the always-enabled stuttering next-state relation. Correctness is checked as refinement of `RandomAccessFile` via a mapping that substitutes `LogicalFileContent` for `file_content` and `curr` for `file_pointer`. Additional temporal properties verify that each concrete action refines its abstract counterpart and that `Inv2` (the buffer-window invariant) can always be restored by a flush-then-seek sequence. The model is checked with two symbols, `MaxOffset = 3`, and `BuffSz = 2`.
desc_intent: Specify a model of a single-threaded buffered random-access file abstraction that sits on top of an underlying file image. The model should expose the externally observable operations: seek, setLength, read (single-byte and multi-byte), write (single-byte and multi-byte), and an explicit flush of the in-memory buffer to the underlying file. The buffered implementation must support a fixed-size in-memory window (buffer) that caches a contiguous region of the file; reads and writes that fall inside the cached window should be served/recorded from/to the buffer without immediately touching the underlying file, while operations that move outside the window must cause the buffer to be refilled (possibly after flushing dirty contents). Flushing must copy buffered bytes to the underlying file and clear the dirty flag. setLength must correctly truncate or extend the logical file and adjust the apparent file length and pointer according to the RandomAccessFile contract. The model must maintain invariants tying the buffer contents, buffer window bounds, and logical file contents (so that the logical file equals the underlying file updated by any buffered modifications where relevant), and must ensure a relationship between the internal file pointer and the underlying file pointer after flush/seek operations. Correctness properties required: (1) internal invariants always hold; (2) the buffered behavior refines an abstract RandomAccessFile specification (i.e., every buffered operation corresponds to a valid abstract operation on the logical file and pointer); and (3) each concrete operation refines its abstract counterpart (reads return the expected bytes, writes/flush update logical contents as if writing to the abstract file, seeks and setLength behave as specified). Also require liveness-style guarantees that a dirty buffer can be flushed when needed so that buffer-restoring sequences (flush then refill or seek) can always restore buffer invariants.

desc_declarative_gpt: This specification models a B-tree-based key-value store supporting get, insert, and update requests over a bounded set of keys, values, and nodes. The state explicitly represents tree structure using node-local key sets, child pointers, last-child pointers, leaf flags, stored values, and a small request/response control interface with operational states for searching, adding, and splitting nodes. It includes a refinement mapping to an abstract kvstore specification, a type invariant and several structural invariants, and a temporal specification with weak fairness for get requests; there is no fault model, and comments note that deletes are not implemented.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies a B-tree data structure supporting get, insert, and update operations, with node splitting modeled as a multi-step process. Deletions are explicitly noted as unimplemented.

The tree is built over a fixed pool of `Nodes` (1..`MaxNode`) and `Keys` (1..`MaxKey`). Each node is characterized by whether it is a leaf (`isLeaf`), its set of keys (`keysOf`), child pointers for inner nodes (`childOf`, `lastOf`), and key-value pairs for leaves (`valOf`). A single `root` node is tracked. An operation in progress is described by `op`, `args`, `ret`, `focus` (the node currently being examined or modified), and `toSplit` (a sequence of nodes that need splitting). The `state` variable drives a state machine through phases: `READY`, `GET_VALUE`, `FIND_LEAF_TO_ADD`, `WHICH_TO_SPLIT`, `ADD_TO_LEAF`, `SPLIT_LEAF`, `SPLIT_INNER`, `SPLIT_ROOT_LEAF`, `SPLIT_ROOT_INNER`, and `UPDATE_LEAF`.

Inserts locate the target leaf via recursive traversal and, if the leaf is at `MaxOccupancy`, propagate splits upward through `toSplit` before adding the key-value pair. Root splits allocate two new nodes and promote a pivot key. The specification includes a refinement mapping to an abstract key-value store (`kvstore`) via a `Mapping` instance, asserting that the B-tree implements a key-value abstraction. The model checks several structural invariants: inner nodes must have a `lastOf` pointer, leaves must not, key order must be preserved across inner nodes and their children, leaf keys must be globally unique, and at least one free node must always remain.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a bounded-memory B-tree used as a persistent key-value store that supports get, insert, and update operations. The model should represent a fixed finite pool of node objects that can be allocated and split but not deleted, and must support both leaf and internal nodes arranged under a single root. Keys come from a fixed finite domain and values from a fixed finite domain. The model must include node occupancy limits (maximum keys per node) and the usual B-tree invariants about keys, children, and ordering.

The model must describe these behaviors without prescribing any particular algorithmic encoding details:

- Get: locate the leaf that should contain a key and return its value if present, otherwise return a distinguished "missing" result.
- Insert: find the target leaf; if the key already exists, report an error; otherwise insert the key/value pair, allocating and linking free nodes as needed, and perform node splits (including special handling when the root must split) so that occupancy limits are respected and the tree remains a valid B-tree.
- Update: locate the leaf for a key and overwrite its value only if the key exists; otherwise report an error.

Required correctness properties to verify:
- Structural invariants: internal nodes have valid child pointers and a non-nil rightmost child; leaves have no rightmost child pointer; key ordering between parent pivot keys and child keys is preserved.
- Uniqueness: each key appears in at most one leaf.
- Resource safety: at least one free node remains available (or otherwise state explicit allocation assumptions), and splits allocate distinct free nodes.
- Functional refinement: externally observable behavior of get/insert/update refines a simple key-value map abstraction that yields the same responses for operations in quiescent states.
- Progress: the system must allow operations to start only when idle and must eventually return to quiescent state after completing an operation (no permanent deadlock during normal operation sequences, modulo bounded-resource constraints).

Do not fix internal naming or control-state encodings; instead require the model to expose an abstract operation/state distinction so that refinement to a simple key-value specification can be stated and checked.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module models a small bounded configuration of the Sailfish protocol with three nodes, one of which is Byzantine. The file defines concrete node sets, quorum and blocking-set predicates, a leader schedule, a global stabilization time constant, and a state constraint that bounds the explored rounds for non-faulty nodes to control state-space explosion. It introduces a terminating variant of the behavior specification and several deliberately false temporal/state predicates intended to help TLC produce interesting counterexample executions, including conditions about all correct nodes finishing and about committed log entries.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module `TLCSailfish1` is a model-checking configuration wrapper for the `Sailfish` consensus protocol, instantiated with a specific small-scale scenario designed to exercise Byzantine fault tolerance while keeping the state space manageable.

The system comprises three nodes (`n1`, `n2`, `n3`), where `n1` is the single Byzantine node (`F = {n1}`). Rounds are bounded to `1..5`. Quorums are defined explicitly as any set containing at least two nodes including `n3` or the full set, and blocking sets are those containing `n3`. The leader schedule cycles through the three nodes in order. The global stabilization time (`GST`) is set to round 3, after which the network is assumed synchronous.

The `Sailfish` module is instantiated with these parameters and the four variables `vs`, `es`, `round`, and `log`, which track vertices, edges, per-node round progress, and committed log entries respectively. The temporal specification `TerminatingSpec` allows the system to stutter once all correct nodes have reached the maximum round, enabling the model checker to terminate cleanly. A `StateConstraint` restricts correct nodes' rounds to the bounded range.

The configuration checks three invariants imported from `Sailfish`: `TypeOK` (type correctness), `Agreement` (safety: no two correct nodes commit conflicting logs), and `Liveness` (correct nodes make progress). Three `Falsy` properties are defined as negations of reachable states—such as all correct nodes reaching the final round, any correct node having a log longer than one entry, or round-2's leader vertex being committed—intended to be used as false invariants to extract interesting counterexample traces from the model checker.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a replicated-state-machine consensus protocol operating among a small set of nodes with at most one Byzantine (arbitrary) faulty node. The model should abstract rounds and leader rotation, quorums and blocking sets, and a notion of proposal logs at each correct replica. The system must allow a Byzantine node to behave arbitrarily while ensuring that the correct nodes follow the protocol rules.

The model must express the progression of rounds, leader selection by round number, and the communication assumptions captured by quorums and blocking sets (quorums must intersect pairwise in at least one correct node; every blocking set must intersect all quorums and contain a correct node). The protocol should support proposal creation, voting/acknowledgement, and log appends; it must allow replicas to advance rounds and commit proposals when they have sufficient support from a quorum.

State invariants to guarantee:
- Safety (consistency): no two correct replicas commit conflicting proposals for the same log position/round.
- Liveness under eventual synchrony: if leaders remain live after GST, the protocol eventually commits new proposals proposed by correct leaders.
- Fault-tolerance: one Byzantine node cannot cause the intersection properties to be violated; quorums of correct nodes suffice to make progress and to prevent equivocation from causing inconsistent commits.
- Termination bound: under the model’s finite round horizon, correct replicas will eventually stop advancing when rounds max out.

Include properties to check both that progress can be made (some correct replica appends multiple entries) and that particular leaders can cause commits, while enabling exploration of Byzantine behaviors that should not violate safety.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a TLC model wrapper for the DijkstraMutex specification rather than a standalone algorithm definition. It declares three model values p1, p2, and p3, defines a constant set containing those values for use as Proc in the model, and maps the model checking configuration to imported top-level operators from the extended module: LSpec as the behavior specification, MutualExclusion as an invariant, and DeadlockFreedom as a temporal property. The file itself contains no state variables, actions, fairness clauses, or proofs; it serves to instantiate and expose model-checking targets for the underlying mutex specification.
desc_intent:
Specify a system that models a classic distributed mutual exclusion algorithm for three processes competing to enter a critical section. The model should represent an asynchronous setting where each process can execute steps independently and may be delayed arbitrarily; there is no global clock. Processes communicate only via shared variables (no message passing), and all actions are atomic. Each process repeatedly alternates between noncritical and critical sections, using the algorithm to coordinate access.

The specification must state the safety requirement that at most one process is in the critical section at any time (mutual exclusion). It must also state liveness requirements: from any reachable state in which some processes continually attempt to enter the critical section, eventually one of them succeeds (no permanent starvation for all contenders), and the system as a whole does not deadlock (if some process is enabled, some process eventually makes progress). The model should allow arbitrary scheduling of enabled actions and must permit modeling fairness assumptions needed to prove liveness properties. Provide invariants and temporal properties sufficient to verify safety and liveness of the mutual exclusion protocol for the three participating processes.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies Safra's distributed termination detection algorithm on a ring of N nodes, based on EWD 998. The PlusCal algorithm models a bag-based message network carrying payload messages and a circulating token with fields q and color; nodes can send payloads, receive payloads, become inactive, pass the token, and the initiator can restart the token circulation depending on token state and local state. The translated TLA+ specification defines the global transition relation, a weak fairness condition for every process action, an instance-based refinement-style comparison to another module EWD998, and a state constraint bounding counters for model checking.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies Shmuel Safra's distributed termination detection algorithm on a ring of N nodes, as described in Dijkstra's EWD 998. It is written using PlusCal and translated to TLA+.

The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, numbered 0 through N-1, where node 0 serves as the initiator. The shared state includes a `network` variable modeled as a bag of messages per node (carrying either payload messages of type `"pl"` or a single token message of type `"tok"`), and per-node variables `active` (a Boolean indicating whether a node is computing), `color` (either `"black"` or `"white"`), and `counter` (tracking the difference between messages sent and received by each node).

Each node can nondeterministically perform one of five actions: send a payload message to another node while active (incrementing its counter); receive a payload message and become active (decrementing its counter); deactivate itself; pass the token toward the initiator (node 0) when inactive and holding the token, forwarding an updated token with an accumulated counter and color; or, if it is the initiator, re-initiate the token when the termination condition is not yet satisfied. The specification asserts weak fairness for every node's combined action.

The model-checking configuration sets N to 3 and applies a state constraint limiting counter values below 3. The module instantiates a separate `EWD998` module and checks the property `EWD998Spec`, asserting that this PlusCal implementation refines the abstract EWD998 specification. An `Alias` definition aids error-trace readability by exposing the token position and pending message counts.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a distributed termination-detection protocol for N processes arranged in a unidirectional ring, implementing Safra’s token-based algorithm. The model should capture asynchronous message passing (payload messages and a circulating special token), local process states (active/inactive), local counters that track outstanding sends, and a two-valued local “color” marker used to record whether a process has sent work since last seeing the token.
