The system must allow arbitrary sending and receiving of payload messages between any processes and must allow processes to become inactive. Exactly one special token circulates around the ring, carried in messages; a process may hold and forward the token only when it is inactive. When the token makes a full round under certain conditions it should indicate global termination.

Specify the safety property that the protocol never declares termination while some process is active or there are undelivered payload messages. Specify the eventual-detection liveness property: if the system truly reaches quiescence (no in-transit payload messages and all processes inactive), then the token circulation will eventually lead to a global termination declaration. Include invariants needed to reason about correctness: conservation/consistency between local counters and the number of outstanding payload messages, monotonicity constraints on token metadata accumulation, and that at most one token exists. The model should be parameterized by N (N ≥ 1) and allow proofs (or checks) of the stated safety and liveness properties.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies the Paxos Commit algorithm, focusing exclusively on safety properties and not liveness. The model simplifies the protocol by letting the variable msgs be the set of all messages ever sent, and does not explicitly model message receipt; instead, actions are enabled based on the presence of messages in msgs. Leader selection is not modeled, and actions that a leader may perform are defined without specifying which process acts as leader. The resource managers (RMs) can spontaneously issue Prepared messages, and Prepare messages are ignored. The specification defines the types and initial states of resource managers, acceptors, and messages, and models the protocol's actions for RMs, leaders, and acceptors. The main temporal property asserts that the protocol maintains type correctness, and the module also asserts that Paxos Commit implements the transaction commit protocol of another module (TCommit) via an INSTANCE statement.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies the Paxos Commit algorithm, a fault-tolerant distributed transaction commit protocol that runs one instance of Paxos consensus per resource manager to decide each RM's prepared/aborted vote, then derives a global commit or abort decision.

The constants are `RM` (resource managers), `Acceptor` (Paxos acceptors), `Majority` (a collection of acceptor subsets such that any two intersect), and `Ballot` (a subset of the natural numbers containing 0). The variables are `rmState` (each RM's current state: working, prepared, committed, or aborted), `aState` (each acceptor's per-instance Paxos state tracking `mbal`, `bal`, and `val`), and `msgs` (the cumulative set of all messages ever sent). The message types cover Paxos phase 1a/1b and phase 2a/2b for each RM instance, plus global Commit and Abort announcements.

RM actions allow a working RM to prepare or spontaneously abort (both send a ballot-0 phase-2a message), and allow any RM to transition to committed or aborted upon receiving the corresponding decision message. Leader actions include initiating a new ballot via `Phase1a`, sending a `Phase2a` message whose value is determined by a majority of phase-1b responses (or "aborted" if no prior vote exists), and issuing a global `Decide` message once every RM instance has chosen "prepared" (Commit) or at least one has chosen "aborted" (Abort). Acceptor actions handle responding to phase-1a and phase-2a messages and updating local state. The specification `PCSpec` is a safety-only formula (no fairness), and the module asserts that `PCSpec` maintains `PCTypeOK` and refines the abstract transaction commit specification `TCSpec` from module `TCommit`. The model checks two RMs, three acceptors, all three two-element majorities, and ballots 0 and 1.
desc_intent:
Model the Paxos-based commit protocol for coordinating a distributed transaction across a fixed set of resource managers and acceptors. The model should capture multiple independent instances of Paxos — one instance per resource manager — that are used to agree on each resource manager’s local decision (prepare or abort), and a separate decision stage that determines the global outcome (Commit if every instance chose "prepared", otherwise Abort if any instance chose "aborted"). The system must include message passing abstractions (non-lossy channels where messages once sent remain visible) and asynchronous participants; leaders may be transient or concurrent and there is no assumed reliable leader election. Model acceptors that participate in Paxos ballots and leaders that initiate phase-1 and phase-2 rounds for any ballot number, with the usual Paxos constraints that a phase-2 value must respect earlier accepted values seen in phase-1 responses from a majority. Resource managers may independently decide to prepare or abort (prepare is an explicit action; abort may be spontaneous). Once a leader observes a majority of phase-2 acknowledgements for a value for a given instance, it may broadcast the final Commit or Abort for the global transaction.

Specify safety properties:
- Agreement: no two resource managers can end in contradictory final global outcomes (no mix of committed and aborted decisions accepted as final).
- Consensus safety per instance: each Paxos instance never chooses two different values.
- Validity: any decided per-instance value must be one proposed by some resource manager (prepared or aborted).
- Consistency of global decision: Commit can be announced only if every instance has chosen "prepared"; if any instance has chosen "aborted" then only Abort may be announced.
- Type and invariant constraints: messages, acceptor state, and participant states must stay within their declared domains.

Do not require liveness (no guaranteed termination), but allow modeling arbitrary interleavings, concurrent leaders, and arbitrary majority definitions (only require any two majorities intersect).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies, via a PlusCal translation, a concurrent double-ended queue based on Detlefs-style lock-free operations using paired updates that model DCAS-like behavior on shared pointers. The shared state includes a memory mapping from addresses to node records, left and right hat pointers for the deque ends, a freelist for allocation, and per-process local variables and program counters for pushLeft, pushRight, popLeft, and popRight operations. The specification includes a test process that nondeterministically pushes and pops values while maintaining a multiset-like valBag consistency check, and it asserts a liveness property that every test process returns to control location T1 infinitely often.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies the "Snark" concurrent double-ended queue (deque) algorithm by Detlefs et al., which uses a Double Compare-and-Swap (DCAS) primitive to implement a lock-free deque over a linked list in shared memory.

The shared state consists of a memory array `Mem` indexed by `Address` (each node holding left pointer, right pointer, and value fields), a `freeList` of available addresses, two head pointers `LeftHat` and `RightHat` anchored at a sentinel `Dummy` node, per-process return values `rVal`, and a `valBag` tracking the multiset of values logically present in the deque (used for correctness checking). The DCAS macro atomically updates two memory locations if both match expected old values.

Four procedures implement the deque operations: `pushRight` and `pushLeft` allocate a new node and use DCAS to link it onto the appropriate end, retrying until successful or the free list is exhausted; `popRight` and `popLeft` use DCAS to unlink and return the node at the corresponding end, returning "empty" if the deque is empty. Each test process in `Procs` loops forever, nondeterministically choosing to push a value (selected from `Val`) onto either end or pop from either end. After a push it rolls back `valBag` if the queue was full; after a pop it asserts via TLC that the returned value was indeed in `valBag` and decrements it, enforcing that no value is popped that was never pushed.

The temporal specification is `Spec = Init /\ [][Next]_vars` with no fairness obligations. A liveness property `Liveness` asserts that every process returns infinitely often to label `T1`, though it is commented out in the config. Symmetry reduction over non-dummy addresses and process identities is declared for model checking.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a concurrent, lock-free double-ended queue (deque) that supports multiple parallel clients performing push and pop operations at both ends. The model should treat the deque as a linked structure of node objects and a pool of reusable node slots, where allocation can fail when no free slot is available and a background garbage collector may reclaim unreachable nodes. The concurrent operations must behave atomically from the client perspective: pushLeft, pushRight, popLeft, and popRight should each return either success with a value (for pops), success/acknowledgement (for pushes), or a distinguished error code ("full" for allocation failure, "empty" for popping an empty deque). Model the concurrency of many clients and allow interleaving and retries; the deque implementation may use multi-word compare-and-swap (atomic updates to two locations) as a primitive for coordinating concurrent updates.

Require the model to guarantee linearizability of all deque operations with respect to a sequential deque specification: every completed operation must appear to take effect instantaneously at some point between its invocation and response and must preserve FIFO/LIFO ordering semantics appropriate for deque ends. Ensure memory safety: nodes must never be reused while still reachable, and the garbage collector may only reclaim nodes that are provably not reachable from any observable deque state. Specify progress assumptions: clients must be able to make forward progress under fair scheduling (no operation deadlocks the system), and the garbage collector runs nondeterministically but does not violate correctness. Include invariants for structural integrity (no cycles except special sentinels, consistency of head/tail pointers) and safety properties (no value duplication or loss beyond what concurrent semantics permit).

desc_declarative_gpt: This module sets up a small model-checking configuration for a percolator-related specification by declaring three clients and three keys, along with a mapping from each client to its primary key. The comments explain that all three clients share the same primary key and are therefore considered symmetric for TLC exploration. The file contains only constant and helper definitions for the model setup; it does not define state variables, actions, temporal behavior, or correctness properties directly.
desc_intent:
Model a concurrent key-value store with optimistic per-key transaction attempts by multiple clients. The system has a fixed small set of keys and a small set of clients that may operate concurrently. Each client repeatedly attempts to perform a single-key update: it reads the current value and metadata for the key, decides on a new value, and then tries to commit the update using an optimistic compare-and-swap style protocol that may fail due to concurrent commits by other clients. If a commit fails, the client retries the transaction. Clients may also abort voluntarily or be preempted; aborted attempts leave the store unchanged. The model should include nondeterministic scheduling of client steps and of commit success/failure when there are conflicting concurrent attempts.

Specify safety properties:
- Serializability of successful commits per key: there must exist a sequential order of committed updates on each key that matches the observed key values.
- Atomicity: a committed update must appear instantaneous; partial effects must never be visible.
- No lost updates: every successful commit must overwrite the previous committed value and not be silently discarded.

Specify liveness properties to check under fair scheduling:
- Progress: if a client keeps retrying a transaction on a key and no other client continuously and infinitely preempts it, it eventually succeeds.
- Absence of livelock: the system should not allow indefinite mutual interference that prevents all clients from making progress.

Allow specification of symmetry among clients and multiple runs with different initial values for keys.

desc_declarative_gpt: This TLA+ specification models Safra's distributed termination detection algorithm on a ring topology, as described in EWD 998. The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, each of which can be active or passive, and a token that circulates to detect global termination. The algorithm tracks the number of messages sent and received, node colors (white/black), and uses a token with position, color, and a counter to aggregate information as it traverses the ring. The specification defines the system's state transitions, including message sending, receiving, token passing, and node deactivation, and verifies both safety (termination detection correctness) and liveness (termination is eventually detected) properties. The model includes state and action constraints to bound the state space for model checking, and an inductive invariant capturing Safra's correctness argument.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies Shmuel Safra's distributed termination detection algorithm on a ring of N nodes, as described in Dijkstra's EWD 998. The system models N nodes arranged in a ring, where nodes can be active or inactive, exchange messages, and pass a token around the ring to detect when all computation has ceased.

The state consists of each node's activation status, color (white or black), a message counter tracking sent-minus-received messages, a pending message count per node, and a token carrying a position, cumulative counter, and color. Initially, counters and pending counts are zero, and the token starts at node 0 as black. The environment actions allow active nodes to send messages to any other node, any node to receive a pending message (which reactivates it and blackens it), and active nodes to deactivate. The system actions are `InitiateProbe`, where node 0 restarts a token pass when the previous round was inconclusive, and `PassToken`, where an inactive node forwards the token toward node 0, accumulating counters and propagating black coloring.

The temporal specification is `Init /\ [][Next]_vars` with weak fairness on system actions. The config sets N=3, applies state constraints bounding counters and pending counts to 3, and checks the invariants `TypeOK` and `Inv`. `Inv` encodes Safra's inductive invariant relating total in-flight message counts to node counters and token state across four disjunctive clauses. The safety property `TerminationDetection` asserts that whenever termination is declared (white token at node 0 with consistent zero-sum accounting), the system has truly terminated. The liveness property `Liveness` asserts that actual termination is eventually detected. An alias provides TLC instrumentation tracking token passes, node activations, and token field statistics.
desc_intent:
Specify a TLA+ model of Safra’s distributed termination-detection algorithm for N processes arranged in a unidirectional logical ring. The model should represent processes that can be active or passive, send and receive application messages asynchronously, and change an internal color (white or black) used by the algorithm. Processes maintain local counters that track the difference between the number of messages they have sent and the number they have received. Messages in transit must be explicitly modeled so that the system can have a nonzero number of in-flight messages.

Include a circulating token that can be initiated by a designated initiator and passed around the ring. The token carries a summary count of outstanding messages collected from a suffix of the ring and a color bit. The protocol must allow processes to start a probe round, pass the token only when passive, and update the token’s count and color in a way that reflects local counters and colors. Processes may become active when they receive application messages and may deactivate at arbitrary times when passive.

Formally state the correctness properties:
- Safety (detection soundness): if the token returns to the initiator white, with its count and the initiator’s local counter summing to zero and the initiator passive and white, then the global system has truly terminated (no active processes and no in-flight messages).
- An inductive invariant capturing Safra’s reasoning that relates the global number of in-flight messages, local counters, token position, token count, and colors, sufficient to prove the safety property.
- Liveness: if the system has terminated (no active processes and no in-flight messages), then eventually the initiator will observe the white token condition (termination will be detected).

Allow nondeterministic scheduling of sends, receives, and deactivations; bound state-space sizes for model checking; and make explicit any assumptions (finite N ≥ 1, unbounded but constrained counters/messages for analysis) needed to verify the invariant and liveness.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module defines a small configuration for a distributed transaction system, likely for testing or demonstration purposes. It declares two keys and three clients, and then defines sets and mappings that specify which clients are optimistic or pessimistic, which keys each client can read or write, and the primary key for each client. The module does not define any actions, temporal properties, or proofs, and serves as a parameterization or configuration layer for the system specified in the DistributedTransaction module.
desc_intent: Specify a distributed transaction processing system for a small replicated key-value store with two keys and three clients. Model clients that perform read and write transactions on subsets of keys; some clients use optimistic concurrency and some use pessimistic locking. The system must support transactions that read a consistent snapshot and write updates atomically: a committed transaction must make all its writes visible together; an aborted transaction must leave state unchanged. Reads by a transaction should reflect either the latest committed values at its start or, for optimistic clients, may detect conflicts and abort. Pessimistic clients must acquire exclusive locks on the keys they will write before reading and hold them until commit or abort, preventing concurrent conflicting commits. The model should include a notion of primary replica assignment per client for coordinating writes, and message-passing between replicas and clients for lock requests, read requests, write proposals, votes, and commit/abort decisions. Key safety properties: (1) atomicity of transactions, (2) serializability (every history is equivalent to some serial execution of committed transactions), (3) absence of lost updates (writes from committed transactions are not overwritten by later commits in a way that loses those effects), and (4) proper use of locks so that pessimistic clients prevent conflicting concurrent commits. Include progress assumptions: nonfaulty clients and primaries eventually make progress (no permanent deadlock), and messages are eventually delivered.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a small wrapper around an underlying Boulanger specification. It introduces a constant bound MaxNat, assumes that MaxNat is a natural number, defines a bounded natural range NatOverride as 0 .. MaxNat, and adds a state constraint requiring each process in Procs to have num[process] < MaxNat. The file itself does not define the underlying algorithm, actions, or temporal properties; it only contributes a bounding assumption and constraint on top of the imported module.
desc_intent:
Specify a parameterized distributed counter service used by a set of processes that must always keep local counts below a fixed upper bound. Model a collection of processes that increment and decrement their own nonnegative integer counters and may read other processes' counters. The service must enforce that no counter ever becomes negative and that no counter ever reaches or exceeds a given maximum value (a strict upper bound provided as a parameter). The model must allow arbitrary interleavings of independent increments, decrements, and reads, and must permit fairness for progress: if a process repeatedly attempts a legal increment or decrement, it should eventually succeed unless doing so would violate the bounds.

Capture the initial condition where every process starts with a nonnegative counter strictly below the maximum. Specify actions for attempting an increment, attempting a decrement, and performing a read of another process's counter. Ensure that attempted increments are disabled when they would reach or exceed the maximum, and that decrements are disabled when they would go negative. Express the key correctness properties: safety properties (no counter ever negative, no counter ever >= maximum, all counters remain integers) and liveness properties (enabled increments or decrements are eventually executed under fairness). Also require invariants that relate local operations to the global bound and that the bound is a fixed natural-number parameter.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking wrapper around a checkpoint coordination specification. It constrains the explored state space with bounded natural-number and log-index ranges, adds a state constraint requiring there to be at least one open index, and defines a node symmetry set using permutations of Node. It also defines an intentionally incorrect optimization predicate for lease replacement that either delegates to the instantiated CheckpointCoordination module's predicate or allows replacement whenever the lease is held by the current leader, as indicated by the comment describing it as a bad optimization.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal TLA+ model of a replicated-state-machine checkpoint coordination service for a distributed system with leader-based lease ownership. The model should describe a set of nodes that coordinate taking and finalizing checkpoints of a shared log, where checkpoints are associated with increasing log indices. Only one leader at a time may hold a renewal lease that authorizes making progress; leases have a holder identity and validity period. The system must allow the leader to propose a checkpoint at a chosen log index, obtain agreement that that index can be truncated or compacted, and safely transfer responsibility when leadership changes.

The model must guarantee safety: checkpoints must never cause loss of committed updates; no leader may finalize a checkpoint that would discard entries still needed by any active or potentially active replica. It must guarantee that two different leaders cannot both consider the same lease concurrently effective unless membership and timing semantics permit overlap, and that checkpoint decisions respect lease ownership (a node without a valid lease must not finalize a checkpoint). Liveness properties should ensure that if a stable leader holds a valid lease and communication is sufficiently reliable, the system eventually completes checkpointing for proposed indices and advances the safe truncation point. Specify invariants capturing monotonicity of checkpoint indices, exclusivity of effective lease ownership, and preservation of committed log entries across checkpointing and leader changes.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module specifies Huang's distributed termination detection algorithm on a fully meshed network of processes with a distinguished leader. Each process has an active flag, a dyadic rational weight, and a queue of in-transit messages; the total weight across processes and messages is conserved at 1, and idle processes return their weight toward the leader. The specification defines initialization, message sending, receiving, and idling actions, adds weak fairness for receive and idle actions, and verifies both a safety property that detected termination implies permanent global termination and a liveness property that global termination eventually leads to the leader detecting termination.
desc_declarative_claude:
The module specifies Huang's algorithm for distributed termination detection. The system consists of a fixed set of processes (`Procs`) with one distinguished `Leader`. The algorithm uses dyadic rational weights to track whether all computation has ceased: the leader begins holding the entire weight (`One`), and whenever it activates another process by sending a message, it splits its current weight in half and includes the half in the message. A non-leader process that finishes its work returns its weight to the leader via a message; the leader accumulates returned weights and declares termination when it holds `One` again while itself being idle.

The state comprises `active` (a per-process boolean), `weight` (a dyadic rational held by each process), and `msgs` (a per-process sequence of in-transit dyadic rational weights). The `TypeOK` invariant enforces that the total weight across all processes and in-flight messages always sums to `One`. Key actions are `SendMsg` (an active process halves its weight and sends the half to any process), `RcvMsg` and `Idle` for non-leaders (receiving a message activates the process and adds its weight; going idle sends weight back to the leader), and `RcvLdr` and `IdleLdr` for the leader (accumulating returned weights or becoming inactive). The temporal specification `Spec` adds weak fairness on all receive and idle actions. Two properties are checked: `Safe` asserts that once termination is detected (`TerminationDetected`) all processes are and remain truly idle (`Terminated`), and `Live` asserts that actual termination eventually leads to its detection.
desc_intent:
Specify a distributed termination-detection protocol based on weight distribution (Huang’s algorithm). Model a fixed set of processes with one distinguished leader. The system must track each process’s local activity state (active or idle), local fractional weight, and messages in transit carrying fractional weights. Initially only the leader is active and holds the entire weight (total weight 1); no messages exist. Processes may send part of their current weight to any other process (model a fully connected network), receive weight-bearing messages which make them active and increase their local weight, or become idle by sending their entire local weight back toward the leader and setting themselves inactive. The leader can also become idle and must absorb incoming weight-bearing messages to increase its weight.

Requirements:
- Conservation of total weight: the sum of all local weights plus weights carried by messages in transit must always equal 1.
- No assumptions about message ordering: messages may be delivered in any order; the network may buffer multiple messages per destination.
- Liveness: if all processes eventually become idle and all in-transit weights return to the leader, the leader should detect termination by becoming inactive and holding total weight 1.
- Safety: once the leader detects termination, the system must remain in a globally terminated state (all processes idle and no messages).
- Fairness: model fair delivery of messages and fairness of leader’s receive actions sufficient to ensure progress toward detection.
- Prevent pathological behaviors like infinite weight halving by bounding representation precision or denominators.

Express these properties as invariants and temporal properties (safety and liveness) to verify that the protocol correctly detects global termination without false positives and that detection eventually occurs when the system has terminated.

desc_declarative_gpt: This module is a model-checking wrapper for the InnerSerial specification. It introduces a bounded natural-number set MCNat and a state constraint that limits the length of each process operation queue to MaxQLen, in order to keep the TLC state space finite. It also defines an arbitrary initial memory function MCInitMem for the constant parameter InitMem, and states a liveness property AlwaysResponds asserting that non-free register operations eventually become free again and that operation identifiers in opId eventually correspond to completed operations.
desc_intent:
Specify a formal model of a multi-processor memory-access coordinator that serializes concurrent read and write operations on shared addresses. The model should describe a finite set of processors that issue operations (reads or writes) identified by per-processor operation identifiers and enqueued for service. The coordinator delivers to each operation a response that reflects a total order of operations per address consistent with program order per processor: for any single memory address, the visible effects of operations must be as if all operations on that address were executed in some sequential order. Concurrent operations on different addresses may be ordered independently.

The model must capture:
- a bounded queueing mechanism per processor for outstanding operations (queue lengths are bounded by a fixed constant),
- the creation of operations (reads producing returned values, writes producing acknowledgements),
- the service/commit of operations by the coordinator that updates a shared memory state and produces responses,
- per-processor registers that track operation status until a response is observed.

Correctness properties to guarantee:
- Safety: linearizability/serializability per address — every completed response must correspond to executing the operation at a single point in a total order for that address that respects real-time order and program order;
- Atomicity of individual operations: each operation appears to take effect instantaneously at its linearization point;
- Progress: every issued operation eventually receives a response (no operation is permanently lost or starved), assuming the queue bounds are respected;
- Queue bounds invariant: no per-processor queue length exceeds the configured bound.

Do not specify internal implementation details of the coordinator or concrete scheduling; instead, specify abstract transitions for enqueueing, starting, committing, and responding, and express the invariants and liveness requirements above.
